notes.title: Raiders of Lyonesse | Patch Notes
notes.content:
[h2][/h2][previewyoutube="nsHJD6OHaNs;full"][/previewyoutube][h2]
Patch Notes[/h2][p][/p][h3][b]PvP Province - Lyonesse[/b][/h3][list][*][p]The PvP Province has been redone and is now much larger.[/p][/*][*][p]Added unique landmark locations, such as ruined old cities, to hint at the history of the province.[/p][/*][*][p]Added new sites in the form of watchtowers, providing a convenient place for players to repair their gear and craft items.[/p][/*][*][p]Fast Travel is now enabled within Lyonesse between the ruined cities and province gateways. [/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3][b]Crafting & resources[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Added two new resources exclusive to the PvP province: Ambergrasp and Canonite.[/p][/*][*][p]Enchantment of gear: the new resources found in Lyonesse can be refined in the Alchemy and Jewelcrafting skill trees and combined into Sanctified Oil, which comes in four tiers, ranging from +50 to +125 points of Item Power boost. The oil can be applied to any item with Item Power to boost its stats permanently.[/p][/*][*][p]Added the ability to craft Founders' rewards in the Log Workbench, located near every Petra Dei. It complements the still available method of using the Founders Crafting Table to craft those recipes.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where the same tier of potions with different durations would wildly and unexpectedly vary in value provided. Now it is standardized with slight variation based on tier.[/p][/*][*][p]You can now craft a total of 36 new RP wearables, with no stats. The selection includes capes, hats, dresses, tunics, pants, shoes, and new diadems.[/p][/*][*][p]Deer bucks now drop antlers as a guaranteed drop. [/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3][b]Building[/b][/h3][list][*][p]The building integrity values of the low foundation pieces were fixed to give more support.[/p][/*][*][p]The building integrity of some smaller foundation pieces was fixed.[/p][/*][*][p]Two Granite foundation pieces now cost 5 instead of 10 granite to better align with the piece size.[/p][/*][*][p]All Plots owned by characters in a specific Server Region are now shown to the Player.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed snapping point on Balustrade, Limestone pieces.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed snap-point selection for several small objects.[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced the amount of Granite needed to build low walls.[/p][/*][*][p]You can now set permissions to sell items at your market stall to Public.  [/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3][b]Revamped Lobby and Character Creator[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Created a new lobby for the game to make it fit better into the style of the game.[/p][/*][*][p]The new lobby includes a short set of introduction screens to Pax Dei. The screens are intended for new players coming to the game, to give them a bit more context on what Pax Dei is about.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a range of new options to customize your avatar’s face.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a couple of tweaks to better match selected color values.[/p][/*][*][p]Adjusted character preset to match their rendered icons.[/p][/*][*][p]Profanity filters are now implemented for the character's name.[/p][/*][*][p]Renamed the body slider to more accurately reflect a range of body types.[/p][/*][*][p]"Always cover body" is now persistent in the Character Selection screen.  [/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3][b]Characters[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Braids no longer behave erratically when approaching other Players.[/p][/*][*][p]Created an alpha mask and set the glove material to double-sided to prevent some unsightly shadows.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where Petra Dei's inventory stopped looking correctly on the highest UI scale.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where ears were clipping through some Head Equipment.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3][b]UI[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Revamped the Tier and Quality symbols. Quality is now shown in a gradient of color in the top half of the icon and also in the segmented outer ring of the new symbol. The segmented inner ring of the symbol indicates the tier. Filled segments show the tier count.[/p][list][*][p]Poor is dark grey[/p][/*][*][p]Common is light grey[/p][/*][*][p]Uncommon is green[/p][/*][*][p]Rare is blue[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]We have added a notification for when you unlock a recipe by levelling up a skill.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where the "Find your friends on Discord" text did not fit the frame.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue with moving items where "Split one" would move the whole stack, instead of adding one item to an incomplete stack.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where the cast bar was not displayed to the Player most of the time.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where chat did not open after pressing "Enter" in some instances.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue with the Commanding Strike ability's description.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where the Discord hyperlink did not work in the "Select your Region" menu.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where, for some localisations, text would exceed window boundaries in the Premium tooltip by applying wrap.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where the Honed Steel Chopping axe would have the same description as a pickaxe.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where the Market Stall Location menu could not be closed using the \[ESC] key.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where the Split Stack slider was too small, reducing UI precision.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where the UI scale slider button did not align correctly with its 4 values and could be dragged across the entire slider surface.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed missing apostrophes from Province Gate names.[/p][/*][*][p]Decreased the font size of the stack on the item icons.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a notification about XP gain whilst Mining, Skinning, and Woodcutting.[/p][/*][*][p]Removed black bars on the sides of the screen on ultrawide monitors[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3][b]World[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Fixed an issue where a gap in geometry appeared on some caves' ceilings.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where grass was floating above the ground in Ancien – Lavedan.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where invisible collision was present.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where some decorative sacrificial assets were misaligned with the ground in The Oubliettes dungeon.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue with particular foliage LOD inside Lyonesse Wildlands.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an instance of floating decorative rocks in a cavern part of The Carcinoma dungeon.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed minor collision issues with bridges.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the issue where setting the streaming distance to zero percent would cause multiple graphics issues.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed two instances of floor z-fighting in The Molting Chambers dungeon.[/p][/*][*][p]Quicksilver drop rates have been increased.[/p][/*][*][p]Rain Lily Extract and Datura Seed Pod Extract will no longer be lootable since they weren't used in any recipes.[/p][/*][*][p]Removed T2 rare spawns from T1 Heartland camps.[/p][/*][*][p]The vase in the Reflection of Holastri dungeon is no longer clipping with the wall. [/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3][b]World visuals[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Improved night sky with more realistic star distribution and relative magnitudes.[/p][/*][*][p]Improved cloud rendering with less grainy appearance.[/p][/*][*][p]Minor image exposure and contrast adjustments.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3][b]Localization[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Added localized names for all Gates between provinces.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where the "Crafter Unlocks" text did not fit in its designated space in Polish localization.[/p][/*][*][p]Adjusted the "Discord Account Linking" text in Chat Settings for the Spanish Language to fit with the UI.[/p][/*][*][p]Localized "Home location updated" notification. [/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3][b]Camera[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Fixed an issue where the camera could clip into a tree.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where previously selected Character preset's highlight did not disappear, unless hovered on.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where the same tier of potions with different durations would wildly and unexpectedly vary in value provided. Now it is standardized with slight variation based on tier. [/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3][b]Audio & VFX[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Added new intro music - it's different depending on the local machine time of day.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where water volume would not have SFX.[/p][/*][*][p]Hid some visible streaks that were causing texture issues with some spell VFX (Bloodfed Grove for example).[/p][/*][*][p]Targeting effects now apply similar visuals to the committed effect. [/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3][b]Crashes[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Fixed an issue where "Sign in with Discord" crashed the game after clicking on accept in the Discord pop-up.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where rapidly opening and closing the miracle menu would cause the game to crash.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h2]Known Issues[/h2][h3]Combat[/h3][list][*][p]Combat state does not end when players who are in combat (against each other) leave a PvP zone and remain in proximity. , preventing equipment changes and affecting regeneration.[/p][/*][*][p]Blocking is not functioning when equipping a wieldable from the inventory. No issue when equipping it from the quick slots bar. This impacts all items that allow blocking: Greataxes, Greatmauls, Two-Handed Spears, and the Shields.[/p][/*][*][p]Shooting with a Bow is possible while using Emotes (no, it is not a feature).[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3]Building[/h3][list][*][p](Not New) Bottom snapping point functionality is missing for multiple foundation building pieces, making construction alignment more difficult.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3]World (Lyonesse)[/h3][list][*][p]Some resources and NPCs are on unreachable mountain peaks in Lyonesse.[/p][/*][*][p]A plank near some ‘empire ruins’ in Lyonesse is clipping through the wooden platform.[/p][/*][*][p]A road leading to one of the Inquisition locations is unnaturally shaped, creating impassable terrain.[/p][/*][*][p]A demonic tree is present on the road in Lyonesse, in the Karrek area.[/p][/*][*][p]The ‘PvP watchtower’ and ‘Fey Slumbering’ icons are missing from the Map Legend in Lyonesse.[/p][/*][*][p]Stretched road textures appear in several locations in Lyonesse, Corbin Zone.[/p][/*][*][p]The biome indicator graphic overlaps water in Lyonesse, Brecilien Zone, misrepresenting terrain on the map.[/p][/*][*][p]Some decorative pillars in Lyonesse, Avalon, appear misaligned with the terrain and are floating above ground in some locations.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3]UI & HUD[/h3][list][*][p]Level requirements for wearables and wieldables are no longer displayed in items’ tooltips.[/p][/*][*][p]Opening the Construction Hammer map briefly stacks all Zone names at the center of the minimap while it initializes.[/p][/*][*][p]On higher UI scale settings, the Equipment UI overlaps the HUD, obscuring health, stamina, and abilities. Character statistics can also be cut off.[/p][/*][*][p]The biome HUD tooltip background does not properly resize to fit text, with specific biome names overlapping or being too close to the frame.[/p][/*][*][p]Opening or closing multiple UIs in a row may trigger an [i]Undefined Error[/i] due to failed API requests.[/p][/*][*][p]The “ESC X” button in Polish localization overlaps outside of the UI frame.[/p][/*][*][p]The internal ID of the enchantment category has not been localized and is displayed in Market Stall, Redeeming Queue, and Journal recipe overview for the items of this category.[/p][/*][*][p]Certain minerals (Lapis Lazuli, Quicksilver) and gemstones (Diamond, Ruby) lack Tier indicators, causing inconsistency and confusion.[/p][/*][*][p]Reopening inventory after enchanting shows an empty Enchanting window until the player reselects the item.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3]Character Creation & Customization[/h3][list][*][p]Character creation may fail and the game can crash if you create a character up to the zone selection step, then cancel each step to return to the character selection lobby, and afterward create and enter the game with a new character. A restart is required to avoid the issue.[/p][/*][*][p]The game occasionally freezes when exiting from the character selection lobby.[/p][/*][*][p]“Reset Sliders” in Character Creator resets values to the minimum instead of the middle, creating inconsistencies between indicators and appearance.[/p][/*][*][p]Rapidly switching character presets in Character Creator can distort the camera, causing it to center inside the character model.[/p][/*][*][p]Character heads appear blurry/pixelated on low graphics settings when viewed from the side or back in Character Creator.[/p][/*][*][p]“UpperCheeks Up/Down” text in Character Creator is missing a space.[/p][/*][*][p]Certain Face Details text entries do not fit in their UI space in Polish and Spanish localizations.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3]Wearables & Cosmetics[/h3][list][*][p]RP shoes and boots clip through most bottom wearables, with high boots showing the worst clipping.[/p][/*][*][p]Some RP clothes recipes are incorrectly unlocked by default.[/p][/*][*][p]RP dresses show a seam near the collarbone when graphics are set to Low quality.[/p][/*][*][p]Some RP wearables have inaccurate Polish translations (e.g., Traveler’s Mantle, Ivorylace Hose, RP Pants).[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Verse 4: Raiders of Lyonesse is coming on September 10
notes.content:
[h3]Hello Paxians,[/h3][p]We’re thrilled to announce that the long-awaited Verse 4 is arriving on live servers this week!

Titled [i]“Raiders of Lyonesse”[/i], this new Verse will be released as soon as tomorrow, [b]September 10[/b]! Let’s get ready for some PvP content! [/p][p]The scheduled [b]maintenance will begin at 10:00 am UTC[/b], with an expected downtime of approximately 90 minutes across all live shards.[/p][p]Now, without further delay, let’s dive into the content of Raiders of Lyonesse.[/p][p][/p][h2]New PvP map[/h2][p]We’re making some big changes to the PvP zone, Lyonesse. First of all, the whole zone is much bigger to support the new gameplay. There are several unique landmark locations in the form of ruined old cities, hinting at the province's rich history. We’re also adding some new sites in the form of watchtowers, serving as convenient places for you to repair your gear and craft some items. Since the new Lyonesse is so big and we wanted to make Fast travel more consistent, we’re now enabling fast travel within Lyonesse between the ruined cities and province gateways. The Fast Travel points exist as Petrae Dei in the four corner areas of Lyonesse, and you’ll have to collect the Fast Travel points in each of these locations the same way as the Petrae Dei in other provinces.[/p][p]Beware, a bigger zone means more riches to find, but also more foes to defeat! Get your swords ready![/p][p]For more details, check out our dedicated article about [url="https://playpaxdei.com/news/game-updates/changes-to-the-pvp-system-in-pax-dei-everything-you-need-to-know"]the future of PvP[/url].[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/975a05f9b186fc2a35c7dac195feee6d5c8c612b.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/5cac568f33dd272295ae90f23796a614a1d4f7e3.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]New resources in Lyonesse[/h2][p]To give each of you a good reason to travel to Lyonesse, we’re adding two new unique resources you can only find in the PvP-enabled areas. Ambergrasp and Canonite are very scarce in the area and sought-after by Zebians patrolling in Lyonesse, so be prepared to be on the lookout for the Residual Harvesters collecting the resources on your behalf. The biggest spoils will be found on their bosses, in PvE sites across the area.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/677d8673873a7b0b3d94aa96cc2ac59f4330ffa6.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/717aedcd1994c3f78047d801794eba5ebc3e62d9.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]Enchantment[/h2][p]The new resources found in Lyonesse can be refined in the Alchemy and Jewelcrafting skill trees and combined into Sanctified Oil, which comes in four tiers, ranging from +50 to +125 points of Item Power boost. The oil can be applied to any item with Item Power to permanently boost all the item's stats.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/1fa00d0f254be353cd891b77df5105c3d1f5d5d9.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]RP outfit[/h2][p]Not sure what to wear while wandering through your clan’s city, stopping by a nearby tavern, or just relaxing at home? We’ve got you covered with a colorful set of 36 wearables perfect for every laid-back occasion. And since pictures speak louder than words, here they are![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/0d45cd9e7b4fd89c3115253d9c12e6ae214bc131.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/0edab6c7bc0d83b458ed0b5f461e1282ba6c62cd.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/a96d94afca4855ad06c0186603cbabc5ba3fb6ff.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/9089279cc2ae8dc0e6350d976263f6ca43eea340.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/735a66530fe693b4ff42a2f77c013da4c745477d.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/4f03c8314151494dbf2e2b293a716f657670c610.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/c4693f6ee282b84b717ec5f4a2016d3a5c9b3dc7.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/52e7cc16ea209337c5f2bf84a9a67252c055be84.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/68cbd8a9796a04dde6cf047a162aece7b162f222.png"][/img][/p][h2]UI updates[/h2][p]We’re making changes to the Items icons, introducing a more visually intuitive system, and making it easier to instantly recognize both the quality level and tier of an item at a glance. More details in our article \[LINK][/p][p]Quality will now be shown in a gradient of color in the top half of the icon and also in the segmented outer ring of the new symbol.[/p][list][*][p]Poor is dark grey[/p][/*][*][p]Common is light grey[/p][/*][*][p]Uncommon is green[/p][/*][*][p]Rare is blue[/p][/*][/list][p]The tier is indicated by the segmented inner ring of the symbol. Filled segments show the tier count.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/4120041f1328edfcf2e329eef2995781c73a5e07.png"][/img][/p][p]Additional UI visual changes are also being made to the style of the bonus display. 

Last, but not least, the HUD now includes the biome and zone you’re currently in. The visual presentation for the feature is not the final design and will likely be more discreet in a future update.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/574d742133b85234a1047c8337a3e8a06a452ae5.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]Cosmos updates[/h2][p]We continue to improve the Cosmos, enhancing both the night sky and cloud rendering. We’re also making some minor adjustments to image exposure and contrast.[/p][p][/p][p]See you in-game for more details![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/31dad685ededac235800cb3c52c0ee6273121a9b.png"][/img][/p][h2]Revamped Lobby and New Character Creator UI[/h2][p]We’re creating a new lobby for the game to better fit its style. More importantly, we’re unlocking a whole range of new options to customize your avatar’s face. You can now alter the shapes of your character’s facial features using sliders as well as control their age and skin complexion (redness, baggy or dark eye orbits…).[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/9caebbd4fcd41794713414a5dad218baec11d44e.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/ce97bba1084552c29d06a0fa97468b78403d74ac.png"][/img][/p][h2]Tutorial pages[/h2][p][/p][p]The new lobby will feature a brief set of introduction screens for Pax Dei. The screens are intended for new players coming to the game, to give them more context on what Pax Dei is about.[/p][p]We’re sure you’re as thrilled as we are with this “back to school” content update, and we can’t wait to read your feedback on the dedicated channels![/p][p]
Pax vobiscum, 
The Mainframe Team[/p]

notes.title: PvP System Changes: Everything You Need to Know
notes.content:
[h2]Hello Paxians,[/h2][p][/p][p]We’re excited to introduce the big changes that will be coming to PvP in Pax Dei, starting with Verse 4! Whether you’re a seasoned fighter or just dipping your toes into the world of player combat, here’s everything you need to know about the [b]reworked PvP system[/b]: what’s changing, what’s staying, and how you can prepare. All the details and concepts below are still a work in progress, and we’re eager to get your feedback and suggestions to improve them and ensure they suit your gameplay style.[/p][p]Before we go into details, let’s first talk about where we are and what we aim to achieve.[/p][p]We know some players hate PvP, some love it and others are in between - if the reward is worth the risk, they’ll do it, but the reward really has to be there and the risk has to be understood. As such, we still think PvP in Pax Dei should be a choice and players should have the ability to opt in, whether that’s through joining a PvP alliance or travelling to a PvP-enabled area in the game.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/c7fba4e2837c2b1e76d6dfefb28abd33a288a4d9.jpg"][/img][/p][p]This brings us to Pax Dei: the peace of the divine mechanic that controls where PvP is available. At the time of writing this blog, the Home Valleys and the Wildlands are protected under Pax Dei and players are safe from PvP mechanics, while Lyonesse is a PvP-enabled forsaken area with no protection. You, as a player, have no control over this… yet. Our goal is to gradually change this over time, introducing elements that make the game more challenging in certain areas while giving you control of Pax Dei through specific mechanics.[/p][p]The role of PvP in Pax Dei is multi-fold. We want to see the PvP systems result in large alliances being formed, castles being built, and drama unfolding in the field of war and politics, with spies, backstabbing and bribery. Getting to the top leadership positions should be hard work - but also attainable with cunning. A ruler leading the largest army in the game should never have to step on the field of battle if they and their subjects so choose. It’ll take time, but each update will take us closer to this vision.[/p][p]We also want to create systems that allow competition - and create tension - along multiple axes of the game, not just PvP. Some players should be able to exert physical power, while a rich merchant should be able to use their gold for power.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/8bbc12d890f437dd306479e9e3ffc2677a588fa9.jpg"][/img][/p][p]All of this will result in a game where we hope to see a healthy player-driven economy, where the competition will lead into destruction and demand of goods, enabling those who love the crafting parts of the game to meaningfully participate and feel their work is appreciated. So while this document will detail elements some of you will not want to participate in, our goal is to make a better game for you all.[/p][p]Let’s jump into a bit more detail on what we’re thinking.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/5cac568f33dd272295ae90f23796a614a1d4f7e3.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]Phase 1 - Verse 4[/h2][p]Lyonesse is becoming much larger. The updated Lyonesse is a full-blown 10x10 km area with 5 zones. Four of the zones are in the corners and contain entry portals, with a central zone in the middle, accessible from all four corners. Each area has PvE sites, with the center being significantly more dangerous than the other areas.[/p][p]The four corner areas all have a Petra Dei inside them, with a Pax Dei protected area surrounding the Petra Dei. The Petra Dei has all the services you expect, with crafters and storage.[/p][p]The thinking behind making Lyonesse larger is, as you’ll read below, that there’s a ton of gameplay we’ll be introducing to Lyonesse in subsequent updates, and this requires space. We’ve looked at the extraction gameplay in Lyonesse and with the gameplay that’s landing, the larger area was also warranted to allow players to dip in and out with significant PvP risk - but no guarantee of getting caught each time.[/p][p]Lyonesse now comes with two new resources only found in the area. Ambergrasp and Canonite are refined using Alchemy and Jewelcrafting and will allow creation of Sanctified Oil, which can be used to Enchant any gear with Item Power, with up to a 125-point boost to the Item Power of the Enchanted item. The enchantment is permanent when applied to the item. The resources can be found on the ground, but are predominantly found as loot on NPCs in the area, and the most lucrative drops will be on NPCs in the central area of Lyonesse.[/p][p]The goal of this update is to prepare for the future, but also give you a good reason to venture into Lyonesse in search of riches.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/677d8673873a7b0b3d94aa96cc2ac59f4330ffa6.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/717aedcd1994c3f78047d801794eba5ebc3e62d9.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/1fa00d0f254be353cd891b77df5105c3d1f5d5d9.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]Phase 2[/h2][p]While Heartlands in Pax Dei will be sacrosanct and will not be wiped after the game launch, Lyonesse will feature seasons. The rules and gameplay will change in Lyonesse between the seasons, and the first one will likely last 6 months.[/p][p]The PvP update after Verse 4 will introduce a new mechanism where clans will be able to claim a piece of land in Lyonesse and place plots in the area they’ve claimed. The plots will allow building exactly as if you were in Heartlands, with the distinction that the plot placement is only available to the members of the clan.[/p][p]The number of spots that can be claimed will be limited. To capture a spot, the clans will have to have access to a new resource to pay for the claim - and upkeep - for the ownership. The resource will be constrained in availability, and clans who want to own land in Lyonesse will be either trading or fighting to get access to it.[/p][p]Having land in Lyonesse will have huge benefits, bringing safety, storage and crafting to the clan. The claimed spot is likely to act as a respawn shrine for the clan in control of the site, so being in control of a spot next to a good PvE site will be extremely beneficial.[/p][p]We are looking at improving some plot-level permissions as part of this work to facilitate creation of safe fortresses.[/p][p]We’re also looking at changing the rules related to death and property. Right now, Pax Dei forces the same rules everywhere across the game world, and the need for corpse runs feels very harsh in the Heartlands. We don’t have final details yet, but it’s likely that going forward you no longer have to make a corpse run after respawning in a Shrine in Home Valleys, but also we’ll likely add a small chance for some stackable items being destroyed and will tune the death damage to any gear with health.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/d2878f124a8bf30ed65e0adb61159154238b7166.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]After phase 2[/h2][p]The following features are in the design phase, so the timing, order and exact design might still change, but we wanted to give you a glimpse of where the game is going.[/p][p][b]Feudal Houses [/b]will allow a Clan to flag itself as a Feudal House, with the Clan leader becoming a Knight. Knights can swear fealty to each other, thus forming a larger alliance, which will affect the PvP flagging of all players in the alliance. We will likely require that the land in Lyonesse can only be controlled by Houses. [/p][p]Houses are likely to get the means to claim areas outside of Lyonesse as their sphere of influence and gain benefits such as taxation rights in these areas. However, doing this will open the alliance up to war declarations, with the alliance being flagged for PvP also outside of Lyonesse when at war.[/p][p][b]Market Towns[/b] will change the areas around the Petra Deis in Lyonesse. The areas will stay as safe harbors inside Lyonesse and feature plots that allow building. Where the plots elsewhere in Lyonesse require combat for ownership, the plots in the Market Towns will use economic competition and you will be bidding gold against other players for control of these plots. We’re looking at making these areas central trading hubs and are likely to make changes related to speed travel and resource transportation as the towns come online, but don’t have exact details to share on that yet.[/p][p][b]Parishes[/b] will allow players to form an alliance to enable a Priest to collect large amounts of Grace. We’re looking at enabling the Priest to not only cast new very expensive Miracles, but also to control Pax Dei with Altars, securing claimed sites in Lyonesse from PvP. We’re also looking at new Positions of Power, where priests can anoint members of the Feudal Houses into new positions.[/p][p][/p][h2]Get Ready for the New PvP Era[/h2][p]As you can imagine, these updates require quite a lot of work, changes, additions and adjustments, and not everything will be released all at once.[/p][p]The new era for Pax Dei PvP will start with the new Lyonesse and Enchanting. Following this, we’ll add building in Lyonesse, with more to follow.[/p][p]Please provide your feedback on Discord, in the [url="https://discord.com/channels/1071081786962088018/1410957277229219900/1410957277229219900"]dedicated thread[/url].[/p][p]Whether you’re looking to dominate the battlefield, build an economic empire in a Market Town, or just survive in the wilds, there’ll be something for every PvP player with these changes.[/p][p]The real fight for Lyonesse will soon begin! 🔥[/p][p]Bellum vobiscum, 
The Mainframe Team [/p]

notes.title: UI & Item icons - Upcoming update
notes.content:
[p]Hello Paxians,[/p][p]We wanted to share with you some work in progress our team is doing regarding icons and UI in general. [/p][p][/p][h2]Items Icons[/h2][p]We’re excited to share that our team is working on an update for the item icons! We know that the recently added icons haven’t been as clear as we’d like, which can sometimes cause confusion. That’s why we’re introducing a more visually intuitive system, making it easier to instantly recognize both the quality level and tier of an item at a glance.[/p][p]The concept below is still a work in progress, but the final result should look quite similar. Bonus: you’ll also catch a sneak peek at the Mastercrafting system mentioned in Tuesday’s news and [url="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WEvYuISwCxI"]interview[/url].[/p][p][/p][h2][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/4120041f1328edfcf2e329eef2995781c73a5e07.png"][/img]
UI Update[/h2][p]Our UI team is also hard at work on unifying the game’s interface. In short, our focal points are essentially to make your experience more consistent, making sure the UI doesn’t get in the way anymore, and allowing our UI’s to be more predictable and scalable. 

To actually show you, instead of writing promising words that might feel empty, we’ve included a bunch of images. Keep in mind though, that these images are a work in progress outline for the design, and their looks will be updated to fit in better stylistically with the medieval setting of Pax Dei. 

We’re aiming to make our in-game main menus, like our Inventory, Crafting menu, Character menu (currently equipment), Clan Menu, Markets, and Grace, follow the standard of our latest Journal update. So we’re gradually moving to a more docked panel on the right side of the screen, moving the UI more out of the way so you can focus on the world of Pax Dei and its gameplay. Identical to the latest Journal update, we’re also moving the details of the focused item into a floating tooltip. Aside from these bigger, more visually apparent changes, we’re also updating all of the keybind inputs along the way to make sure that the UI of the menus no longer conflict with the inputs that you need for combat and other gameplay-related features.[/p][p][/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/1bfe11a1c9b32c6dfb93b3a49fb46c2ce45f29c1.png"][/img][img a bit of previously built systems. We know you’ve been waiting, and we are working hard with our small team to get these improvements in as fast as possible for you. Because of this, we are aiming to roll these updates out in chunks, so you’ll get to enjoy updates more frequently. 

We’re excited about making Pax Dei better, and we’re looking forward to getting these updates in, we wanted to give you a glimpse of what’s coming to share that excitement with you.[/p][p]

The Mainframe Team[/p]

notes.title: Pax Dei - The journey so far
notes.content:
[p]Hello Paxians,[/p][p]We recently celebrated one year of early access for Pax Dei and wanted to provide an update on where we come from, where we’re at, and what’s coming.[/p][p][/p][h2]The beginnings[/h2][p]Pax Dei has been long in the coming. The idea for the game started brewing in the minds of a few of the Mainframe founders 20 years ago. The core of the game was clear already back then: making an open sandbox world inspired by medieval myths, driven by players in a fully open economy. The first challenge was that what didn’t exist back then was a game engine capable of running the game as envisioned, with visuals grounded in the real world but made larger than life, so one would yearn to live in the world of Pax Dei with a sense of wonder. The second challenge for MMOs has historically been the server-side capabilities needed to run a game with thousands of players. The requirements of MMOs are enormous compared to other games, and the game as envisioned just would not have been possible 20 years ago.[/p][p]In 2019, we decided it was time and founded a company to make the game real. What had changed was that the Unreal Engine render engine was now very mature and could cater for the style of visuals we wanted, and server compute & Internet bandwidth was now on a level that could be used to run the game. As with most game projects, it took about a year to get a team together, so the preproduction effort for Pax Dei began in earnest in 2020, with us working on designs and developing technical solutions to drive the MMO backend needed on top of Unreal. Another piece of technology we put a significant emphasis on was the world generation pipeline, to enable our relatively small world team to build a game world hundreds of square kilometers in size.[/p][p]With the player community being the core of the game - all the really interesting things in Pax Dei are intended to be a result of emergent player actions - we started to hit a point in 2023 where developing the game was becoming hard without having the players deeply involved. The Mainframe team has quite a few people who have both worked on MMOs and played them extensively, and we’re very firmly in the camp that believes the player community is what makes MMOs interesting. That, in turn, means we believe developing the game without involving the players from early stages of development won’t result in the best possible MMO, so we wanted to get people on board even knowing the game wasn’t “done” yet, which, in many ways, MMOs never are. As communities form in a game, they shape the game through interaction with the developer, feeding a cycle of adding new gameplay to keep games fresh and interesting.[/p][p]Given we were far from even Early Access at that point, we opted to start running larger playtests inside a closed beta and collecting feedback from the closed community instead of launching the game in public. This worked fabulous and we made considerable strides in improving the game, but even this started to run out of scale for some of the systems, as having a few hundred people in the game was a far cry from the 8000 players we supported for each world instance at the time, so we decided to launch the game in Early Access.[/p][p]At this point, we had a building system that showed great promise, an intentionally simple combat system with a variety of PvE content ranging from simple ruins to larger dungeons, a vast, beautiful world for everyone to explore and the beginnings of a PvP system. The game was, and still mostly is, balanced so that it’s highly beneficial to cooperate with other players, which had worked well in the testing, but we wanted to get more insight on how this plays out with a larger group of players.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/c7de59d9155ade8275a93e899b3cb01657eeee79.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]Early Access starts[/h2][p]Enter June 2024 - the game launches in Early Access, and our real learning begins.[/p][p]At this point, we were very excited and had a ton of plans for what we wanted to put into the game next, which, as you know, got published as a roadmap. In hindsight, we should have been clearer at that point about wanting to change the plans according to feedback from the community and the roadmap as published at that point was a 100% full booking from the team with relatively little booking for changes from all of you, which obviously started flooding soon after.[/p][p]As you know, the first weeks were pretty rough. We discovered several issues that hadn’t been uncovered in earlier tests, despite those being pretty big. So, in the first month, the team was in firefighter mode and literally fixed more than 100 bugs a week, primarily based on reports from the players. While the fixing was ongoing, we were also collecting feedback from new players and reflecting the roadmap we had for the game against the feedback. And by reading all the feedback, it was evident that the first major update post-launch would have to focus on improving pretty much all areas of the game instead of adding significant new features.[/p][p]The first update, Proving Grounds, included pretty massive changes to the world and progression. We’d underestimated the amount of time people would play the game alone, even if in a clan. So we restructured the PvE sites and added a significant amount of soloable and small group PvE content into the Heartlands. The combat system got extensive changes on the locomotion to stop the game from feeling like the combat was fighting your controls, which hugely improved the overall feel in combat. Literally everything was rebalanced, aiming to make crafting less grindy. Many locations in the world were found that could be blocked out in unintended ways, which were adjusted, and a lot of roads were added. A load of usability issues were fixed. Last but not least, we made significant changes to the building system to improve performance, where the towns and cities that all of you were building turned out to be a lot bigger than anyone had anticipated.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/d37e750b71feabcf35b0fcf84d4d4ad6ace6d401.jpg"][/img]While most of the team was focusing on the Big Fix Update, we were working on two initiatives that saw the light of day later in the fall of 2024.[/p][p]A huge patch updated the game to use Discord as the underlying tech for chat. Using their tech, we added a load of critical features into the game - friend list, DMs to friends and better public text channels, as well as prepped the game for more features like voice chat. Great communication tools are essential inside an MMO, and this was a big step toward improving them. Chat is also a good example of a feature we all take for granted in MMOs, and due to it being a prominent feature, we never really consider how much effort it takes to implement it well. For smaller developers, these must-haves can end up consuming a large portion of the team time, as no ready-to-use solutions exist for almost anything one needs in games.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/790c4bc6d2f6683b8976a7815b0d90c28a68ec32.jpg"][/img]The second big thing to land was the Market Square patch, which added the Gold currency and marketplaces you can build onto your plots. The market is a crucial piece of the puzzle for making the game economy interesting, and while we’d know this to be the case, many of you reminded us of this in a flood of feedback for this not being in the game before the update.[/p][p]We added to Verse 2 in January by introducing another critical component of the game economy loop - Grace and Miracles. You get Grace by sacrificing Gold, which allows for a variety of non-combat spells to be cast, enabling Gold to have value. We originally intended to launch Grace and Markets at the same time, but the plan changed as we were implementing the two and discovered how hard it was to create a full-blown technical solution that works for an MMO. We deemed the markets inherently valuable and pushed them out early, with a plan to follow with Grace as soon as we could, which we did.[/p][p]The Market Square update triggered a flurry of feedback. One of the biggest gripes you all had was the distributed nature of the markets. While building a stall on your plot was deemed great, running around a valley to find deals was considered too much effort, resulting in overall poor experience. We already had a design to address this, so based on the feedback this was prioritised as an important improvement.[/p][p]The update in March added the ability to browse all the markets in the world area you were in at the time. While working on this, we also decided to improve the navigability of the world. The game earlier had a wind feature where you could mark a spot in the map and then press a key to get wind to blow in the direction of the marker, but this was both unknown to a lot of players and worked poorly in many world areas, so it didn’t actually help navigation very much. The replacement for the wind was a compass in the HUD, with indicators for your plots and other nearby points of interest, along with a marker to a market picked in the remote browsing, making the process of navigation a lot easier.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/e6e65aa26400d1fcdc73e4b3ecb9f87889234df2.jpg"][/img]The update also added a bunch of building content, using a mix of ideas from our Discord community and our designs. We also added voice chat that had been requested by many players and automated the selection of harvesting tools for wood chopping and mining.[/p][h2]Verse 3 - The latest update[/h2][p]The next major update - Path of the Adventurer - took until June to go out. We originally wanted this to release around a month earlier, but the QA & polish process for the release ended up taking a lot longer than expected. What happened here is as follows.[/p][p]One of the biggest sources of feedback for the game had been the combat system, or lack thereof, as some of you would say. The game launched with a very simple combat model and this clearly did not meet the expectations of many of you. The first update after launch fixed combat locomotion issues, which helped a lot, but the big missing feature was still the ability to meaningfully form the MMO holy trinity groups, with some players specializing as healers, some tanking and some acting as DPS. This also meant there was a very specific tank mage set of armor that was the most optimal for playing Pax Dei, which devalued a lot of the game progression and made it a lot less interesting than any of us wanted. The combat team decided to address this for real and started the combat system revamp already in November.[/p][p]The work ended up taking six months, with a lot of the combat being essentially reimplemented. The changes are too numerous to list here, but with the new combat system and gear progression, we now have a much deeper, more interesting progression for combat, with the specialized roles the player community had been asking for.[/p][p]At the same time, we had listened and learned quite a bit about how the world worked for a variety of things, from resource gathering to travel and PvE to population density. The world team decided to put these learnings into practice and make sweeping changes into the world. This meant increasing the amount of buildable area in the game to increase the population count of a world to 14,000 players, adding crafters around the Petrae Dei to make new player life and travel easier and redesigning the biome setup in the world to make the resources found in each biome more distinct.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/9ca5e6d081e9e7e47f7d7945a86ade8ba13e5164.jpg"][/img]This, of course, came with another massive balancing pass on the crafting to match the new biomes, but also to address another pain point from the community. While it was great that the crafting had co-dependencies between professions, we had implemented this in a manner where it was hard to progress in any of the professions without progressing in all of them. This was a massive undertaking for any player and not really what we wanted, where the intent had always been that you could progress in a profession as a master and not need to spend time in all professions. Verse 3 - Path of the Adventurer saw huge changes in this, for the better.[/p][p]Our original plan was to launch these as separate updates, but come spring and us starting to package Verse 3 to be releasable, we realized the complexity of version management for the changes effectively forced our hand into combining everything into one huge update - bigger than any of the prior updates - and getting this into properly playable state took a lot longer than we expected.[/p][h2]But not the last one…[/h2][p]This is pretty much where we’re at with the public updates at the time of writing this. We ended up making a huge amount of progress and changes during Early Access have improved the game significantly compared to a year ago. We did end up implementing a lot of things we’d talked about, but also as it happens, the changes we made based on learnings and feedback ended up eating a lot of our time, so not everything we thought of a year ago ended up making it into the game.[/p][p]Having said that, let’s talk about what we think we’d like to do in the future.[/p][p]Pax Dei is intended to be a living, breathing beast nurtured by both us at Mainframe and you, the players. Our job is to funnel a mix of our and your ideas into the game to make it as good as possible and ensure you have a great time playing and enjoying the company of everyone in the Pax Dei community. As such, we don’t foresee a future where we stop adding features and content into the game - the upcoming 1.0 moment is not the end of this continuous evolution of Pax Dei.[/p][p]The big theme of what we’re planning to do next is the societies in the game. This entails organizing as groups beyond clans, both for your benefit but also for the purposes of conflict. In practical terms, we’re finally working on expanding the conflict and PVP in the form of the Feudal system and looking at adding a deeper social layer to the Grace mechanics. The main focus of development for the rest of the year is planned to be in this area. Our intent and goal is that, quite soon, each of you will not only belong to a clan, but also to other larger player-driven organizations that have influence in how the game plays.[/p][p]While those systems form the basis for our work, we’ll also continue to work on items we’re hearing from the community. The social layers we’re looking at strongly synergize with finally improving the permissioning, both for clans and plots. We’re reading all your feedback on the crafting systems, and we’re indeed grinding our way through the balancing to improve the crafting experience and to make some of the less developed professions better. As an example, work is underway to make the foods and potions a lot more interesting, with a more diverse range of buffs. We’ll also definitely look into everything that touches the economy, from markets to loot, as it all ties strongly into how the game works as a social sandbox.[/p][p]The next update of the game will start by setting the stage for what's to come. The old Lyonesse will be gone and replaced by a new, much larger Lyonesse, the same size as the other Provinces, which will be needed for the gameplay we’ll be introducing in updates as the year progresses. As a first taster, there will be two new resources exclusively available from Lyonesse, which will enable a new Enchanting feature tied to Alchemy and Jewelcrafting. After refining the resources with the two professions, you can manufacture consumables that permanently boost the Item Power of enchanted items. There are rumors that Cultists in the area are also interested in the resources, so keep an eye out for the gatherers and collectors in the area.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/677d8673873a7b0b3d94aa96cc2ac59f4330ffa6.png"][/img]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/717aedcd1994c3f78047d801794eba5ebc3e62d9.png"][/img][/p][p]As an aside, one reason we’ve been changing the inventory icon symbols recently is the work related to showing the Enchantment status of items in the icon. The other related feature that needs a place in the icons is Master Crafting, where the design intent is that, in the future, any item with Item Power that gets crafted with a near 100% success rate will get an additional Item Power boost and Master Crafted label.[/p][p]The rationale for these changes to Lyonesse is twofold. Firstly, with unique resources in Lyonesse, we wanted to tune the risk-reward for playing in Lyonesse. Especially with some of the harvesting being tied to PvE, the additional risk of PvP meant we wanted to make it easier to slip into Lyonesse, get some goods and slip out undetected, as the number of people playing in Lyonesse is expected to grow quite a bit.[/p][p]Secondly, we don’t yet have an ETA for the other features we’re working on for Lyonesse, but we intend to add Trade Towns where you’ll bid gold to get hold of a plot safe from PvP, as well as PvP battling over controlling towers and their associated areas to build a home in Lyonesse. As mentioned above, this requires space in the world area.[/p][p]The features in Lyonesse will be built on top of a foundational Feudal System. This is a new system that will allow the formation of PvP alliances, which will influence the PvP flagging in Lyonesse. We are also looking at connecting the alliances into a dominion system that will allow taxation of the player markets based on a set of rules on which properties the alliance controls in the world.[/p][p]Last but not least, we’re looking at introducing Parishes. On a high level, this will mean the ability to create an altar that forms a parish, to which other players can join. As players in a parish earn grace, Priests and other members of the Parish who are in a position of power will gain a Grace kickback. This system will come with Miracles that are very expensive and effectively only available to the players in a position of power, with some tied into enabling actions for the Feudal alliances.[/p][p]With all that said, thanks for reading until the end. We’ll be releasing more details on all of the above as things get closer to release.[/p][p]Pax vobiscum, 
The Mainframe Team[/p]

notes.title: Verse 3 Part 2 is now live
notes.content:
[p]Hello Paxians,[/p][p]Our latest content update is now live.[/p][p]This minor content update is a continuation of Verse 3, in which we’re introducing quite a few changes to enhance your gaming experience. Let’s deep dive into what’s coming.[/p][p]
[b]New Journal[/b][/p][p]We’re making updates to the UI, including the Journal, so that it displays recipes more effectively and smoothly, as well as the Plot window and item tooltips. It is still a work in progress, but most are here.[/p][p][/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/bec296b85738aa46e33129c7f963f7a5446f3d15.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/81587c1ea4ed9f3a1d9a459051348c9b3eb5da30.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/2e7939ff193030094c15e4500436fb0da39c74d9.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/8eab467c1b3ac97198f1ca5d89adfb891a649717.jpg"][/img][/carousel][p][/p][p][b]Storage at Petra Dei[/b][/p][p]We’re adding a personal storage at the Petrae Dei to complete the crafters already implemented with the previous patch. Each Petra Dei will have its own storage, serving as a private storage space for each player. Each Petra Dei storage unit starts with 20 slots and can be expanded to a maximum of 80 slots, with some Grace offerings.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/2b14206e7352e9f01746f446edddd6c5c921d62e.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]New Sky, New Lights[/b][/p][p]We’re making visual updates to what we call the “Cosmos”. For example, you’ll be able to see new biome atmospherics and color grading. There will also be a new multilayered cloud system. We’re also improving the lighting in previously overly dark areas such as caves, forests and building interiors.[/p][p][/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/3a0d554141cfa1d410ab0282ec315ac87f15860f.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/ea20c8fce46743c5ec1bdfc4d6ca8c7fe63ad02b.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/3aa57c643361a9ea6538b16bf47b893179ad87cc.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/6b895ee5bc2732b934b368f11d44a017fb2ce622.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/ba412e5d5a6241496aa9258aeba1c4e2086bca2f.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/19e70f3124f0bc5fac82793e121daa225cfeccfc.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/159935d367bb2d78208edfa5223ea2a530b4e1cc.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/b143ab99d8ea6cef9446314ce84ef2cd421c0801.jpg"][/img][/carousel][p][/p][p][b]Markets[/b][/p][p]We’re now adding public permissions to market stalls. When a market stall owner cancels a sell order from another player, the items are returned to the redeeming queue of the owner of the sell order instead of to the inventory of the market stall owner.[b] [/b][/p][p][/p][p][b]New notification system[/b][/p][p]The new notification system introduces several global improvements to enhance user experience and ensure clarity. Notifications are now consistently placed based on their type, always appearing on top without overlapping critical information. The updated menu aligns with the latest UX framework for a more streamlined interface. For default notifications, interactivity has been added to improve the discoverability of new content. To minimize clutter, notifications are now sequenced so that only one appears at a time, and similar types are grouped into a single message to prevent spamming. Pickup notifications have also been optimized, allowing a maximum of three to appear on screen simultaneously, reducing overlap. Additionally, both crafting/harvesting and combat skill notifications now feature improved and consistent tracking of XP progression, providing users with clearer feedback on their development.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Various bug fixes[/b][/p][p]This patch also presents a good opportunity for the team to implement several bug fixes. All details will be included in the patch notes, which will be published on the deployment day. [/p][p][/p][p][b]Premium Status experience[/b][/p][p]As outlined in our recent [url="https://playpaxdei.com/news/information/everything-about-monetization-after-early-access"]blog post[/url], all Early Access players already benefit from the Premium Status, and this hasn’t changed. What’s new with this update is that these Premium bonuses are now explicitly visible and active in-game, allowing you to clearly see and feel the advantages while playing.[/p][p]These include:[/p][list][*][p]+50% Grace from daily login[/p][/*][*][p]+50% Grace from Gold offerings[/p][/*][*][p]+50% XP on all activities[/p][/*][/list][p]The XP rates themselves remain unchanged, as the original Early Access progression was already balanced with Premium Status in mind. However, we’ve taken this opportunity to increase the Grace bonuses, so you will notice a tangible improvement in Grace income after the patch.[/p][p][i]NB: As with all things during Early Access, these values may evolve based on feedback and gameplay data.[/i]
[/p][p]Pax vobiscum,
