notes.title: Everything About Monetization After Early Access
notes.content:
[h3]Hello Paxians,[/h3][p][/p][p]As we prepare for Pax Dei’s full release later this autumn (OMG, LEAK!!!), we’re excited to share full details about how the game’s pricing model will work, including how you can continue to enjoy the core Pax Dei experience without a subscription.[/p][p]Earlier, [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1995520/view/524216645064853377"]we shared our release plans,[/url] and today, we’d like to delve deeper into what Core Access and Subscription mean, as well as how the new Plot Token system works.[/p][p][b]Note that subscriptions will only be introduced at 1.0 release, for which we have no set date as of now. [/b][/p][p][/p][h2]Playing Pax Dei at 1.0 release[/h2][p][b]If you’re an Early Access Founder:[/b][/p][list][*][p]You already have access to the game and won’t need to make any additional purchases to continue playing.[/p][/*][*][p]You will receive a number of free Plot Tokens equivalent to the number of plots of your Founder’s Pack (1, 2, or 4). Each Token allows you to claim a plot for 1 month, or add 1 month to a plot you’ve already claimed. You decide when and how you spend your Plot Tokens. [/p][/*][*][p]You will also receive one month of Premium Status, granting you exclusive perks that will start the first time you log in. [/p][/*][*][p]You will keep your Character Slots and the Founder’s recipes granted by the Founder’s Pack you purchased during Early Access.[/p][/*][*][p]Note that your Early Access progress will not carry over once the game is released, as all plots, characters, and shards will be wiped a few days before the 1.0 deployment.[/p][/*][/list][p][i]Note: the descriptions of the Founder’s Packs on our website, Steam, and Epic store pages will be updated accordingly with this information. [/i][/p][p][b]If you’re a new player[/b], you’ll need to purchase the base game, which includes:[/p][list][*][p]Game access[/p][/*][*][p]2 Character Slots[/p][/*][*][p]1 Plot Token, allowing you to claim a plot for 1 month[/p][/*][*][p]1 month of Premium Status[/p][/*][/list][p]You can then choose between 2 different ways of playing Pax Dei:[/p][list][*][p]Continue playing for free with access to the entire core experience.[/p][/*][*][p]Subscribe to one of our Membership plans for added convenience, storage, crafting options, plot(s), and bonus rewards. [/p][/*][/list][p]Keep reading for all the details![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/ed85678cf0af46efca95b025613c395c9d308076.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]Play free – The core Pax Dei experience[/h2][p]We want to be very clear: you do not need a subscription to enjoy Pax Dei.[/p][p][b]The base game gives you:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Full access to all gameplay systems: PvE, PvP, crafting, building, and more.[/p][/*][*][p]Public crafting stations and storage in starting zones near the Petrae Dei.[/p][/*][*][p]The ability to buy gear and consumables from other players, using Gold looted from PvE.[/p][/*][*][p]The chance to join a Clan and use their plots, contributing to a shared village or an ambitious city.[/p][/*][*][p]Access to high-tier crafting materials and rare loot through PvP.[/p][/*][/list][p]This is the full game, not a demo or trial.[/p][p][/p][h2]Subscription – Expand your role in the world[/h2][p]For players looking to claim and manage their own land, host friends, or dive deep into advanced crafting and trading, a subscription offers added depth.[/p][p][b]By subscribing to a Membership plan, you will receive monthly:[/b][/p][list][*][p]One month of Premium status, activated on the day you activate your subscription, which will grant you bonuses:[/p][list][*][p]+50% Grace from daily login,[/p][/*][*][p]+50% Grace from Gold offerings,[/p][/*][*][p]+50% XP boost on all activities.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]1, 2, or 4 Plot Tokens (depending on the subscription plan you choose).[/p][list][*][p]Each Token allows you to claim a plot of land for 1 month, or add 1 month to a plot you’ve already claimed. [/p][/*][*][p]You decide when and how you spend your Plot Tokens: one by one to maintain a single plot during several months, or all at one time, to maintain several plots during one month.[/p][/*][*][p]Maintaining your personal home in-game enables you to: [/p][list][*][p]Unlock unlimited storage by building your own containers.[/p][/*][*][p]Set up advanced crafters tailored to your playstyle.[/p][/*][*][p]Run a shop by setting up your personal Market Stalls.[/p][/*][*][p]Host your friends or clanmates by sharing your plot’s permissions.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][/list][p]Here are the Membership plans that will be available at the Pax Dei 1.0 release:[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/4e96515580b6def82020ad0b33f8889706d7c20d.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Note that subscriptions will only be introduced at 1.0 release, for which we have no set date as of now. [/b][/p][p][/p][h2]How do Plot Tokens work exactly?[/h2][p]After we exit Early Access, Plot Tokens will be the key to owning land in Pax Dei. Each subscription grants a set number of Plot Tokens every month:[/p][list][*][p]1 Plot Token = 1 plot of land for 1 month.[/p][/*][*][p]Tokens can be used to claim new plots or extend the duration of your current ones.[/p][/*][*][p]You decide when and how you spend your Plot Tokens: one by one to maintain a single plot during several months, or all at one time, to maintain several plots during one month.[/p][/*][*][p]When a plot expires, its contents are safely stored in your Redeeming Queue.[/p][list][*][p]Once expired, your plot will enter a “frozen” state for a limited grace period. You will not be able to build or destroy anything while the plot is frozen. [/p][/*][*][p]If you decide to spend a Plot Token to add one month to that plot, you just pick up where you left off.[/p][/*][*][p]If you choose not to add more time to that particular plot, then all your plot’s content will be safely stored in your Redeeming Queue after the grace period ends. [/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Tokens are yours to keep and use at any time, even after canceling a subscription.[/p][/*][*][p]Tokens remain valid for 12 months from the date you receive them.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Please note[/b] that if you [b]release [/b]your plot, your [b]goods won’t be stored[/b] in your Redeeming queue, and your building will decay.[/p][p]This gives you flexibility: whether you’re an active landowner or playing more casually, you remain in full control.[/p][p][/p][h2]How does Premium Status work exactly?[/h2][p]Each subscription plan grants one month of Premium Status from the start date, and this status is renewed automatically each time the plan is renewed. Premium Status and Plot Tokens are not tied: after canceling your subscription, you can run out of Premium Status but still have Plot Tokens left to activate, depending on how you use those. [/p][p]The bonuses granted by the Premium Status are: [/p][list][*][p]+50% Grace from daily login,[/p][/*][*][p]+50% Grace from Gold offerings,[/p][/*][*][p]+50% XP boost on all activities.[/p][/*][/list][p][i]Note: This is the first iteration of Premium Status perks, and they may evolve in the future to align with future content in Pax Dei.[/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/cc3a89c051c8644f96b09d11041571b141d02db6.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]What’s Next? Early testing ahead[/h2][p]To help you get familiar with the system, we’ll soon deploy a patch to the Early Access build, letting you experience the Premium status and its bonuses. Of course, this comes for free as part of your Founder Pack for the remaining duration of Early Access.[/p][p]We’re also adding a personal storage at the Petrae Dei so you’ll be familiarized with the experience without a subscription. Each Petra Dei will have its own storage, serving as a private storage space for each player. Each Petra Dei storage unit starts with 20 slots and can be expanded to a maximum of 80 slots, with some Grace offerings.[/p][p][b]Note: this is not the 1.0 release patch, and no subscription system will be activated during this test.[/b][/p][p]We’ll share a more detailed overview closer to the patch date.[/p][p]We know monetisation is a sensitive topic, and we’re committed to making Pax Dei a game where you decide how to engage. We believe this model respects your time, gives flexibility, and keeps the core experience fully accessible to everyone.[/p][p]As always, we want to hear your feedback, so please drop your questions in the [url="https://discord.com/channels/1071081786962088018/1397549157958549564"]dedicated Discord thread[/url].[/p][p][/p][p]Pax vobiscum,[/p][p]The Mainframe Team[/p][p][/p][h1]FAQ[/h1][p][/p][p][b]How many Plot Tokens can I purchase at the same time?[/b][/p][p]At 1.0 launch, we will offer Membership plans including either 1, 2 or 4 Plot Tokens. Plot Tokens are valid up to 12 months after purchase.[/p][p][/p][p][b]How long does the Premium Status last?[/b][/p][p]When you activate a subscription, you receive the corresponding number of Plot Tokens and the Premium Status for one month. The Premium Status is automatically activated upon subscription and renewed automatically with your subscription, every month.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Can I offer a Plot Token to a friend?[/b][/p][p]We do not propose this feature at present, but it is something we’d like to offer in the future.[/p][p][/p][p][b]What happens if my subscription ends, but I did not activate any of my Plot Tokens?[/b][/p][p]You are free to activate your Plot Token(s) at any time, regardless of whether you have an active subscription or not. Each Token has a duration of one month. Plot Tokens are valid up to 12 months after purchase. [/p][p][i]For example,[/i] your subscription ends on January 15, but you still have 2 unused Plot Tokens. You can choose to activate both on March 1st, or one on March 20 and the other on May 12. [/p][p][/p][p][b]Does that mean I can have a plot active but no Premium Status active?[/b][/p][p]Yes. Premium Status and Plot Tokens are not dependent on one another. Premium Status is linked to your subscription and is automatically activated when you subscribe. Plot Tokens can be spent at any time while they are valid. Plot Tokens are valid up to 12 months after purchase.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Will we have regional pricing?[/b][/p][p]While regional pricing isn’t available at this stage, it’s something we’d love to offer and very much have in mind as we continue to grow and refine the Pax Dei experience.[/p][p]We’re committed to making the game as accessible as possible. We regularly run promotions on Founder’s Packs, so keep an eye out for those opportunities. [/p][p][/p][p][b]Can I purchase additional Character Slots?[/b][/p][p]Yes, we plan to offer the possibility to purchase additional character slots at some point around release, with a limit of 10 characters per account. [/p][p][/p][p][b]Can I still buy a Founder’s Pack or Early Access bundle after release?[/b][/p][p]The Founder’s Packs are only available during Early Access. [/p][p][/p][p][b]Can I subscribe at any time? [/b][/p][p][u]Note that subscription will only be introduced after we exit Early Access, for which we have no set date as of now.[/u] After our 1.0 release, you will be able to subscribe to a Membership at any time and upgrade your game experience with additional benefits. Your subscription will then renew automatically every month. Membership is not required to play Pax Dei and is subject to cancellation by you at any time.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Can I stack Plot Tokens on a single Plot to be spent automatically or will I have to activate my Tokens manually every month?[/b][/p][p]You will have the option to renew plot periods automatically or manually. By default, upon expiration, a plot will attempt to consume an unspent token for renewal. However, you can disable this automatic feature if you prefer manual renewal. Additionally, you can frontload extensions by injecting multiple unspent tokens to extend the plot period's duration.[/p]

notes.title: Patch Notes - 03/7/2025
notes.content: [list][*][p]Stamina Regen on food items (cooked, baked… all non-raw) has been increased by 100%.[/p][/*][*][p]Raw food items were much stronger than intended; they’ve been nerfed. A more holistic revamp of food buffs is in the works, so these food item changes are temporary solutions.[/p][/*][*][p]Jumping stamina cost has been reduced.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the missing status effect icon for the Roar spell.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the Killmark spell that did not give the movement speed buff after the target's death.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where sprinting while autorun was enabled did not consume stamina.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where players would sometimes be invisible to other players.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed some crash issues[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an exploit that was allowing players to ‘re-roll’ spawned enemies.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the intro video[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Patch Notes - 26/6/2025
notes.content: [h3][b]Stamina & Health Changes[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Sprinting stamina cost has been reduced by ~30%.[/p][/*][*][p]Jumping stamina cost has been reduced by 50%.[/p][/*][*][p]Mantle stamina cost has been reduced by 50%.[/p][/*][*][p]Base stamina regen has been increased by 25%.[/p][/*][*][p]Stamina Regen on wearable items (armor) has been increased by 90%.[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Wieldable durability changes[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Durability and Lifetime Durability on all wieldable items have been adjusted. Overall, the durability has increased, while the lifetime durability has decreased. This will mitigate the need to bring several weapons and shields into dungeons.[/p][/*][*][p]Also, Tier 1 and Tier 2 wieldable items have less durability/lifetime durability than before, while Tier 3 and Tier 4 items have more durability/lifetime durability than before.[/p][/*][*][p]Staves have seen their durability/lifetime durability decreased.[/p][/*][*][p]The tools now have different and progressive durability/lifetime durability through the Tier.[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Skill progression changes[/b][/h3][list][*][p]The XP needed to level up, for combat, crafting, and harvesting skills, have been reduced, especially for levels above 20. Getting to the skill max level is still intended to be challenging, but not quite as challenging as it was.[/p][/*][*][p]XP earned from killing enemies of Tier 2 and above have increased.[/p][/*][*][p]Soloable enemies (no skull icon) now distribute more XP when killed in a party of 2+ players. The enemies with a skull (intended for parties) still give more XP overall when engaged in a party.[/p][/*][*][p]Harvesting skills now give XP based on the damage caused as a % of the total health of the tree/mineable/carcass being processed, so tools that cause more damage give more XP / XP event. With the earlier balance, using better tools in some cases was reducing the total XP earned due to chopping/skinning/mining faster and this no longer happens.[/p][/*][*][p]The XP earned in mining, woodchopping, and skinning has been re-balanced to match the new level requirements, so the total amount of actions needed to reach the skill cap has been reduced significantly compared to earlier balances.[/p][/*][*][p]Note: XP progression of the harvesting skills is not currently popping in the HUD when harvesting.[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Carpentry Progression[/b][/h3][list][*][p]We recognized that progression in the Carpentry skill, particularly at higher levels, currently feels too restrictive. While we plan to address this more thoroughly in an upcoming update, we've made some immediate adjustments:[/p][list][*][p][b]Lime Mortar[/b] recipe difficulty has been reduced to [b]35[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]All level [b]39 unlocks[/b] have been moved down to [b]level 30[/b].[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p]These changes should help ease the bottleneck while we work on a broader rebalancing.[/p][h3][b]Other[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Damage to shields from blocking has been reduced by 75%.[/p][/*][*][p]Inquisitor Captain’s Rallying Cry damage buff has been reduced by 80%.[/p][/*][*][p]Searing Rage damage bonus now correctly scales with higher-tier items.[/p][/*][*][p]Imps summoned by Cultist overseers no longer give combat XP when killed.[/p][/*][*][p]The skill required to use low-tier wieldables is now correctly shown.[/p][/*][*][p]The skinning hardness of some animals has been reduced.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed multiple cases where the game unintentionally changed avatar movement mode to walking.[/p][/*][*][p]Resource instances should now be properly rotated.[/p][/*][*][p]Some plant max sizes have been adjusted[/p][/*][*][p]The Sacrament of Strife sound effect has been adjusted.[/p][/*][*][p]The Aura of Life VFX no longer sticks forever when double-activated.[/p][/*][*][p]A keybind field was added to the settings/keybinds menu to allow players to hide the UI.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a number of recipe unlocks that we overlooked when we simplified unlocking requirements to either rely on skill level or key ingredient discovery (not both).[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where HP were not granted adequately upon respawn after death.[/p][/*][*][p]Some item descriptions have been fixed to show correct data instead of a {} tag.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed some localization issues where debug strings were displayed to players.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed some bugs that were crashing the game.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug where resurrecting at a shrine sometimes resulted in having 100 health instead of 1000.[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Hotfix - 18/6/2025
notes.content: [h2]Combat XP[/h2][list][*][p]The combat skill XP requirements and ranges of XP earned for enemies have been comprehensively revamped. The XP for a Tier 1 base level enemy is now 100 XP, with other enemies scaling this number up or down based on the enemy tier and rank. The resulting combat XP requirements are now very close to the crafting skills.[/p][/*][*][p]The XP gained from hard-to-kill enemies has been increased relative to the easier-to-kill enemies. The XP requirements to level up have been adjusted, so it’s highly beneficial to group up and hunt for harder-to-kill enemies instead of grinding easy kills in Heartlands. With the combination of the two, there’s no more effort to level up to the skill cap if you solely kill easy enemies and less effort if you group up and go after the hard enemies.[/p][/*][*][p]XP earned when in parties has been tuned. Enemies intended for soloing now distribute the XP across the party in a manner where the total XP earned by the party is the same as if you were soloing the enemy. Enemies intended for parties now give an increasing amount of total XP based on the party size, for up to 3.3x their base XP for a party of 6, so the most effective way to level up should always be to party up.[/p][/*][*][p]XP gained from animals has been significantly increased to make it easier to level up combat skills related to hunting.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug related to some enemies giving 0 XP.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug related some enemies giving more XP.[/p][/*][/list][h2]Spells / Weapons[/h2][list][*][p]Bow damage has been increased across all tiers.[/p][list][*][p]The arrows provide a stronger progression on damage.[/p][/*][*][p]Bow damage has been increased throughout the whole itempower range.[/p][/*][*][p]The bow handling and draw speed increases faster with itempower.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue that caused Aura of Life spell to cause lingering particle effects and performance drop[/p][/*][*][p]Breath of Joy I & II, Surging Stride and Spirit Stride now do not interrupt autorunning once activated.[/p][/*][*][p]Quiet stand and Sanctified Stance now handle their cooldown properly, consistent with the item slot they are in. They also now correctly forces the other one on cooldown when attempted to overlap their activations.[/p][/*][*][p]Fix for Divine Intervention applying both the <40% heal and normal heal when it was applied.[/p][/*][*][p]Divine shield now only reflects damage up to a maximum value described in the spell's description[/p][/*][*][p]Greatsword weapon special "Guardbreaker" now properly forces a block break in PvP[/p][/*][*][p]Killmark spell now correctly grants movement speed when the target is killed.[/p][/*][*][p]Sacrament of Strife healing provided appropriately scales with ItemPower.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where some status effects were not removed with cleanse or revoke.[/p][/*][*][p]Windlash now correctly shows the duration of the chained status.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue with Jester's Flask spell disappearing when throwing at other characters.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed revoke not removing divine rapture stacks from the target.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed for all non damaging spell projectiles doing damage based on the wieldable damage[/p][/*][/list][h2]Gathering[/h2][list][*][p]Hold to interact resource gathering will now correctly re-equip offhand wieldables upon completion.[/p][/*][*][p]Resource node hardness value now matches the tool's tier required to gather it. (0-4)[/p][/*][*][p]Gathering tool damage progression was rebalanced, significantly increasing the tool damage across the whole range.[/p][/*][*][p]Skinning hardness of wolves were increased to 1 (in the new range).[/p][/*][*][p]Skinning health was rebalanced for all skinnable animals[/p][/*][/list][h2]Audio[/h2][list][*][p]Fixed audio from Water wells being too loud.[/p][/*][*][p]Polished audio for sitting animations.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue with Tempest Command not playing its chain sound on bound enemies.[/p][/*][/list][h2]Crafting[/h2][list][*][p]Recipe List refresh on level up.[/p][list][*][p]When you gain a profession level while crafting and you unlock new recipes, the recipe list now automatically refreshes and you no longer need to manually reopen the crafter.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Crafting Time Reduction[/p][list][*][p]Crafting timers were very excessive (especially when crafting gear). We've reduced these timers substantially or by roughly 1/2. We will continue to monitor feedback regarding them for future refining of the system.[/p][/*][*][p]Gear should now take 9-12 rolls to craft, based on recipe complexity (down from a whooping 21 roll afk coffee break).[/p][/*][*][p]Once fully Mastered, these crafts should only require you 3-4 rolls.[/p][/*][*][p]Other non-gear recipes should also be slightly faster.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Recipe Unlock Progression[/p][list][*][p]Many crafting stations — particularly processing crafters — previously had unclear progression paths that often left players confused or blocked. It wasn’t always obvious what each station was for or how to progress in the associated profession, largely due to missing or hidden recipes.[/p][list][*][p]To improve this, we’ve made recipe progression more transparent: more recipes are now unlocked by default, and key recipes that were previously gated behind obscure item requirements now unlock through skill progression instead.[/p][/*][*][p]These changes affect many crafters including Spinning Wheels, Looms, Tanning Racks, Charcoal Kilns, Pottery Kilns, Furnaces, Tailoring Tables and Leatherworking Tables.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][*][p]More crafting stations unlocked by default[/p][list][*][p]We wanted to smoothen out some basic progression discovery at the start and therefore the [b]Founder’s Crafting Table, Basic Charcoal Kiln, the Log Workbench and the Basic Furnace are now all unlocked by default[/b] in the build menu.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Furnace Parts[/p][list][*][p]Many of you reported that they couldn't find the recipe for Furnace Parts [i]Sorry!![/i]. The recipe can now be found in the Basic Forge, as it should :)[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Steel Anvil and other unintended items[/p][list][*][p]Quite a few items accidentally made it into the game in the latest creation, same with recipes or items visible in the Journal that shouldn't have. A lot of these were either deprecated items or placeholder items that may or may not be part of future content releases. They've now been properly removed. Example: Steel Anvil.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Nightshade Fruit[/p][list][*][p]A recipe for the T2 Alchemy Workbench mistakenly called for a “Deadly Nightshade Fruit” — which, tragically, did not exist. It now correctly asks for Nightshade Fruit. Please note: we still do not recommend eating it. Side effects may include confusion, nausea, alchemical mishaps, and/or death.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Crafting Blessings at max level[/p][list][*][p]When using a profession blessing at level 40 takes you to level 41 but it didn’t effectively increase your skill beyond 40. Now it will! [/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][h2][b]Other[/b][/h2][list][*][p]Fixed an issue in the Construction hammer UI where "Claim a plot to start building crafters" in German and French exceeded its designated space[/p][/*][*][p]Updated localization in several instances.[/p][/*][*][p]Clay now spawns in greater density around water, in addition to new spawn locations near cliffs.[/p][/*][*][p]Hunters have discovered a breakthrough in animal carcass logistics. You can now pile up 20 of them.[/p][/*][*][p]Game no longer switches to walk mode when opening inventory while stationary or when interacting with crafters.[/p][/*][*][p]Spirit regain floating text numbers are now only visible to the user.[/p][/*][*][p]Healing floating text numbers are scaled down when targets are at full health.[/p][/*][*][p]Arrow recipes (in the crafting menu) now show the intended item description.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where swapping equipped items which share the same base granted spell would lose the ability to determine the granting item (and thus their ItemPower) causing them to fall back to minimum stats.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed sprint players being able to sprint without consuming stamina after passing zone boundary[/p][/*][*][p]The gold amount shown in the top bar and in your inventory will now consistently show you the correct amount.[/p][/*][*][p]You can no longer open the Redeeming Queue and Redeem items while dead.[/p][/*][*][p]Consumables now correctly show the cooldown of it instead of the duration of its effect.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed some world areas close to the the Province edges that had an unintended non-blocking landscape mesh.[/p][/*][*][p]Teleporting while wielding a hammer no longer results in an extra cylinder in game view.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h1][b]Patch Notes - Hotfix - 17/6/2025,[/b][/h1][list][*][p]Fixed an issue to address various server crashes.[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Audio Q&A - Verse 3
notes.content: [p]Hello Paxians,[/p][p]Following the Q&A from early June, we received additional questions regarding audio in Pax Dei and in Verse 3 in particular.[/p][p]Here are some answers from our audio team![/p][p][/p][h3]Have there been some major unannounced audio system updates in Verse 3?[/h3][p]As before the patch, there are only ambient and combat modes, but both modes have been heavily revised. In particular, ambience now has more than double the amount of new music, and the soundscape itself has been revised with new details, some of which have been removed and mixed differently. We still have some work to do here.[/p][p][/p][h3]Did armour consolidation affect sound systems in some way?[/h3][p]It is meant to be fully customizable depending on which armour you are wearing and your movement. Currently, only certain types of armour detect changes and detect only bigger changes in materials, but the plan is to have it much more granular in the future.[/p][p][/p][h3]Does mixing and matching different types of armours affect walking sounds, etc., or is it based on a few armour pieces? Does each piece give its own contribution to the soundscape?[/h3][p]It is meant to work that way, so that every little piece has some contribution, but certain types are also not very audible. We haven’t had the opportunity to create all that content yet, but the plan is as your question suggests.[/p][p][/p][h3]Are there new sounds for new building materials? So, walking on a limestone foundation differs from walking on a gneiss one?[/h3][p]Currently, no, and stone will be stone for now, but it would definitely fit into the granular style of the game to allow that kind of detail.[/p][p][/p][h3]You mentioned indoor detection about a year ago. We have not noticed a system like that in-game yet. Was this added at some point?[/h3][p]Currently, there is no indoor system available to detect it on player-built structures. Some dungeons and certain areas of camps and adventure sites have gotten some added manually in controlled areas, but a systemic approach is yet to be fully functional and implemented.[/p][p][/p][h3]Is there any change in audio perspective based on item quality or tier, or is it based on base material?[/h3][p]Currently, it is only on base material, but the technical setup is already able to determine every weapon, wearable, etc. from one another. Therefore, technically, we can add sound to any unique item; it just takes time to create the content. We would definitely like the higher-tier weapons to sound cleaner and impressive than the lower tiers.[/p][p][/p][h3]Are there any "special" weapons/armour from an audio perspective?[/h3][p]Not yet; the audio for weapons hasn't been revised in a while, and there will be a bigger content push in that regard at a later point.[/p][p][/p][h3]How does the new weapon skills variety affects the sounds players hear? Is there a difference between previous attack chains and new special attacks from an audio perspective?[/h3][p]Most special attacks have custom audio that plays along with the typical weapon swings and attack sounds - the game is also mixed quite differently from before, and weapons and special attacks are much clearer and upfront, also sounding different in the mix.[/p][p][/p][h3]Are there pronounced sound effects for skills like for the greatmaul special?[/h3][p]All special attacks are meant to have a little or big special sound with them, to make it more apparent that you made a special attack.[/p][p][/p][h3]We can sometimes hear enemies both in PvE and PvP before we see them. Same for some skills. Are there any plans to have skills affecting what players hear?[/h3][p]That would be a game design decision rather than the actual audio design of it - the sound itself can be changed for players and what you hear, but that decision would be a game design decision, as well as what NPCs hear would be in that field. But it's a very good point and idea.[/p][p][/p][h3]Have there been updates to existing biomes or dungeons?[/h3][p]The mix is different, prioritization of which sounds are allowed to play and changes to when in combat over ambience have been made.[/p][p][/p][h3]Do Verse 3 NPC AI changes affect the audio system?[/h3][p]Not directly.[/p][p][/p][h3]Is the floor creaking sound while crafting intended?[/h3][p]That’s because of the floor material and steps being played while crafting - most of the steps have been altered to play a quieter version of themselves if standing pretty much still.[/p][p][/p][h3]How did you get wild goat sounds?[/h3][p]Finding good recordings is really hard, and background noise is quite apparent. The first pass of the goat still needs some love to be where we want it to be, but it's a mix of various goat recordings and a lot of editing, especially for more combat-focused sounds, as we can’t really go punch a real goat to get that sound, can we?[/p][p][/p][p]Pax vobiscum, [/p][p]The Mainframe Team[/p]

notes.title: Building Issue Messaging
notes.content: [h2]Statement regarding the building issue[/h2][p][/p][p]We are aware of two issues affecting some players while they are building:[/p][list][*][p]Players can sometimes build without structural integrity checks being applied. Pieces that should be immediately destroyed because of a lack of support are not destroyed. These pieces are likely to be destroyed later at an unpredictable time.[/p][/*][*][p]The visualization for structural integrity may not always work. It should show building pieces in green if they have strong support, red if they lack support, and something in between if the support is neither full nor completely lacking. In some cases, the building tool shows all pieces red, as lacking support, despite them having various degrees of support.[/p][/*][/list][p]The above issues combined make it difficult to build reliably, unless you pay close attention to the building piece support visualization. To build safely without a risk of some pieces being destroyed later, you would need to:[/p][olist][*][p]ensure the support visualization is working correctly, and[/p][/*][*][p]ensure the building piece is not visualized as red.[/p][/*][/olist][p]To ensure the support visualization is working correctly, you can check if existing building pieces are showing different levels of support, from green to yellow and orange. Foundations directly on the ground should be green.[/p][p][/p][p]We understand this situation is not ideal and might prevent some of you from building, as they would not want to start over again. Rest assured that we’re working on solving the issue as fast as possible.[/p][p][/p][p]We are also running a script to ensure that all pieces being destroyed will be refunded to the character that built them, in their Redeeming Queue.[/p][p][/p][p]Thank you for your patience.[/p]

notes.title: Path of the Adventurer - Patch Notes
notes.content: [p]This update significantly changes core systems, world structure, and gameplay flow. Verse 3 lays the foundation for a richer, more immersive journey.[/p][previewyoutube="QymybCFt_Oo;full"][/previewyoutube][p]Please note that [b]we anticipate an 8-hour maintenance window on June 11, starting at 8:30 a.m. UTC,[/b] during which the servers will be unavailable. [/p][h2][b]New Features[/b][/h2][h3][b]World[/b][/h3][p]The world has been resculpted, with an increased maximum number of plots per Province. Changes include:[/p][list][*][p]Ten Home Valleys per Province (instead of six).[/p][/*][*][p]Smaller but more engaging Wildlands.[/p][/*][*][p]Merrie and Kerys Provinces have swapped their positions.[/p][/*][*][p]Biome distribution and enemy camp placements have been adjusted worldwide.[/p][/*][*][p]Petra Dei sites revamp with starting crafters.[/p][/*][*][p]Some crafting sites have been added to the world.[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Building/Crafting[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Several professions have been reviewed to fit the RPG changes and to make the onboarding easier, the progression smoother, and the dependencies smarter.[/p][/*][*][p]New starting crafter: the Log Workbench. The Carpenter's Workbench is now dedicated to Furnishing pieces.[/p][/*][*][p]The 'chamois goat' (aka wild goat) was added in mountainous areas, which provides wool.[/p][/*][*][p][b]New Profession: Skinning[/b][/p][list][*][p]Skinning knives with new skinning skill requirements.[/p][/*][*][p]Can be used on dead creatures to extract valuable components for crafting.[/p][/*][*][p]Dead creatures respect the existing rules for looting permission.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Several new building pieces have been added to the game: a Granite Foundations set, a Limestone set, a Log set, and more.[/p][/*][*][p]A hunter-themed Market Stall variant has been added to the game.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h2][b]Gameplay[/b][/h2][h3][b]Combat Skill Progression[/b]:[/h3][list][*][p]We introduced new combat skills reflecting your affinity with armor slots: six skills (head, chest, legs, feet, arms, and hands) per armor strength (Heavy, Medium, Light), so eighteen in total.[/p][/*][*][p]Combat XP comes from killing enemies and now contributes to leveling specific weapon/armor skills.[/p][/*][*][p]Combat XP gains now appear as floating numbers near your character, similar to damage indicators.[/p][/*][*][p]Killing harder enemies generally means they grant more experience.[/p][/*][*][p]Party Experience is shared with all members in proximity.[/p][/*][*][p]Party Experience shares experience depending on the type of enemy killed:[/p][list][*][p]Veteran enemies (shown by a skull icon in their nameplate) are meant for full parties.[/p][/*][*][p]Normal enemies are meant for solo or small groups.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][h3][b]Blocking[/b][/h3][list][*][p]One-handed weapons can no longer block (without holding a shield)[/p][/*][*][p]Improved responsiveness of blocking in certain situations[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]New Gear and Weapons[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Reduced the number of equipment slots: we reduced the number of slots specifically in areas where all armor types didn't have an item available in those slots.[/p][/*][*][p]The following slots are now combined:[/p][list][*][p]Top, Top-Outer and Shoulder slots were changed to a combined Top slot.[/p][/*][*][p]Bottom and Bottom-outer slots were changed to a combined Bottom slot.[/p][/*][*][p]Armor roles are defined using new attributes with these themes:[/p][list][*][p]Heavy armor has the best physical resistances and the least damage. Additionally, it grants the user with bonus threat generation and crowd control efficiency.[/p][/*][*][p]Medium Armor has average survivability and decent damage output. Making it an ideal choice for physical damage dealers.[/p][/*][*][p]Light armor (clothing) has the best magical resistances and the best damage but the worst physical defense values. Additionally, it gains bonuses to healing.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Each armor item in the Head/Chest/Legs/Feet slots has a spell, even for common crafted items:[/p][list][*][p]Heavy armor offers spells primarily for the tank role.[/p][/*][*][p]Medium armor class offers spells primarily for physical damage dealers.[/p][/*][*][p]Light armor class offers spells primarily for healers and spellcasters.[/p][/*][*][p]It is expected that players will be mixing and matching different armor classes for certain attribute setups and spell combinations.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][h3][b]Item power[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Items now have minimum skill requirements to use; if the player does not meet these requirements they will get a notification about not having enough skill to use.[/p][/*][*][p]Item power scales items and spells:[/p][list][*][p]All weapons and gear are now defined with an Item Power, which is used to describe their basic attributes. This helps differentiate Tier levels for gear, while providing more visible, granular gains as players level up the skills associated with their favorite gear and weapons.[/p][/*][*][p]Item quality and Tier level influence the gear’s base Item Power.[/p][/*][*][p]Character skill level further influences the Item Power, further increasing the base stats of those items, and the abilities they grant.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][h3][b]New spells on Armor items[/b][/h3][p]List of spells per wearable[/p][list][*][p][b]Heavy Helm[/b][/p][list][*][p]Mental Fortitude[/p][list][*][p]Makes you [b]immune to displacement[/b] effects and increases your crowd control resistance by [b]25[/b] for [b]20s[/b].[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Quick Remedy[/p][list][*][p]Increases healing received by [b]25%[/b] for [b]10[/b] seconds. Heal yourself and allies in close proximity by [b]170 health[/b].[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Roar[/p][list][*][p]Generates 50 aggro towards all enemies in a cone in front of you. Gain stamina over time based on how many enemies were affected.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Breath Of Spirit[/p][list][*][p]Replenish 64 spirit.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Heavy Torso[/b][/p][list][*][p]Ironroot Grasp[/p][list][*][p]While channeling, the caster becomes immobile, entering a trance-like state. Enemies within a 5m radius are [b]chained[/b] to the ground.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Taunt[/p][list][*][p]Taunts an enemy forcing them to attack you for a while. Additionally target's damage is reduced by -24% for 4 seconds.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Windlash[/p][list][*][p]Pull an enemy to you and cause them to become [b]chained[/b] for 2 seconds.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Breath of life[/p][list][*][p]Regain [b]1086 health[/b] over the duration of the prayer. Can only be used while out of combat.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Blessed Breath[/p][list][*][p]Regain [b]744 health[/b] and [b]90 spirit[/b] over the duration of the prayer. Can only be used while out of combat.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Heavy Greaves[/b][/p][list][*][p]Rallying Banner[/p][list][*][p]Call down a battle standard that stuns enemies on landing. The flag motivates allies, increasing their attack speed by 9% while in its proximity. The flag disappears after 30 seconds.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Sanctified Stand[/p][list][*][p]Increases all physical defenses by 33 for 8 seconds. Protects for the next 12 instances of damage. Reduces mobility for the duration. Can be turned off by activating again.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Aura of Life[/p][list][*][p]Grants allies in radius with +414 maximum health for 20 seconds. Additionally allies in close proximity to you will get 12% increased healing received while the effect is active.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Searing Rage[/p][list][*][p]When active gain 8% damage bonus and 8% Crowd Control effectiveness every time you take damage. Effect stacks up to 10 times.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Breath of Balance[/p][list][*][p]Replenish 74 stamina of a non-hostile target.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Heavy Boots[/b][/p][list][*][p]Surging Stride[/p][list][*][p]Increase movement speed by 4% every second. Stacks up to 10 times. Effect lasts for 15 seconds.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Quiet Stance[/p][list][*][p]Increases all physical defenses by 18 for 8 seconds.
