After 3 stacks have been applied, the next stack will overflow giving 152 health and removing all stacks.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Overgrowth[/p][list][*][p]Heal allies within 7 meters based on the number of [b]regrowth[/b] stacks on them for 98 | 120 | 160 | 205 and refresh the duration of all [b]regrowth effects[/b].[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Bloodfed Grove[/p][list][*][p]Place a 8 meter area lasting 5 seconds which applies a scaling heal over time based on the number of enemies inside the area for 106 | 112 | 123 | 123 | 135.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][/list][h3][b]Weapon update[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Weapon attack chain no longer deals extra damage on the last hit.[/p][/*][*][p]Offhands (like the shield) no longer grant special attacks (Shield slam was removed).[/p][/*][*][p]Shield still grants the ability to block attacks (Right mouse button) and now comes with some additional stats.[/p][/*][*][p]All weapons now have 3 special attacks / spells.[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]New weapon specials per weapon[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Mace[/p][list][*][p]Commanding Strike[/p][list][*][p]Swing your weapon with authority. Deal 130 damage and become [b]threatening[/b], 334% increased threat generation for 10 seconds.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Forceful Strike[/p][list][*][p]Perform a heavy strike, dealing 116 damage and [b]stunning[/b] enemies for 2 seconds.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Earthquake[/p][list][*][p]Smash down violently, fracturing the ground beneath you. The impact deals 391 damage and [b]weakens [/b]enemies, reducing their damage by -12,3% for 18 seconds.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Great Maul[/p][list][*][p]Vexing Sweep[/p][list][*][p]Deliver a powerful sideways smash, dealing 321 damage and generating 100 threat.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Overhead Slam[/p][list][*][p]Prepare for a powerful strike and slam your mace down, dealing 380 damage and 132 threat.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Tempest Command[/p][list][*][p]Become the eye of a storm. Command violent winds to spiral around you, pulling nearby enemies into your reach. Enemies are chained for 2 seconds upon landing.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Great Axe[/p][list][*][p]Armor Shred[/p][list][*][p]Deliver a powerful overhead chop, dealing 162 damage and each strike adds a[b] armor shred[/b] on the target. Reduces the target’s physical defense by -20 for 10 seconds. Stacks up to 3 times.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Vicious Sweep[/p][list][*][p]Swing in a broad arc, dealing 342 damage. All enemies struck gain [b]armor shred [/b]charges equal to the highest count among targets hit.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Radiant Cleave[/p][list][*][p]A vicious twirling, forward moving attack - sending the axe blade’s razor cutting edge through anything within reach. Deals 333 damage on both swings.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Sword[/p][list][*][p]Righteous Strike[/p][list][*][p]Deal 193 damage. Each strike fills you with [b]divine rapture, [/b]increasing attack speed by 4% and movement speed by 5% for 10 seconds. Effect stacks up to 4 times.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Jolting Kick[/p][list][*][p]Perform a kick that deals 192 damage and [b]interrupts[/b] enemy spell casting. If a spell is interrupted, the target also becomes silenced for 10 seconds.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Crusader’s Bid[/p][list][*][p]Deals damage based on the amount of [b]divine rapture[/b] stacks on you. 199 | 319 | 478 | 677 damage. Consumes all stacks when used.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Greatsword[/p][list][*][p]Righteous Slash[/p][list][*][p]Deal 214 damage. Each strike fills you with [b]divine rapture, [/b]increasing attack speed by 4% and movement speed by 5% for 10 seconds. Effect stacks up to 4 times.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Guardbreaker[/p][list][*][p]Perform a heavy rising slash that breaks through blocks, dealing 337 damage. Successfully breaking a block briefly stuns the enemy.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Crusader’s Closing[/p][list][*][p]Deals damage based on the amount of [b]divine rapture[/b] stacks on you. 274 | 440 | 659 | 933 damage. Consumes all stacks when used.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Handspear[/p][list][*][p]Swift Jab[/p][list][*][p]Quickly drive your spear forward in a focused thrust, dealing 194 damage.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Barrage[/p][list][*][p]Overwhelm your target with relentless pressure. Deliver a rapid series of thrusts, each striking for 148.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Intercept[/p][list][*][p]Leap forward to deliver a crippling strike, dealing 365 and reducing the target movement speed by 50% for 8 seconds.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Polearm[/p][list][*][p]Heavy Thrust[/p][list][*][p]Thrust the spear forward to deal 224 damage.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Impaling Strike[/p][list][*][p]Drive the spear down to incapacitate your target, causing them to be [b]chained[/b] for 7 seconds. Deals 411 damage.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Overhook[/p][list][*][p]Perform a full reach thrust for 367 damage. Pull the polearm back to launch the enemy behind your position. Enemy is [b]chained [/b]for 2 seconds on landing.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][/list][h2][b]Rebalance and changes[/b][/h2][list][*][p]Default health now starts at 1000.[/p][/*][*][p]All in-game armor and weapons have been recreated.[/p][/*][*][p]Adjustments to attribute values (downwards) of Max Health / Max Spirit / Max Stamina is now 10% of the base value per second. This happens when food, removing attribute giving armor piece or any other effect makes adjustments to the maximum health.[/p][/*][*][p]Spirit, a new resource to replace stamina as the spell casting and weapon special abilities resource:[/p][list][*][p]Stamina will still be used for sprinting/blocking/jumping/climbing/gathering.[/p][/*][*][p]Used for spells and weapon special abilities (previously was stamina).[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Equipment (armor etc.) cannot be switched while the character is in combat.[/p][list][*][p]Weapons can still be switched but you are then subject to the skill cooldown.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Armor spells share the same cooldown across the same slot to disincentivize armor switching to quick cast spells.[/p][/*][*][p]Weapon abilities share the same cooldown across different weapon types to disincentivize weapon switching while in combat.[/p][/*][*][p]Weapon passives have been removed.[/p][/*][*][p]Weapon & staff normal attacks replenish a small amount of energy.[/p][/*][*][p]Players are able to hold the primary attack input to continuously chain normal attacks.[/p][/*][*][p]New Gear Attributes added to accentuate different playstyles for Tanking, DPS, and Healing.[/p][list][*][p]Stamina Cost Modifier - Reduced stamina costs of your abilities.[/p][/*][*][p]Spirit Cost Modifier - Reduced the Spirit cost of abilities and spells.[/p][/*][*][p]Damage Taken Modifier - Damage Reduction applied before resistances.[/p][/*][*][p]Physical Damage Modifier - Damage modification to the weapon damage dealt by you.[/p][/*][*][p]Magic Damage Modifier - Damage modification to the spell damage dealt by you.[/p][/*][*][p]Attack Speed Modifier - Modify your base attack speed for your weapon.[/p][/*][*][p]Spell Casting Time Modifier - Modify the casting speed if your spells.[/p][/*][*][p]Ability Cooldown Modifier - Modify the cooldowns of your abilities and spells.[/p][/*][*][p]Crowd Control Resistance Modifier - Reduce the duration of crowd control effects dealt to you.[/p][/*][*][p]Crowd Control On Others Modifier - Increase the duration of crowd control effects you deal to others.[/p][/*][*][p]Healing Done Modifier - Increase the healing delivered by you.[/p][/*][*][p]Healing Received Modifier - Increase the amount of healing received by you.[/p][/*][*][p]Aggro Modifier - Modify the amount of hate you generate with NPCs.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Fix: Aggro properly scaling based on damage dealt to enemies.[/p][/*][/list][h2][b]UI / UX[/b][/h2][list][*][p]We now natively support most keyboard layouts (AZERTY, DVORAK…).[/p][/*][*][p]New Input System: The entire keymapping has been reviewed to accommodate the RPG and combat systems changes. Among the main changes (on QWERTY layout):[/p][list][*][p]ESC now opens the inventory (top bar menu).[/p][/*][*][p]The system menu is accessible from the top bar menu's top right corner.[/p][/*][*][p]Q, R, and F are the default for Weapon abilities.[/p][/*][*][p]1, 2, 3, and Left Ctrl for the spells.[/p][/*][*][p]4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 0, - are the new Hotbar slots.[/p][/*][*][p]V is the new Secondary Interact (was F).[/p][/*][*][p]H will open the Teleport and Miracles wheel.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Spell targeting:[/p][list][*][p]Holding ALT while targeting a spell will target the caster (self)[/p][/*][*][p]Holding ALT while casting a targeted spell will skip the targeting phase and cast the spell on yourself immediately[/p][/*][*][p]Party targeting[/p][list][*][p]Each party member has a F1-F6 key assigned in the party HUD[/p][/*][*][p]When in spell targeting mode, pressing the corresponding key will cast the spell on that person as long as they are within the spells range.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][/*][/list][h2][b]Miscellaneous[/b][/h2][list][*][p]Being in combat now has reduced regeneration on different resources:[/p][list][*][p]Health regeneration is reduced to 10%[/p][/*][*][p]Stamina regeneration is reduced to 50%[/p][/*][*][p]Spirit regeneration is reduced to 50%[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Falling damage is now more forgiving. Starts at ~5 meters and becomes lethal at ~20 meters.[/p][/*][*][p]Sprinting and jumping while the inventory menu is open is now possible.[/p][/*][/list][h2][b]AI[/b][/h2][list][*][p]Improved pathfinding of enemies inside dungeons[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced likelihood of enemies teleporting when they cannot reach their aggro target[/p][/*][*][p]When AI is unable to fight with their aggro targets they will leave combat (hard leashing) and regenerate to full.[/p][/*][*][p]Leashing improvements:[/p][list][*][p]When leashing, enemies will regenerate health 4 times faster than before[/p][/*][*][p]Enemies run during their leashing behaviour[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][h2][b]Character[/b][/h2][list][*][p]The Cultists of Zeb have received a massive visual update to fit more of what they are and what they do.[/p][/*][/list][h2][b]Audio[/b][/h2][list][*][p]All crafters now have unique SFX.[/p][/*][*][p]New ambient sounds and music.[/p][/*][*][p]More grunt sounds for the Zebians.[/p][/*][*][p]New spell sounds.[/p][/*][*][p]New mixing to improve transitions and 'busy' situations.[/p][/*][/list][p]Visit our latest publications to learn more about the features and changes in Verse 3: [i]Path of the Adventurer[/i]: [url="https://playpaxdei.com/news"]https://playpaxdei.com/news[/url][/p][p] [/p][h2][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/h2][h3][b]World Fixes[/b][/h3][list][*][p]The grass blend is now smoother across biome borders.[/p][/*][*][p]The size and the shape of clay deposits have been adjusted.[/p][/*][*][p]Improvements to wind and foliage fade.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue in Caves that could cause lighting to render incorrectly when fighting NPCs.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where the lighting in dungeons was too dark.[/p][/*][*][p]The road leading to the northern gate in Lyonesse, the Gwydion Stone, has been moved to the western side of the river, as it was too steep.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where part of a river was lacking water in Lyonesse.[/p][/*][*][p]Inquisitors are no longer spawning on top of banners.[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Building Fixes[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Rebalanced resource costs for various stone foundation building pieces[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed Climbing Ivy's blueprint, which sometimes appeared leafless from the rear side.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an integrity issue with Supported/Curved Beams placed on half-supported structures.[/p][/*][*][p]The moss spread area is no longer affected by opening or closing the door on a stone building.[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]User Interface Fixes[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Fixed an issue where the "deposit gold" pop-up would persist on screen after closing the chest[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue that prevented picking up an item when in Examine view.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where, sometimes, hovering over a spell or a weapon slot blocked keyboard inputs.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where spamming opening and closing the redeeming queue would crash the game.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed performance issues with the redeeming queue when there are many items in it.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where Map markers placed on high-altitude areas were not always displayed in the Compass.[/p][/*][*][p]All Gates are now visible on the Compass from a certain distance, even from nearby zones, which improves navigation.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where Icons sometimes did not appear on the Compass despite being present on the map[/p][/*][*][p]Death Markers can now be seen in all zones, regardless of the distance within the same Province.[/p][/*][*][p]Wieldable Torches and Lanterns are removed from the game.[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Combat Fixes[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Attempting to use a weapon ability on cooldown will no longer interrupt an ongoing attack or combo.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where NPCs could get stuck by dropped inventory items.[/p][/*][*][p]Players can no longer get EXP by simply blocking weak NPCs.[/p][/*][*][p]Players' corpses can no longer block NPCs and projectiles.[/p][/*][*][p]Healing numbers are no longer visible from far away distances[/p][/*][*][p]Zebians no longer use melee attacks when they are far away from players' characters.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue in The Reflection of Holastri where players were teleported to the dungeon's entrance when entering a specific body of water.[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Miracles Fixes[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Fixed some issues with notifications when approaching fast travel destinations.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where specific animations initiated with precise timings could halt fast travel while still consuming grace.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where the Get More Grace key became unresponsive after switching to other tabs in the Miracles menu.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where gate travel would rarely fail, leaving the character in the same Province inside a dead-end segment behind the physical gate structure.[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Chat Fixes[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Fixed an issue where the player could not "Join other Voice Chat" after previously cancelling this option.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where leaving any Voice chat after canceling "Join other Voice chat" resulted in the player being moved to the canceled channel.[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Audio Fixes[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Fixed an issue that caused the main menu music not to trigger consistently.[/p][/*][*][p]Female NPCs and avatars now use appropriate voice and grunt sound effects.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where Zebians' idle grunt was too loud.[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Other[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Fixed an issue with editing the price of a market order while the buyer was starting a transaction.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where Consumables of the same type could sometimes be stacked.[/p][/*][/list][h2][b]Known Issues[/b][/h2][list][*][p]XP gained in combat: the text is bugged in non-EN languages and does not display the XP amount.[/p][/*][*][p]Changing your keyboard layout while in-game does not update the displayed key prompts. You can force a refresh with a logout/login.[/p][/*][*][p]Health, Stamina, and Spirit do not update correctly when the character transitions through zones with a food buff.[/p][/*][*][p]Characters respawn with 100 HP only and no Spirit, forcing them to wait for regeneration.[/p][/*][*][p]When levelling up a Crafting skill, the list of available recipes is not refreshed and needs the crafting station to be closed and reopened.[/p][/*][*][p]The common, uncommon, and rare versions of a wearable item have the same names.[/p][/*][*][p]The descriptions of the spells and weapons' abilities are only available when the item is equipped.[/p][/*][*][p]Contrary to what the patch notes mention, players are currently not able to hold the primary attack input to continuously chain normal attacks. We are looking into fixing this asap.[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Path of the Adventurer is Coming on June 11
notes.content: [p]Hello Paxians,[/p][p][/p][p]We are excited to finally announce that [b]Path of the Adventurer will be deployed on June 11[/b]![/p][p][/p][p]Please note that [b]we anticipate an 8-hour maintenance window on June 11, starting at 8:30 a.m. UTC,[/b] during which the servers will be unavailable. [/p][p][/p][p]Verse 3 is the most expansive and ambitious update Pax Dei has seen to date. If you haven’t caught up yet, don’t miss the deep dives we’ve prepared on what’s coming:[/p][p][/p][h3][b]World changes[/b][/h3][p]The world of Pax Dei is transforming itself to welcome more players, and we are reshaping the land, streamlining exploration, and bringing players closer together than ever before.[/p][p][/p][p]All details: [dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1995520/view/806818250769826386?l=english"][/dynamiclink][/p][h3][b]New RPG system[/b][/h3][p]The classic RPG trinity, Tank-Healer-DPS, will now have meaningful roles in Pax Dei with the new RPG system. From new armors, to new spells and a new resource - Spirit - gear yourself for a revamped PvE and dungeon experience. [/p][p][/p][p]All details: [dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1995520/view/524217913946669175?l=english"][/dynamiclink][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1995520/view/524217913946670580?l=english"][/dynamiclink][/p][h3][b]Updated crafting progression[/b][/h3][p]Crafting is undergoing major changes, with Tailoring, Blacksmithing and Leatherworking being completely revamped, in order to match the new armor system. Other professions will also benefit from those changes.[/p][p][/p][p]All details: [dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1995520/view/524217913946670445?l=english"][/dynamiclink][/p][h3][b]World wipe[/b][/h3][p]All those changes require that we wipe the existing world: we’ll remove your plots and their content will be stored in your Redeeming queue. While your character will retain their crafting skills, all other skills, their gear, and their name will be reset. Clans will also be deleted and you’ll need to recreate them. Note also that the number of shards opening after the deployment of the update will be reduced, as those will welcome more players overall.[/p][p][/p][p]All details: [dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1995520/view/524216011267768620?l=english"][/dynamiclink]And more on [url="https://discord.com/channels/1071081786962088018/1380523264077598831/1380523264077598831"]our Discord FAQ[/url].[/p][p][/p][p]Each of these updates brings meaningful changes that will shape the way you experience Pax Dei moving forward.[/p][p]Keep an eye out for the full patch notes, we’ll be sharing them soon with all the details.[/p][p][/p][p]Pax vobiscum, [/p][p]The Mainframe Team[/p]

notes.title: Path of the Adventurer Q&A
notes.content:
Hello Paxians,

The development team recently gathered for a dedicated Question and Answers session with the players, focused on Verse 3 – [i]Path of the Adventurer[/i]. To make sure you don’t miss any of the key takeaways, we’ve compiled a detailed, topic-by-topic summary covering the most important insights, updates, and behind-the-scenes perspectives shared during the discussion.

Whether you're curious about upcoming features, design decisions, or the vision behind this new chapter, you’ll find everything you need right below.

[h2]Verse 3 Q&A with the devs - Recap[/h2]

[h3]Verse 3 wipe[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]Relics return[/b]: For non-unique relics, you will get back exactly what was used in the original item.
[*][b]Gear materials[/b]: Gear will be broken down into raw resources during the wipe. This includes items that will be removed with Verse 3.
[*][b]Unique relics[/b]: These will [i]disappear[/i] entirely. Faction relics remain and can still be used.
[*][b]Resources[/b]: Steel gear converts to [i]pure[/i] iron. Any raw material harvested stays intact.
[*][b]Items at 0 durability[/b]: These will also return their base materials.
[*][b]Resource refunds[/b]: General policy is that materials are returned in their base form during the transition.
[/list]
[h3]Gear & armor[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]Movement speed[/b]: Armor types do [i]not[/i] passively affect movement speed. Speed boosts come only from spells (e.g., foot-slot buffs), and these are temporary.
[*][b]Armor quality levels[/b]: Common, Uncommon, and Rare are the tiers available.
[*][b]Threat mechanics[/b]: Threat is influenced by damage, specific stats (on heavy armor and shields), and abilities. Both spells and weapon specials can increase threat.
[*][b]Crowd Control (CC):[/b]
[list]
[*][i]CC Power[/i] on tank gear makes effects like stun last longer.
[*][i]CC Resistance[/i] reduces the duration of incoming CC.
[/list]
[*][b]Armor types[/b]: Chain and Plate are both classified as [i]Heavy Armor[/i]. Choice is mostly about material cost.
[*][b]Helmet visibility[/b]: No option to hide helmets in Verse 3. We plan to add it later, possibly with PvP exceptions (i.e., others may still see it).
[*][b]Dye system[/b]: Not in Verse 3. It is [i]planned[/i] for the future, but time constraints prevented implementation.
[*][b]Physical resistances[/b]: All physical resistances (slash, pierce, blunt) are now unified into a single Physical Defense stat. The original types still exist under the hood for [i]future use[/i].
[*][b]Tanking[/b]: Tanks will be able to hold aggro on multiple mobs if supported by a healer.
[*][b]Durability[/b]: Durability will not be increased. You will still need 2 or more gear sets for longer hunting sessions.
[*][b]Gathering gear[/b]: Discussed internally, but it is [i]not part of Verse 3[/i].
[/list]
[h3]Weapons & combat[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]Item Power system[/b]: Item Power affects all stats and scales with item tier (+100 per tier), quality (+100 per quality level), and relevant skill (+100).
[*][b]Weapon switching[/b]: Still incurs a cooldown. No exemptions or changes planned for now. Bow functionality as a pull tool will [i]eventually[/i] be adjusted.
[*][b]Zweihander[/b]: Not returning soon. The Great Sword model has been resized instead.
[*][b]Solo viability[/b]: Not all weapon/armor combinations are suitable for solo play. Some roles (e.g., tank/healer) are designed for groups.
[*][b]Animations[/b]: Most weapon skills use new animations; only a few reuse existing ones.
[*][b]Gathering tools[/b]: Require skill levels to equip. There are no [i]sub-specializations[/i].
[*][b]Damage scaling[/b]: Player skill level increases item power, which directly influences damage output.
[*][b]Weapon cooldowns[/b]: Default layout uses Q (short cooldown), R/F (longer cooldowns).
[*][b]Dual wielding[/b]: Might be added later, but only as fixed sets (e.g., “Dual Axes”). [i]No plans[/i] for freeform dual-wielding.
[*][b]Skill progression[/b]: Combat skills can only be leveled by killing PvE enemies in Verse 3.
[*][b]Bow usage[/b]: Bows are good for hunting now. Ranger-style abilities and bow-specific specials are [i]planned for a future update[/i].
[*][b]Movement during combat[/b]: Characters move during attacks but cannot move freely until the attack animation finishes.
[/list]
[h3]Skills, abilities & Grace[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]Stamina bar[/b]: Only appears when stamina is not full.
[*][b]Ability canceling[/b]: Weapon specials are fully committed once activated. You cannot cancel or fake them currently. This may change in the future for some abilities.
[*][b]Grace & Miracles[/b]: No new Grace or Miracle content in Verse 3. These systems will be expanded later as part of broader social gameplay.
[*][b]Dodge system[/b]: A traditional dodge ability is [i]not planned[/i]. Developers want group tactics over reflex-based mechanics. If dodge is ever added, it will have a long cooldown (20/30 sec).
[/list]
[h3]Magic & spells[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]New spell types[/b]: Divine Orb is a new healing projectile that requires manual aiming.
[*][b]Consecrated Ground[/b]: Reworked; now provides defensive benefits but no longer generates threat.
[*][b]DPS spells[/b]: No major damage spells in Verse 3. They are [i]planned for future versions[/i].
[*][b]Pilgrim’s Fire[/b]: Removed in Verse 3. Similar offensive spells will return as weapon specials later.
[*][b]Grace transfer[/b]: Not possible and Grace [i]will remain non-transferable[/i].
[/list]
[h3]PvP & Lyonesse[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]PvP experience[/b]: Killing players does [i]not[/i] provide combat XP.
[*][b]PvP design[/b]: Abilities were balanced with both PvP and PvE in mind.
[*][b]PvP zone[/b]: PvP remains restricted to Lyonesse in Verse 3.
[*][b]Dueling[/b]: Dueling is a desired feature but [i]not yet implemented[/i]. No ETA.
[*][b]Lyonesse 2.0[/b]: In development. Will offer unique rewards to increase PvP participation.
[*][b]Current Lyonesse map[/b]: No changes to layout in Verse 3.
[*][b]Resource incentives[/b]: Pure iron is now more abundant in Lyonesse. High-tier resource respawn timers encourage gathering there.
[*][b]Skill use in PvP[/b]: All armor/weapon skills are usable [i]except[/i] Mesmerize, Haunting Memories, and Pacify.
[/list]
[h3]PvE, dungeons & loot[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]Forts & ruins[/b]: Increased number, especially in Home Valleys. Respawn times may still be tuned.
[*][b]Group composition[/b]: Balanced around 1 tank and 1 healer. Players may discover more efficient setups.
[*][b]Cave updates[/b]: Slight spawn/difficulty updates; lighting and utility improvements ongoing.
[*][b]Boss mechanics[/b]: Not in Verse 3. Foundations for future dungeon content are in place.
[*][b]Named NPCs[/b]: Now reliably drop unique relics.
[*][b]Dungeon maps[/b]: No in-dungeon maps are planned.
[*][b]Loot system[/b]: Remains unchanged in Verse 3. Further balancing is planned.
[*][b]XP gains[/b]: Higher-tier and veteran mobs give more XP. Veteran enemies are group-oriented.
[/list]
[h3]Clans & group features[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Clan roles[/b]: No expanded roles in Verse 3, will come later.
[*] [b]Party visibility[/b]: Marking groups for visibility is on the QOL wishlist but [i]not coming[/i] in Verse 3.
[*] [b]XP bonus[/b]: Group XP scales with group size and enemy tier (especially veterans).
[*] [b]Clan emblems[/b]: No new emblems or uses added in Verse 3, but [i]planned[/i] for future updates.
[/list]
[h3]Mobs & camps[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Mob rebalance[/b]: All NPCs have been rebalanced for health, damage, and difficulty.
[*] [b]Named vs Bosses[/b]: Verse 3 adds named NPCs with relic drops. No true boss entities with phase mechanics yet.
[*] [b]Solo experience[/b]: Small ruins and caves now explicitly support solo/duo play. Larger camps and dungeons are for groups.
[*] [b]Zebian cultists[/b]: Receiving visual updates. More variety and improvements planned for later.
[*] [b]Damage scaling[/b]: Enemy power increases by tier (1-4) and type (normal/veteran).
[*] [b]Bear hunting[/b]: Bears are tougher but still soloable with good gear.
[/list]
[h3]Resources & economy[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Upcycling[/b]: Wrought iron and impure iron can now be smelted back to pure iron (resource-intensive).
[*] [b]Economy rework[/b]: More materials are used across all tiers, reducing obsolescence.
[*] [b]Node spawning[/b]: Static spawn blocking fixed. Nodes and animals now reposition if obstructed or overbuilt.
[*] [b]Stack sizes[/b]: We acknowledge this needs work; no changes yet.
[/list]
[h3]Crafting[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Healing staves[/b]: Crafted via weaponsmithing.
[*] [b]Crafting rarity[/b]: Determined by rare materials. No mastercrafting bonuses in Verse 3 yet.
[*] [b]Recycling[/b]: [i]Planned[/i] for the [i]future[/i] but not in Verse 3.
[*] [b]Skinning tools[/b]: Higher-quality knives offer faster results. Still being balanced.
[*] [b]Cooking[/b]: Carcass yields and recipes have been rebalanced.
[*] [b]Consumables[/b]: Minimal changes in Verse 3; full overhaul [i]planned later[/i].
[*] [b]Crafting range[/b]: No ability to craft from nearby/plot chests. No plans to add this.
[*] [b]Solo crafting access[/b]: Higher-tier gear can be learned and crafted solo with PvE materials.
[*] [b]Enchanting[/b]: Planned as a future profession; not in Verse 3.
[/list]
[h3]Audio, graphics and performance[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]UE update[/b]: Verse 3 is not on UE 5.5, but asset streaming and server transitions improved.
[*] [b]Audio[/b]: New ambient music, clearer mixing, better spell/NPC sounds. Work continues post-Verse 3.
[*] [b]FSR support[/b]: Disabled due to crash issues; devs are still investigating.
[*] [b]Performance[/b]: Significant improvements in NPC streaming and rendering stability.
[/list]
[h3]World & map[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Wildlands & Home Valleys[/b]: World reshaped to add more Home Valleys, slightly reducing Wildlands.
[*] [b]Terrain features[/b]: Large trees remain. Terrain is gentler with fewer steep cliffs.
[*] [b]Water features[/b]: Ponds added. No creeks or flowing water yet.
[*] [b]Map changes[/b]: Only Kerys and Merrie swapped. No changes to Ancien/Inis Gallia.
[*] [b]Citadel[/b]: Remains closed. Content will be revealed in the future.
[*] [b]Trees respawning inside plots[/b]: trees on plots still appear. [i]Plot setting to suppress them planned[/i].
[*] [b]Construction bugs[/b]: Known issues like the “4-plot square hole” are not fixed in Verse 3, but will be later.
[*] [b]Mountains[/b]: Still present, though slightly softened.
[/list]
[h3]Travel & mounts[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Fast Travel[/b]: Remains unchanged. Petra Mea is the only travel point.
[*] [b]Plot teleportation[/b]: Not available and not planned, [i]but related systems are in early development[/i].
[*] [b]Mounts & travel gear[/b]: Horses and carts are not in Verse 3. [i]Planned[/i] for future updates.
[/list]
[h3]Building & furnitures[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Lighting/Decor[/b]: No new decor or lights in Verse 3, but assets (e.g., sconces, clutter) are being created for later.
[*] [b]Granite foundations[/b]: Available with Verse 3.
[*] [b]Limestone pieces[/b]: Released with Verse 3.
[*] [b]Building rotation[/b]: No vertical rotation planned.
[*] [b]Animal farms & pets[/b]: Desired [i]but no ETA[/i].
[/list]
[h3]Market System[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Buy orders[/b]: [i]Planned[/i] but not in Verse 3.
[/list]
[h3]Food & consumables[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Food effects[/b]: Foods still offer specific defenses, though their effectiveness was slightly reduced.
[*] [b]Balance pass[/b]: Full food and potion rework is [i]planned[/i] but not included in Verse 3.
[/list]
[h3]Miscellaneous[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]First-Person camera[/b]: Might come [i]for building only[/i]. No plans for full first-person gameplay.
[*] [b]Lore content[/b]: No new books/scrolls yet, but the framework is being laid for future narrative expansion.
[*] [b]Night time[/b]: Slightly darker in forests due to denser foliage. General night lighting remains unchanged.
[*] [b]Fantasy setting[/b]: The world is low-fantasy inspired by [i]Game of Thrones[/i]. Magic exists but must be discovered. There are no fantasy races like elves.
[*] [b]Haircuts[/b]: No option to change hairstyle in Verse 3; not planned for now.
[*] [b]Swimming/Diving[/b]: Swimming is simple and meant for navigation (e.g., reaching islands). Diving is [i]not[/i] supported, and [i]no plans[/i] for it yet.
[*][b]Keybindings[/b]: Most gameplay keybindings are rebindable. UI keybindings [i]may[/i] not be fully configurable yet.
[/list]

notes.title: Spotlight - Upcoming Crafting Changes
notes.content:
Hello Paxians,

As we continue reshaping Pax Dei’s core systems, crafting is stepping into the spotlight. With the arrival of [i]Path of the Adventurer[/i], we’re not just adding new recipes or tweaking numbers: we’re rethinking the entire structure and flow of crafting to make it more engaging, intuitive, and meaningful at every tier.

This revamp is major. It complements the updates to combat and progression, and it reflects months of work by the design team to better align the system with how players actually want to play: more meaningful gathering, more strategic crafting, and clearer professional identities.

[i]Disclaimer: it’s possible that, by the time the update is deployed, some minor changes will occur to the details below. [/i]

[h2]Four Key Goals[/h2]

We’ve structured the crafting overhaul around four core design goals:

[h3]Easier Onboarding[/h3]

One of the most common points of feedback from players, especially newer ones, has been that starting a crafting profession feels unclear or overly dependent on other players. We're addressing that by:
[list]
[*] Making it faster and simpler to start any core profession,
[*] Removing the need for a dedicated processing crafter to begin basic crafting,
[*] Streamlining the early game to help you get into the loop quickly without getting stuck on bottlenecks.
[/list]
This lowers the barrier to entry and makes early progression more rewarding.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/de4cb2fa2fc42b6c6a80a0a5b2b772d8cac51dfe.png[/img]

[h3]Real Complexity, Not Confusion[/h3]

Crafting should grow deeper as you master it, not just more time-consuming. We're adding real structure and logical depth to recipes across tiers:
[list]
[*] Tiered complexity: T1 recipes remain simple, but higher tiers introduce more layered ingredient chains.
[*] Cross-profession clarity: Components will now more clearly belong to your profession or to another, reducing ambiguity.
[*] Persistent value: Early-tier items, especially Tier 1, will retain relevance at higher tiers  (e.g., as ingredients or in alternate recipes)
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/3d2efe92401c8f9d3b92201b1b7303b87e0df882.jpg[/img]
[h3]Smarter Dependencies[/h3]

Crafting collaboration is good, but dependencies shouldn’t be frustrating. We’re restructuring how professions rely on each other:
[list]
[*] Components from other professions will now be at least one tier lower than the item being crafted,
[*] This preserves interdependence while avoiding deadlocks and confusion,
[*] It also helps reduce crafting overhead when you’re focused on progressing in your own field.
[/list]
This change keeps specialization valuable without punishing solo crafters or small groups.

[h3]Better Pacing[/h3]

We want crafting to be more about the world, and less about waiting at a bench.
[list]
[*] Progress and costs are being balanced across all three core professions,
[*] We’re increasing the importance of gathering and reducing the need to be idle at crafting stations,
[*] Changes include adjusted yields, ingredient costs, and XP multipliers to reflect this philosophy.
[/list]
This means that your time in the world — gathering, hunting, mining — is what drives your progress, not just standing still and watching a progress bar.

[h2]What’s New in the Toolbox[/h2]

This revamp comes with new workflows, new materials, and ultimately, new gear. Here are some highlights:

[h3]New workflow[/h3]

As we introduced in our recent post on RPG, the crafting changes are designed to support and enhance the new combat system. That’s why tailoring, leatherworking and Blacksmithing are the three professions undergoing drastic changes, as they are the ones used to craft gear and weapons. 
[list]
[*] New spells and gear stats require new crafting inputs,
[*] Combat roles like Tank, DPS, and Healer are now reflected in the gear you craft,
[*] Reworked recipes will provide tactical choices for builders, gatherers, and fighters alike.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/39432046113098f82291275a75d3a7dbf2c05824.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/8a3d6441b0438ffc4bd13c371b1dd4b29e4d4e1b.png[/img]

[h3]New Crafting Components[/h3]

Most professions are gaining a full suite of new intermediate material, designed to support the new tiered structure. These parts will appear at different tiers and will help distinguish recipes by complexity and function.

For example, leatherworkers will now work with a new intermediary material: Leather Splits, available in various qualities. This gives more control over final item quality and adds depth to leatherworking progression.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/9e72ccad3f697c79479db12de68a415c13447a5a.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/9e08b7568e2ab02cdecabdfed62dc9076a971b64.png[/img]

[h3]New Items Replacing Old Gear[/h3]

Almost all existing crafted gear, including weapons, will be phased out and replaced with newly designed items that better match the revamped progression and balance systems.

If you’ve been hoarding mats for that perfect build, keep an eye on the new crafting tables — what’s viable and valuable is about to change significantly.

Crafting is one of the core pillars of Pax Dei, and this update is a long-overdue leap forward. It makes the system more intuitive, rewarding, and integrated with the rest of the game. Overall, progressing in a profession should be more rewarding; the higher the craft, the better the value. However, higher crafts will require more materials, so more time wandering the world - or quite some gold to buy those at a market stall.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/80a5c42181d071750f38778a134c16dee7c601f0.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/064e26ab6107eef99d21edd2c94724117bb7bc07.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/064e26ab6107eef99d21edd2c94724117bb7bc07.png[/img]
Whether you're just picking up your first tool or running a full workshop, we can’t wait to see what you build next.

Pax vobiscum,
The Mainframe Team

notes.title: Clarification on the upcoming RPG System
notes.content:
Hello Paxians,

Thanks to all of you who’ve been diving into our recent spotlight on the [url=https://playpaxdei.com/news/game-updates/spotlight-the-new-rpg-system]upcoming RPG System[/url]. We wanted to clarify some important aspects of the update, based on your feedback and the info shared so far in the various Discord channels.

[b]Spirit vs Stamina[/b]
[list]
[*] Spirit is used exclusively for spells, including those cast with armor, Healing Staffs, and weapon special attacks.
[*] Stamina remains essential for physical actions like blocking, gathering, swimming, sprinting, jumping, and climbing.
[*] The two resources work very differently:
[list]
[*] Stamina: Small pool, fast regeneration.
[*] Spirit: Large pool, slow regeneration.
[/list][/list]
[b]Healing staff & viability[/b]
[list]
[*] Healing Staffs are primarily support tools, but they include a weak projectile attack (left-click).
[*] Soloing is possible, but leveling as a healer is best suited for group play.
[*] Targeting improvements:
[list]
[*] ALT for self-casting.
[*] F1–F6 to target party members.
[/list][/list]
[b]Sigils & rarity[/b]
[list]
[*] Sigils are still required to craft some of the new items.
[*] Items now have rarity levels: [i]Common, Uncommon, Rare[/i].
[list]
[*] Common items do not require relics.
[/list][/list]
[b]Armor, weapons & mobility[/b]
[list]
[*] All players move at the same base speed, regardless of armor weight.
[list]
[*] However, feet slot items include spells that can temporarily improve your movement speed.
[/list]
[*] Heavy armor: More protection, more threat/aggro, and slower damage output.
[*] Tank weapons (Mace, Greatmace): Lower DPS but generate extra threat/aggro.
[/list]
[b]Combat roles & progression[/b]
[list]
[*] This system supports roles like tank, healer, and DPS, without locking you in.
[list]
[*] Note that the spells/stats/armor type is a combination that cannot be tweaked separately. However, you are welcome to mix and match different items from different armor types that come with different stats & spells.
[/list]
[*] Each armour type and slot now has its own combat skill.
[*] Combat XP is earned by defeating enemies, and:
[list]
[*] Shared with your party.
[*] Granted to all equipped weapons and armor types.
[*] Killing veteran enemies (group content enemies, with skulls next to their names) will grant more XP.
[/list] 
[*] Gear (armor) switching will be blocked during combat.
[/list]
[b]Weapons & abilities[/b]
[list]
[*] Every weapon now comes as a “package” with 3 built-in abilities, tailored to its style and role.
[*] Weapon types are now available across all tiers, so you can pick based on playstyle, not just item level.
[/list]
[b]Blocking & defense[/b]
[list]
[*] Shields and two-handed weapons can block.
[*] One-handed weapons and Healing Staffs cannot block.
[/list]
[b]Spells & PvP/PvE[/b]
[list]
[*] Some older spells like Mesmerize or Pacify still do not function in PvP.
[*] Cooldowns: For example, [i]Ambush[/i] (a chest spell) typically has a 50–70 second cooldown, subject to balancing.
[/list]
[b]Durability & loot[/b]
[list]
[*] Heavy armor and weapon durability are increasing while a larger durability rework is in progress.
[*] Loot drop tables are being rebalanced.
[*] Stronger gear is meant to be rare, harder to craft, but with improved durability.
[/list]
[b]Skill requirements[/b]
[list]
[*] Gear now has minimum combat skill requirements.
[list]
[*] For example, if an item needs 30 skill, you must meet that level to equip it.
[/list]
[*] Combat skills scale the item’s power, so investing in your role matters.
[/list]
We will very soon publish a spotlight regarding Crafting changes. We are also looking into the possibility of organising a Q&A with the devs on this Discord in the coming days while we get closer to the release of Verse 3 - Path of the Adventurer. Stay tuned for more details!

Pax vobiscum,
The Mainframe Team

notes.title: Spotlight - The new RPG system
notes.content:
Hello Paxians,

With the arrival of [i]Path of the Adventurer[/i], we’re rolling out the most substantial RPG and combat update to date. These changes have been in development for nearly six months now, and they represent a foundational rebuild of Pax Dei’s core systems.

[h2]The reasons behind the changes[/h2]

Combat in Pax Dei has, until now, lacked some depth, with limited tactical options and gear choices that didn’t matter enough. This update addresses those concerns head-on by:
[list]
[*] Creating distinct [b]combat roles[/b] (Tank, DPS, Healer) without forcing rigid builds. [b]Hybrid builds[/b] remain viable, especially with mixed armor and gear synergies. Your identity on the battlefield is up to you.
[*] Making [b]gear matter[/b]: armor, weapons, and spells now contribute significantly to your strategy and effectiveness.
[*] Giving players [b]more control[/b] through a tactical combat system, improved UI, and a shared resource called [b]Spirit[/b].
[*] Aligning [b]progression[/b] with playstyle: the more you use a piece of gear, the more experienced your character becomes with it.
[*] Introducing [b]Item Power[/b] to make gear scaling visible, meaningful, and skill-dependent.
[/list]
This is more than a patch, it’s the first step toward a new Pax Dei.

[h2]Updated combat system: deeper, smarter, and more purposeful[/h2]

[h3]Item Power and Progression[/h3]

Every weapon and armor piece now has an [b]Item Power[/b] score that scales with both gear quality and your combat skill level. In addition, [b]Armor Skills[/b] have been introduced. These determine your effectiveness with specific armor types. Higher-tier gear requires higher corresponding skill to use.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/3d299893ed2a9e78b42d40f77d282803ce888532.png[/img]
Combat XP is now gained from killing enemies, and it contributes directly to leveling up [b]specific weapon and armor skills[/b]. The harder the enemy, the more XP you gain. Party members in proximity share XP, especially when fighting [b]veteran enemies[/b] (marked with a skull).

[h3]Fewer equipment slots, more impact[/h3]

We’ve consolidated some equipment slots (e.g. shoulder and top slots are now combined) to streamline gear without diluting build depth. Each remaining piece carries more weight in shaping your character’s abilities and stats.

[h3]Gear: more than just stats[/h3]

We’ve redesigned all armor classes to support specific combat roles:
[list]
[*] [b]Heavy Armor[/b]: High physical resistance, increased threat generation, bonuses to blocking, crowd control effectiveness and resistance. Tanking, survivability and crowd control related spells
[*] [b]Medium Armor[/b]: Balanced survivability and damage, frontline dps and frontline utility spells.
[*] [b]Light Armor (Clothing)[/b]: Weakest defense, strongest damage and healing done, spells for healers and spellcasters.
[/list]
Core gear pieces - [b]head, chest, legs, and feet[/b] - now have built-in spells, even at common quality. With 36 unique spells across wearable gear, every piece of armor you choose matters from the start. We’re also adding incentives to [b]mix armor types[/b] to tailor spell and stat bonuses to your build.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/3d8750b170a892bf89b19da0b8de169190fdf74c.jpg[/img]
Examples of spells on gear:

[list]
[*] [i]Heavy Armor[/i]: 
[list]
[*] [b]On Head: Taunt[/b] – Taunts an enemy, temporarily forcing them to attack you. Additionally, the target's damage is reduced by 25% for 4 seconds.
[*] [b]On Chest: Ironroot Grasp[/b] - While channeling, the caster becomes immobile, entering a trance-like state. Enemies within range are chained to the ground.
[*] [b]On Chest: Windlash[/b] – Pull an enemy towards you and chain them in place for 2 seconds.
[/list]
[*] [i]Medium Armor[/i]: 
[list]
[*] [b]On Chest: Ambush[/b] – Become invisible and gain empowered attacks while hidden.
[*] [b]On Head: Jester’s Flask[/b] - Throw a flask that splashes on impact, reducing the movement speed of affected enemies by 40% and reducing their physical damage dealt by 12%. Lasts for 10 seconds.
[/list]
[*] [i]Light Armor[/i]: 
[list]
[*] [b]On Chest: Divine Shield[/b] – For the next 4 seconds, reflect all melee damage taken back to the attacker and heal for the same amount.
[*] [b]On Feet: Spirit Stride[/b] – Increase your movement speed by 20% and regenerate 5.9 spirit per second for 7 seconds.
[/list][/list]
[h3]Weapons: three specials per weapon[/h3]

All weapons now grant [b]three unique special attacks[/b] and there are no more generic final-hit bonuses. Each weapon type has a distinct identity, helping define your combat rotation and strategy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/edff9f42d8a3d874e8ad28c4b1d75c6222189ee9.jpg[/img]
Examples of weapon abilities:
[list]
[*] [i]Mace[/i]: 
[list]
[*] [b]Earthquake[/b] – Smash down violently, fracturing the ground beneath you. The impact deals 403 damage and [b]weakens[/b] enemies, reducing their damage dealt by 12.5% for 8 seconds.
[/list]
[*] [i]Greatmaul[/i]:
[list]
[*] [b]Tempest Command[/b] – Become the eye of a storm. Command violent winds to spiral around you, pulling nearby enemies into your reach. Enemies are [b]chained[/b] for 2 seconds upon landing.
[/list]
[*] [i]Greataxe[/i]: 
[list]
[*] [b]Sunder[/b] – An overhead chop that reduces the target’s physical defense with stacking armor shred.
[*] [b]Vicious Sweep[/b] - Swing in a broad arc, dealing 354 damage. All enemies struck gain armor shred charges equal to the highest stack count among targets hit.
[/list]
[*] [i]Sword[/i]: 
[list]
[*] [b]Interrupt[/b] – A kick that interrupts spellcasting and silences the caster if successful.
[/list]
[*] [i]Greatsword[/i]: 
[list]
[*] [b]Guard Breaker[/b] – Perform a heavy rising slash that [b]breaks through blocks[/b], dealing 348 damage. Successfully breaking a block briefly stuns the enemy.
[/list][/list]
[h3]Healing Staves: better tools for healing[/h3]

Three new Healing Staves, each with a full kit of healing spells, bring dedicated healing roles to dungeon groups.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/7421690a1905994f07ded728aee1e4910a6e1752.jpg[/img]
Examples of healing abilities:
[list]
[*] [i]Cleric Staff[/i]:
[list]
[*] [b]Divine Missive[/b] – Fires a projectile that splashes for 202 health to all allies within 4 meters.
[*] [b]Divine Intervention[/b] – Heal a target below 40% health for 380, otherwise heal for 175 health.
[/list]
[*] [i]Sylvan Staff[/i]:
[list]
[*] [b]Regrowth[/b] – Give a stack of [b]Regrowth[/b] to an ally, providing 15 | 30 | 45 health per second for 8 seconds. After 3 stacks have been applied, the next stack will overflow giving 173 health and removing all stacks.
[*] [b]Overgrowth[/b] – Heal allies within 7 meters based on the number of [b]Regrowth[/b] stacks on them for 111 | 137 | 130 | 232, and refresh the duration of all [b]Regrowth[/b] effects.
[/list][/list]
[h3]New Resource[/h3]

These abilities consume [b]Spirit[/b], a new resource shared across melee and magic users, adding an extra layer of timing and choice.

[h3]Improved dungeon experience[/h3]

[list]
[*] We have completely rebalanced the game, with a specific focus on difficulty. Progression should feel smoother and content we design to be harder (for example, dungeons) should be more challenging.
[*] We’ve improved AI behavior on navigating to and around players. This means that the previous temporary teleportation fix has been removed. Issues with pathing should be rarer, but if they happen, enemies will reset position instead of teleporting to your party.
[*] We have revisited aggro management and made it easier for tanks to hold aggro using their new spells and tank weapons (Maces and Greatmauls).
[/list]
[h2]UI and input updates[/h2]

We’ve made [b]input and interface improvements[/b] to combat, including:
[list]
[*] A new default keyboard layout with access to all 7 abilities - no modifiers needed.
[*] HUD updates to display your [b]Spirit[/b] pool and new party targeting/self-cast options.
[/list]
[h2]What’s next
[/h2]
These changes aren’t just about the now, they lay the groundwork for what’s coming:
[list]
[*] More [b]crafting depth[/b] tied to gear identity.
[*] Richer[b] loot tables[/b] and smarter item distribution.
[*] More [b]build diversity[/b] and better dungeon composition.
[/list]
These updates ensure Pax Dei grows into a world where [b]your gear choices[/b], [b]playstyle[/b], and [b]combat decisions[/b] shape your journey.
 
We’ll be sharing more info about crafting changes in an upcoming spotlight. But for now, we’re thrilled to bring you the first taste of a Pax Dei where every swing, spell, and stance means something. We’re building Pax Dei with you, and this RPG update is one of the most significant steps yet in bringing the world (and its conflicts) to life.

Pax vobiscum,
The Mainframe Team

notes.title: Clarifications: Playing Pax Dei without a subscription
notes.content:
Hello Paxians,

Following our post on Pax Dei’s subscription system, we’re bringing some clarifications on two topics: plot management and Premium Membership - that will answer some of the questions asked regarding the model planned for Pax Dei at release. As a reminder, we haven't announced a release date yet.

[h2]Plot management[/h2]

[h3]What happens when my plot expires?[/h3]

When a given plot runs out of time, it will first enter a frozen state, providing a window to take precautions or secure resources. During this phase, permissions of the frozen plot can’t be edited, no new building piece can be added, while people with access can still destroy pieces and interact with crafters and containers. During this grace period, you can reactivate it, continuing where you left off without losing progress.

Assuming this doesn’t happen, once the grace period is over, the plot is considered expired and will be released. The content of an expired plot is securely stored in your redeeming queue, while the in-game space is now freed and can be claimed by another player, for example, a clan member, ensuring we keep the world of Pax Dei vibrant and full of life. Note that, upon release, adjacent plots will lose any expanded space, and all objects in the joint area will become publicly accessible and begin to decay.

[h3]Will there be some kind of very obvious notification if a clan plot (that you are using as well) will become inactive, or is it only the original owner who will be notified?[/h3]

Only the plot owner will receive a notification that their plot is running out of time and will enter the frozen state. However, once a plot enters the frozen state, this should be clearly visible to all players in-game.

[h3]Is there a way to claim a friend’s plots if they become inactive? Or transfer between players?[/h3]

If your friend becomes inactive and their plot expires, you can place a plot instead, provided you have plots left to be placed.

We are currently working on a feature that would allow plot ownership transfer, however, we cannot guarantee that it will be available at release. 

[h3]Will clan permissions for plots be reworked?[/h3]

We’ve had long-standing plans to add more granular permissions, especially regarding trusted individuals and friends who’re not necessarily in your clan. We expect to get working on this in the near future, but our priority is to add a new clan rank.

[h2]Premium Membership[/h2]

[h3]Will there be an option to pay for a friend’s plot, if they are still active?[/h3]

Gifting of plots (or membership) won’t be available initially. It’s certainly something we will consider adding later if there is appetite for it in the community. In the meantime, we’re working on a feature to allow plot ownership transfer between characters. 

[h3]Will I need a Premium Membership to build at all? [/h3]

You won’t need Premium Membership to build. If you don’t have your own plot, you will still be able to build on the plot of a friend or a clan member, provided they’ve shared permissions with you.

As for crafting, Petra Dei shrines will offer public access to basic crafting workstations - ideal for newcomers or players without land.

[h3]When does the “free month of Premium Membership” at 1.0 actually start? Can I choose when I activate it?[/h3]

As we exit Early Access, Founders will automatically receive game access, and will keep their exclusive recipes and the number of character slots they have now. Founders will also get a free month of Premium Membership with a number of plots corresponding to their Founder’s Pack.

The free month of Premium Membership will be granted the first time you log into the game. 

[h3]Will I require a Premium Membership to access the market system?[/h3]

No, you won’t require Premium Membership to use markets and gold to purchase advanced gear and materials. If you decide to skip the Membership, you will still have access to the same features: clans, crafting, building, dungeons, exploration, markets, etc., except you won't have a personal plot at your disposal.

[h3]Are you concerned that making the subscription optional will open the door to bots and gold farmers?[/h3]

Gold farming and bots have been present in MMOs irrespective of their business models. We will continue to take appropriate action against accounts breaking our Terms of Use and Code of Conduct, regardless of their subscription status.

[h3]What about Founders that have the Journeyman and Master Upgrades, but not Artisan?[/h3]

As we exit Early Access, Founders will automatically receive game access, and will keep their exclusive recipes and the number of character slots they have now. Founders will also get a free month of Premium Membership with a number of plots corresponding to their Founder’s Pack.

In the specific case of players owning the Journeyman and Master upgrade DLCs but NOT the Artisan upgrade DLC, that means: game access, 4 character slots, the Founder’s Outfit and Wyvern Building Set recipes, along with a free month of Premium Membership that includes 3 plots.

notes.title: World Changes Coming with Verse 3: Path of the Adventurer
notes.content:
Hello Paxians,

Verse 3 brings a major transformation to the world of Pax Dei: reshaping the land, streamlining exploration, and getting players closer together than ever before. From social-focused design changes to structural foundations for future features, here’s what awaits you in [i]Path of the Adventurer[/i].

[h2]More Heartlands, Closer Communities[/h2]

The number of Heartlands, aka the home valleys, has increased from 6 to 10 per Province, as seen on the [url=https://playpaxdei.com/media/player-resources]newly updated maps[/url]. These valleys are now [b]smaller and more numerous[/b], and the reasons behind this change are both practical and social:
[list]
[*] [b]Higher player density[/b]: You’ll now encounter other players more often, making the Heartlands feel livelier.
[*][b] Stronger local communities[/b]: Tighter spaces foster more natural cooperation, trade, and neighborhood-building.
[*] [b]Smarter Wildlands[/b]: Previously vast and often empty, the Wilds have been slightly reduced in size to concentrate activity, encourage encounters, and make exploration more meaningful.
[*] [b]Improved balance[/b]: Biome distribution and enemy camp placement have been adjusted across the world to ensure a smoother progression and more thematic consistency. The enemy camp’s density has also increased significantly, both in the Home Valleys and the Wildlands.
[*] [b]Scalability[/b]: With more Heartlands per Shard, the world can now accommodate a growing player base without fragmenting the community.
[/list]
This marks one of our boldest steps yet toward a more dynamic, interconnected world.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/1a9d8229c668b9a28e121013753ad416d1638ba7.jpg[/img]
[h2]A Living, Breathing World[/h2]

The world of [i]Pax Dei[/i] has never felt more alive or more mysterious.

Across every valley and ridge, you’ll discover [b]new sites and visual upgrades[/b] that elevate the landscape and deepen immersion:

[list]
[*][b] Revamped stone circles[/b], each with unique architecture and a stronger sense of history.
[*] [b]Rebuilt Petra Dei starting zones[/b], reimagined as ancient sanctuaries turned base camps, complete with warmth, crafting stations, and space to welcome new and future ‘plotless’ players.
[*] [b]Adding crafting sites[/b], expanding settlement strategies, and crafting hubs. On top of the revamped Petra Dei sites, we added some small crafting sites with public crafting stations in the Home Valleys and the Wildlands.
[/list]
And if you're paying attention, you'll notice [b]sealed cave entrances, foundations for future town sites[/b], and [b]ominous Inquisitor Citadels[/b] on the horizon, silent promises of stories yet to unfold.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/2e8adda76668165fd4d759fcdfa479890ada23db.jpg[/img]
The natural world has evolved too:
[list]
[*] [b]Forests are thicker[/b], richer in atmosphere and detail.
[*] [b]The Corrupted Planes twist with strange new growths.[/b]
[*] Regions like the [b]Scrublands, Whispering Woods, and Cursed Rockland[/b] have been refreshed with deeper textures and moodier biomes.
[*] [b]Grass and trees sway with the wind:[/b] we made some improvements to limit motion sickness while keeping the atmosphere vivid.
[*] [b]Ancient Stelae[/b] are now more naturally embedded in the terrain, enriching lore and immersion.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/20b935438fe7ae3ecb9971ee0dc71b72b51a7cb0.jpg[/img]
To complement the visual upgrades, the terrain itself is now more welcoming:
[list]
[*] [b]Fewer steep cliffs[/b], smoother [b]travel routes[/b], and improved [b]road intersections[/b] mean easier, more enjoyable navigation.
[*] [b]Backdrop mountains and snowlines[/b] have been fine-tuned for visual coherence.
[*] [b]Small ponds[/b] now dot the countryside, adding charm and diversity.
[*] And though the world retains its rolling hills, [b]foundation pieces make it easier than ever to build on any terrain[/b].
[/list]
[h2]A Not-So-Subtle Map Shift[/h2]

If you're a seasoned traveler in Pax Dei, you might notice something... off. That’s because [b]Kerys and Merrie have swapped places on the map[/b].

This wasn’t part of a grand redesign plan, rather, a practical adjustment driven by [b]some upcoming needs tied to Verse 4[/b]. We needed to create a bit more room near the Lyonesse gates, and this reorganization turned out to be the simplest way to make it happen.

We understand this may feel disorienting at first, especially for veteran players. But we hope the long-term benefits will make it worth the adjustment.

[h2]Polish, Performance, and Promise[/h2]

Behind the scenes, the world’s streaming systems have been upgraded for [b]better performance and faster asset loading[/b]. Countless floating objects, terrain glitches, and visual oddities have also been cleaned up to provide a more polished and consistent experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/49fcea1b4d1f8ec94872880ba00cc307ac456dd1.jpg[/img]
Together, these changes bring a world that feels more cohesive, more believable, and more ready for the adventures to come.

We hope you're as excited as we are to set foot in this revitalized world when [i]Path of the Adventurer[/i] launches.

Stay tuned for upcoming deep dives into the [b]RPG system overhaul and crafting evolution[/b].

Pax vobiscum,
The Mainframe Team

notes.title: Playing Pax Dei without a subscription
notes.content:
Hello Paxians,

Today, we want to talk about one of the new features coming out with Verse 3 - Path of the Adventurer - and how, combined with other changes we’ve introduced over the last few months, it opens the option to play Pax Dei without a plot — and therefore, without a subscription.

Yes, you read correctly. We've listened closely to your feedback and decided to adjust our approach to monetization. We don’t yet have all the details to share, but we can already confirm that, as we exit Early Access, [b]we will offer a way to play Pax Dei without a subscription.[/b]

[h2]New spawning zones[/h2]

With Verse 3, we will start to introduce new [b]Petra Dei spawning zones[/b]. 
[list]
[*] Each spawning area will now feature starting crafting stations, allowing all players to craft basic (aka Tier 1) items.
[*] At a later point, the altars in front of Petra Dei will grant access to private storage. While each Petra Dei altar offers unique storage, it will be shared across all your characters on a given shard/world.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/f4e2942877cb342d1cd77a227cfd249956dbf6f1.jpg[/img]
These changes are meant to make discovering the game easier. New players will be able to craft basic equipment and start their adventures sooner, but this also opens a way to play Pax Dei without the need for a personal plot.

[h2]Playing without a plot[/h2]

Playing without a personal plot won’t hold you back. We’ve been introducing, and will keep adding in the coming weeks and months, a number of changes to the game to allow plot-less play, along with reinforcing game loops that don’t rely on plot ownership:
[list]
[*] The [b]Clan system[/b] already allows players to share plot permissions with their Clan mates.
[*] The recent introduction of the [b]Gold economy[/b] enables players to buy gear and consumables from other players, without having to craft everything themselves.
[*] Finally, the new [b]Petra Dei spawning zone[/b] will offer limited individual storage to each player, and their surroundings will feature basic crafters for public use.
[/list]
Allowing all play styles to connect and complement each other is one of the core tenets behind Pax Dei. If you’re the kind of players that prefers fighting Inquisitors, wants to specialize in dungeon crawling, or simply likes to hang out with friends and help them in their projects, we wanted to open a way to enjoy Pax Dei without having to own and maintain your personal plot — and therefore [b]without a monthly subscription.[/b]

[h2]Introducing: [i]Premium Membership[/i][/h2]

For those who do want their own personal plot(s), we will introduce the Premium Membership program. It will offer several [i][u]entirely optional[/u][/i] subscription plans. Premium Members will enjoy various in-game benefits - we’re still working on finalizing the offer - the most important being the [i][u]ability to claim and maintain in-game plots[/u][/i].

By picking the [i]Premium Membership[/i] plan that best suits their needs, players will choose how many plots they want to claim in-game. If they decide to cancel, the space will be freed up for other players at the end of the subscription period, and the content of the plot will be stored in the player’s Redeeming Queue, allowing players to quickly rebuild in a new location when they decide to come back.

Pax Dei base game will include a free month of [i]Premium Membership[/i] with 1 plot.

[h2]Founders at launch[/h2]

[u]Founders don’t need to purchase anything at launch[/u]. As we exit Early Access, Founders will automatically receive game access, keep their exclusive recipes and the number of character slots they have now, as well as get a free month of [i]Premium Membership[/i] with a number of plots corresponding to their Founder’s Pack (1, 2 or 4).

We’ve aimed for a balance that offers [b]flexibility[/b], multiple ways to engage with Pax Dei based on your play style, and [b]sustainability[/b], ensuring the most engaged players can support the project long-term.
We’ll share more details on how [i]Premium Membership[/i] works, its bonuses and pricing as we get closer to release. Stay tuned!

Pax vobiscum,
The Mainframe Team

notes.title: Upcoming wipe - Your concerns about the RP Shards
notes.content:
Hello Paxians!

First, we want to thank you all for your continued passion and feedback around [b]Verse 3 – Path of the Adventurer[/b]. We’ve read your comments about the upcoming wipe and the availability of RP (roleplay) shards, and we want to address your concerns directly.

For this next wipe, we plan to open one shard per region. It is a change, but it’s a deliberate one: each shard will now support higher capacity, which allows us to gather more players in a single shard to enhance the gameplay experience.

That said, we may open additional shards if existing ones fill up, but we can’t promise when or if that will happen.

As for RP-specific shards, our original intent was to test whether the interest was strong enough to have some worlds specifically marked as RP. Based on what we’ve seen, we believe there is, so we’re likely to open RP shards at release.

We understand some of you are concerned about the potential for trolling or disruptive behavior on non-RP shards. Unfortunately, these issues can appear on any shard type. That said, we’ve also seen RP clans thriving on non-RP shards, and we’re confident many of you will continue to find ways to build meaningful, immersive experiences together.

As always, our Code of Conduct applies across all shards. If you encounter serious misconduct, please report it to our [url=https://support.playpaxdei.com/]Customer Support team[/url] so we can take action.

To help the RP community coordinate, we’re opening a [url=https://discord.com/channels/1071081786962088018/1368931099342016595]dedicated thread on Discord[/url] where RP clans and players can plan together, choose their region, province, and home valley, and regroup ahead of the wipe. We’re also sharing updated maps showing the revamped provinces to make that easier.

notes.title: Upcoming wipe - Clarifications
notes.content:
Hello Paxians,

As some of you have noticed in the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1995520/announcements/detail/524212840420082890]latest roadmap update[/url], quite a few changes to the world of Pax Dei have been announced for the upcoming Verse 3. This means that a wipe is also coming with Verse 3.
 
[h2]Why is there going to be a wipe?[/h2]
We are making substantial changes to the world, gear and crafting progression, along with combat skills for Verse 3, and we cannot deploy those changes without a wipe. This wipe is also a good opportunity to remove all inactive plots and “ghost towns”.

[h2]When will we know more about the actual coming changes?[/h2]
We are planning a series of spotlights that will be published in the weeks leading up to the release of Verse 3. Stay tuned for all the details!

[h2]What is being wiped?[/h2]
We are doing a very wide wipe, which means that:
[list]
[*] The world geography will change, and there will be more Heartlands (aka Home Valleys) per Province.
[*] Your placed plots will be removed.
[*] All your belongings on your plot and in your inventory will be removed.
[*] All the gear worn by your character will disappear.
[*] Clans will be wiped and will need to be recreated.
[*] All character combat skills will be reset.
[*] Crafting skills may be partially or fully reset. This is still being discussed, and we will provide more details as soon as possible.
[/list]
[b]Note: your Gold and Grace will not be reset.[/b]

As the world is changing, each shard will allow for more characters than they do now. As such, we will open one shard in each region, at first, and will continue to open more as these are filled up. Note that we won’t have an RP shard from the start, but might open one at a later stage. We will use the same shard names as before.

[h3]LIST PER REGION[/h3]
EU: Mimir
US: Apollo
SEA: Nuadu
 
[h2]What compensation do we get as players?[/h2]
We know a major wipe like this might make some players think twice about coming back and testing the newly added features and revamped world. As such, we plan to compensate you in several ways.
First of all, as per previous wipes, we will use the redeeming queue to compensate for the items you’ve accumulated in the game. Due to the extensive changes to the game economy in this update most, if not all, items will be converted into the resources from which they were crafted (assuming the resource still exists in the new economy). We aim to compensate for all types of items: 
[list]
[*] All furnishings that were on your plots.
[*] All components used to make building pieces and crafting stations that were placed on your plots.
[*] All items stored in containers placed on your plots.
[*] All processing crafters on your plots and the materials for each task. Only the materials placed in the crafters will be returned - the output will not be returned, even if the task is completed.
[*] All items in market stalls will be returned to sellers.
[/list]

Note: The compensation of all potential item types and conversion to materials is somewhat complicated. While this is our aim, we may need to make some adjustments as we build and test this. We will inform you of any changes to the compensation plan. Also, please note that we will not be able to fully compensate for materials used in items, weapons, equipment, resources, etc., as some will be removed from the game with this update.

[b]However, we will grant 100 Grace to all accounts once the content update is deployed.[/b] 

[h2]What will happen when Verse 3 is released and maintenance is over?[/h2]
Once the content update is fully deployed:
[list]
[*] The world will have changed, so you’ll need to find a new location for your plot(s). We’ll try to publish the updated maps as early as possible.
[*]  Your character will keep their name and appearance, but when logging in for the first time:
[*] They’ll be “naked” as if they were a newly created character.
[*] They won’t be part of a clan anymore.
[*] They’ll need to choose a new name if their initial name is already taken, as it will be on a first-come, first-served basis.
[*] All compensated materials will be available in your redeeming queue, except for items that have been removed from the game with this content update.
[*] You will need to recreate your clan and invite all members again.
[/list]
[h2]Since you’re not changing the shard structure, do you plan to open character transfers between shards of the same geographic region?[/h2]
Since only one shard will be opened per region at first, no character transfer will be offered. That might change when more shards are opened later on.

[h2]When will the wipe be confirmed?[/h2]
We will confirm the full details of the wipe at least one week before the content update is released.

[h2]When is Verse 3 expected?[/h2]
As mentioned in the roadmap, Verse 3 should go live this spring, so by the end of June. We cannot commit to an exact timeline right now as we are still finalizing the development of crucial features and changes. We do not want to announce a date only to have to move it later.

[h2]Is this the last wipe before release?[/h2]
The wipe accompanying Verse 3 should indeed be the last wipe before the “release” wipe. Note that this may change depending on the game's development.

[h2]What will happen at release?[/h2]
When Pax Dei is released out of Early Access, we’ll start with fresh new worlds and will perform a total database wipe. Everything will be deleted: plots, characters, and items; redeeming queues will be wiped, and Gold and Grace will be reset. At release, everyone, Founders and newcomers alike, will start their adventure in the world of Pax Dei from scratch.

We hope this clarifies the situation and answers the concerns some of you may have had regarding the upcoming content update. We will, of course, communicate a deployment date as soon as possible, so you can be fully prepared for when the wipe occurs and new content arrives.

Pax vobiscum,
The Mainframe Team

notes.title: Easter Surprise Patch - Patch Notes
notes.content:
[h2]Patch Notes[/h2]
[h3]New Miracle: Fast travel[/h3]
[list]
[*] New Miracle available, allowing you to travel across the land more quickly — for a price.
[*] Using this Miracle, you can teleport within a province directly from the Map. It consumes Grace to perform and offers a practical way to cut down on long travel times.
[*] Here’s how it works:
[list]
[*] Destinations must be discovered before you can travel to them.
[*] You can teleport to a Petra Dei (the large standing stone in Home Valley center) for 20 Grace points.
[*] You can teleport to a Gateway (portals to other Provinces) for 30 Grace points.
[*] Petra Mea (returning you to your Petra Dei) is still free with a cooldown, but now, you can spend Grace to bypass that cooldown.
[*] Teleporting to Lyonesse Gateways is also free on cooldown, but you can spend Grace to travel there when the free option is on cooldown.
[*] Travel between provinces is not yet available, but it may be in the future.
[/list][/list]
[h3]Localization[/h3]
[list]
[*] We’ve added two new languages, and you’re now able to play Pax Dei:
[list]
[*] in Spanish (Castilian) (es-ES)
[*] and in Polish (pl-PL).
[/list][/list]

While the game and the website will be available in those languages, we won’t add specific language sections on Discord for Spanish and Polish.

[h2]Known Issues[/h2]
[*] If the Player begins chopping or mining action during the Fast Travel animation, it is possible to trigger the Grace cost without being moved to the Petra Dei.
[*] The default home shrine does not appear on the map with a new character unless you go to Petra Dei to set it manually.
[*] Players can sometimes be re-notified that they have unlocked a location that has been previously unlocked.
[*] Gates are not unlocked immediately sometimes when arriving at a new province. The players need to walk closer to the gate to unlock it.
[*] When localization is set to Spanish or Polish, some individual text strings may still appear in English (for example, trees are not yet localized in PL).
