notes.title: Migration Update: Upgrading from Amazon RDS Postgres to Amazon Aurora
notes.content:
Hello Paxians,

We know some of you are eager to learn what’s happening on the backend. Today, we’d like to shed some light on the recent changes we made to our database, why we made the upgrade and the consequences for Pax Dei.

[h2]Overview[/h2]
To improve the reliability and scalability of our system, we recently migrated from our legacy Amazon RDS Postgres system to Amazon Aurora (Postgres compatible). This migration required us to schedule two maintenance breaks to make necessary database changes with a double goal.

[list]
[*] Enhanced Reliability:
[list]
[*] Our previous setup with Amazon RDS Postgres, which used a primary and a secondary node, offered a reliable setup where the secondary node can take over and be promoted to a master node in the case of a failure. This failover worked well but could result in several minutes of downtime during the switch.
[*] Aurora databases have a shared, reliable storage layer between all nodes, which 
significantly reduces recovery time from minutes to seconds by offering rapid failover from a primary to a secondary node.
[*] Aurora also allows us to dynamically add and remove additional nodes from the database cluster.
[/list]
[*] Improved Scalability:
[list]
[*] The old system required significant downtime to implement changes - as any major changes require us to use the failover mechanisms between nodes while performing upgrades or changes to each.
[*] Aurora provides the flexibility to scale resources up or down and adjust database node sizes with minimal disruption.
[/list]
[/list]
With the migration to Amazon Aurora now complete, we now have a better uptime and enhanced reliability with faster failover, as well as seamless scalability to support future growth. 

This migration positions us to better serve you, our community, by providing a more robust and flexible database infrastructure.

Stay tuned for more insights on Pax Dei development!
Pax vobiscum,
The Mainframe Team

notes.title: The Road Ahead – March Update
notes.content:
Hello Paxians,

Since the beginning of Early Access, Pax Dei has been a journey shaped by you — our passionate players. As we reflect on the progress we’ve made and the path ahead, we want to be transparent about the challenges we’ve faced, priorities we’ve had to adjust, and our ongoing commitment to building a game that thrives on meaningful player interactions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/8933d815aa4eb4f27e94477c58063d4b48f9ee23.jpg[/img]
[h2]Reflecting on Early Access[/h2]
The main goal for us moving into Early Access was to get constant feedback from a live community to help us develop the game. And wow, did the community deliver!

We’re grateful for, and humbled by, your continuous engagement. Over 70,000 of you are following Pax Dei’s development journey on our official Discord, and sharing tips and tricks daily to help other players.  

Looking at the different parts of the game, here is where we stand today. We spent the first months stabilizing the game. Then, our first update, [i][b]Proving Grounds[/b][/i], was about addressing some of the biggest challenges we saw emerging before we could focus on adding new systems to deepen the game with [i][b]Market Square[/b][/i] onwards.

We also had to make tough decisions. Some features we initially planned had to be deprioritized as we focused on strengthening the foundations of Pax Dei.

While this meant delays in some areas, like the highly expected PvP system or the Knight/Soldier feature, it has also allowed us to deploy some elements sooner than planned in the roadmap — and even to add new elements that will make Pax Dei stronger in the long run.

[h2]Early game [/h2]
The first obvious lesson from Early Access was that it took too long to get to the fun at the first contact with the game. Part of [i][b]Proving Grounds[/b][/i] was about addressing this: we placed enemy camps in the Heartland valleys and added basic gear and spells so that players now have the option to go on an adventure within the first few hours of play.

The introduction of the Journal, along with an overall balancing pass, also helped make the learning curve for crafting less steep.

And talking about adventure, the world revamp also included our first new biome since Alpha, the Corrupted Plains. More recently, the addition of the Compass makes finding your way around the world of Pax Dei more convenient.

We’re far from done with this aspect of the game and intend to keep iterating on it in upcoming content updates.

[h2]Combat[/h2]
Combat remains a major focus. In [i][b]Proving Grounds[/b][/i], we reworked the animation and player movement systems to improve the sec-to-sec combat experience, making it feel smoother and more responsive, while also laying a stronger foundation for future improvements.

We also added new spells, rebalanced gear, and gave the Inquisitors and Lost Souls a full rework.

In its current form, however, combat often lacks meaningful decision-making. We aim to move to a state where your gear choices and abilities will shape your tactics, encouraging you to build specialized roles.

This will be the central part of our next Verse. Check below for a sneak peek, and we look forward to sharing more soon.

[h2]Building[/h2]
Building is undoubtedly the most complete system in the game. We’re amazed at how it unlocks the creativity of the community. Watching the world fill up with beautiful villages, mighty fortresses, and sprawling cities is a constant joy.

We’ve been regularly adding new pieces to the game and plan on expanding the building sets to give even more options to our master builders. Yes, the highly expected Limestone should be part of Verse 3!

That said, the free-form nature of our building system comes with a number of challenges, notably on the performance side.The valleys with the most spectacular creations tend to be the hardest on framerate.

We’ve already rolled out a number of performance improvements — it was one of the underlying reasons for our recent shift to Unreal Engine 5.4 — and more are in the works.

Finally, we still have to tackle the “ghost town” syndrome, when the world gradually fills up with the homes of inactive players. Work on a more robust system to clean up plots of inactive players has started — more details will come soon.

[h2]Building Bridges Between Players[/h2]
At the heart of any MMO lies one simple truth: connection fuels the experience. That’s why Pax Dei was among the first games to integrate the new [url=https://discord.com/developers/social-sdk]Discord Social SDK[/url]—bringing seamless text chat, friends lists, voice chat, and more into the game.

Our goal is to make it easier for players to communicate, coordinate, and share adventures—whether they're crafting in a village or battling side-by-side.

And because connection also means speaking your language, Pax Dei is now available in German and French, with Polish and Spanish coming soon.

[h2]Closing the loop[/h2]
As a player-driven Social Sandbox MMO, the heart of Pax Dei is very much its economy, thriving not through scripted content but by fostering meaningful social interactions, trade, and competition.

If we take a bird’s eye view, Pax Dei relies on one core engagement loop: Harvest, Create, Destroy — a cycle that empowers players to shape the world of Pax Dei.

Harvest covers actions like cutting wood, mining, hunting, and ‘farming’ PVE enemies for gold and loot. Create encompasses crafting and building systems. While much work remains, these two parts of the loop are now firmly in place.

For the game economy to become self-sustaining on a larger scale—to truly close the loop—we now need to offer players meaningful ways to spend what they earn.

In other words, there must be systems that allow value to be removed from the economy, balancing what’s gained through harvesting and crafting.

By “value,” we mean your gear, gold, and Grace. Don’t worry—your plots remain safe and will continue to be protected under the Pax Dei.

From that perspective, [i][b]Market Square[/b][/i] added two crucial components to the game.

[list]
[*] Market Stalls and the Gold economy allow player-to-player trading, which opens ways for players to specialize. If you prefer playing a crafter rather than a fighter, you now have a way to get the components you need from other players — by selling them the equipment they require for the part of the game they prefer to engage with.
[*] By spending Grace, players can now access effects that will help them progress in the game. We’ve only added a few spells for now, and more are coming. This is one part of the game where we want to give players ample opportunities to feel good about spending some of the value they have accumulated.
[/list]
Balancing the in-game economy will require more work, not only to make it more profound and more rewarding, but also to ensure it's sustainable long term. It’s the reason we will be focusing more on this part of the game loop in the coming months.

[h2]What’s Next[/h2]
Our next major update, Verse 3 - name still to be decided, will mark a significant step forward for Pax Dei. With it, you’ll experience a world that feels more rewarding and more strategic.

We’re making some changes to the combat system by adding several new spells and new characteristics to gear. We are adding a new weapon type, staves, which will be dedicated to healing spells.

Additionally, all melee weapons will have three distinct abilities to further differentiate their playstyles. These additions aim to create a more dynamic combat experience, deepen the interplay between roles, and offer more tactical options.

Whether you prefer the brute force of melee, the steadfastness of a tank, or the supportive role of a healer, you'll find more ways to customize your build.

Naturally, these combat updates will impact the crafting system, particularly Tailoring, Leatherworking, and Blacksmithing. We’re refining onboarding, dependencies, and progression pacing.

We aim to simplify the early game with more intuitive crafting chains, meaningful low-tier items, easier access to spells, and reduced cross-profession dependencies in the first levels.

We’re also adjusting the balance to emphasize gathering over extended crafting sessions.

Another major component of Verse 3 is a world revamp. We aim to increase player density and interaction by adding more Heartlands per Province and slightly reducing the overall size of the Wildlands. While resource locations will shift, biome gathering rules will remain consistent.

Additionally, a new Fast Travel Miracle will be introduced, reshaping how players traverse the world and improving the global economy.

The revamped world will also feature improved starting areas: Petra Dei will offer limited storage for all players and include pre-placed, entry-level public crafting stations, making the onboarding experience smoother and more accessible to newcomers.

[h2]Looking Further Ahead[/h2]
Later this year, we’ll be expanding PvP in meaningful ways. PvP will play a key role in keeping Pax Dei’s economy vibrant and dynamic. Central to this evolution is a reimagined Lyonesse—a larger, high-stakes PvP zone where risk and reward go hand in hand.

Players will battle for control of valuable, exclusive resources, but success won’t come easily.

Coordination, strategy, and bold action will be essential to claim key locations, like what we currently call the Trade Towns.

We’re also planning to introduce new customization options, including a cloth dye system that gives crafters greater creative freedom.

Alongside this, expect quality-of-life improvements—and, if all goes well, mounts may finally make their way into the game.

[h2]Transitioning Beyond Early Access[/h2]
Pax Dei is a live, evolving world — we will continue to deliver meaningful updates as we expand the game.

To sustain this, we’ll soon share more details on our monetization plans designed to support server costs while ensuring fair value for players.

We sincerely appreciate your ongoing support, and we remain committed to delivering an experience that empowers you to shape your own adventures in Pax Dei.

Thank you for being part of this incredible journey — we can’t wait to see what stories you create next.

Pax vobiscum,
The Mainframe Team

notes.title: Plot Cleaning & New EU Shard on March 14
notes.content:
[h2]Hello Paxians,[/h2]

On Friday, March 14, at 9 a.m. UTC, we’ll perform a plot cleaning session on all shards to remove inactive plots.

Here are the five criteria a plot must fulfill to be considered inactive - all requirements must be met:
[list]
[*] Player inactivity: The player who owns the plot has not logged in on any of their characters in the past 28 days (on the cleanup day).
[*] Building Pieces: The plot contains fewer than 20 building pieces.
[*] Chests: The plot has fewer than 7 chests.
[*] Crafters: The plot has fewer than 7 crafters.
[*] Market Stalls: The plot has no Market Stall.
[/list]
Please note that we are still investigating the implementation of an automated process to clean inactive plots more regularly. However, starting Monday, March 17, we will perform a plot cleaning session every Monday at 9 a.m. UTC, using the same criteria mentioned above. 

[h2]New EU shard: Chernobog[/h2]

As mentioned, we closely monitor the population on all Pax Dei shards. The EU shards are becoming increasingly full, making it difficult for newcomers to find free spots to settle and start playing.

As such, we have decided to open one new shard for the EU region on Friday, March 14, following the plot-cleaning session. It will be named [b]Chernobog[/b], after a deity from Slavic myths..

Note that you might need to restart the game once the shard has been opened to see the newly added shards on Friday. 

We will temporarily open[b] character transfers from existing EU shards[/b] to the new shard [b]until March 31 [/b].

[h2]FAQ[/h2]

[h3]Is the new shard RP (Roleplay)?[/h3]
No, the new shard is a standard one. It is not flagged as RP.

[h3]When I create a character on the new shard, will I get access to my redeeming queue?[/h3]
If you already have a redeeming queue with your other characters and create a new character on a new shard in the same region, you’ll have access to the same redeeming queue.

[h3]Can I transfer an existing character to the new shard?[/h3]
As we do not yet have a self-service character transfer, we will temporarily offer character transfer via our Customer Support team. Note, however:
[list] [*] You cannot transfer your character if
[list] [*] You have a placed plot,
[*] You are part of a clan,
[*] You are in a party.
[/list] [/list]
Please release your plot and leave your clan and any parties you’re in before contacting our Support Team. 

[list]
[*] Only the items that are in your character’s inventory will be transferred to the new shard:
[list]
[*] The gear your character wears and the items in their inventory will be carried over.
[*] The skill levels reached by your character will also remain.
[*] BUT: all the items and material left on a plot you release will not be carried over, will not be added to the redeeming queue, and will be up for grabs publicly as soon as the plot is released. Make sure to add any precious items you’d like to carry over to your character’s inventory so as not to lose them. 
[/list]
[*] If the character name is already taken, your character will need to be renamed. 
[*] You can only transfer to a shard from the same region (EU to EU, in this case).
[*] We will only offer transfers until March 31.
[list]
[*] If the population levels of the destination shard reach their limit sooner than the date mentioned above, we will stop offering character transfers to them. 
[/list][/list]
Please note that transfers will only be offered to characters on existing shards and will not be offered to characters created or already moved to the new shards.

If you wish to have your character transferred to one of the new shards in the same region, please contact our Support team directly: https://support.playpaxdei.com/hc/ 

Please note that this is a manual process, and delays may arise when processing your request.

Thank you for your patience and understanding.
Pax vobiscum,
The Mainframe Team

[*] Sorting by Durability in a Market Stall will display non-durable items alongside durable ones. This does not occur with Heartland Markets.
[*] The Market Stall waypoint can only be removed by logging out of the game.
[*] Canceling or buying an order breaks the sorting option in the Market Stall for all the players looking at the given Market Stall. You must either close the Market window and reopen it or change the sorting option to a different one and back.
[*] The Market list does not show the Tier tips on the icons. You must select an order to show the item's Tier.
[*] In Heartland Markets, when filtering orders, the text "Filters active, showing X of Y orders" always displays the number of orders on the current page for both X and Y instead of showing the number of filtered orders and the total number of orders.
[*] Sticky Selection: The player can use key binds on the last selected item in the market stall even after reopening it
[*] After canceling a sale, the [E] key on the keyboard can become unresponsive in Market Stall and storage interfaces.
[*] When opening the Market UI from the Main Menu when outside a Heartland where there are no market orders to browse, (for example in the Wilds or in Dungeons) the UI instructs you to select an item in the inventory and click the [Create Sale] button to create a sale order even if its not possible and can only be done at a Market Stall.
[*] Sort by name is currently (and temporarily) not available in market stalls.
[*] When browsing market orders remotely (by using Markets from the Main Menu), sorting by name or using text search is temporarily not available. In the meantime you can use all other sorting and filtering options to narrow down your search.
[/list]

[h3]Chat / Voice chat[/h3]

[list]
[*] In most situations, the chat doesn't open after pressing "Enter" when the Building menu is already open.
[*] When a player is in both a Clan and a Party, if they join one of the Voice Chat channels (Party or Clan) and then click "Join other Voice Chat" to switch to the other Voice Chat channel but cancel or dismiss the confirmation box, the "Join other Voice Chat" option will become greyed out and unusable. This issue can be resolved by leaving the party and rejoining it.
[*] Leaving any Voice Chat channel after canceling the "Join other Voice Chat" action with the ESC key will move the player to the canceled channel. This does not occur when clicking the Cancel button instead of using the ESC key.
[*] The "Push to talk" setting is only accessible from the Voice Chat settings, while it should also be in the general settings menu. The same issue applies to the volume settings of the voice chat.
[*] If a window is opened before the Chat window, it does not accept keybind inputs. 
[*] F5 doesn't hide the Chat bubble above your character.
[/list]

[h3]Miscellaneous[/h3]

[list]
[*] Characters lobby: the Discord hyperlink in the Maintenance message is broken, leading to a ‘no text channel.’
[*] Demonic trees have the [E] Felling option but should not, as they are not choppable.
[*] Emotes are not functional while the Construction Hammer is equipped.
[*] Furnishings and Crafters can be placed in the air.
[*] Integrity Issue: Construction elements can extend infinitely over water without proper support. This can lead to building destruction when it is fixed.
[*] Some Gates to other provinces are not displayed on the Compass.
[/list]

notes.title: Market Square Part 3 Arrives on March 13
notes.content:
Hello Paxians,

Get ready for an exciting new chapter - Market Square Part 3 is dropping on March 13! 
We’ll be performing maintenance starting at 10:30 am UTC, with an estimated downtime of 1 hour. 
Along with the features we’ve already revealed in the recent spotlights, we’re adding a bunch of extra content, mainly quality-of-life improvements, to make your Pax Dei experience even better. Full patch notes will be available on maintenance day, but here’s a sneak peek at what’s coming.

[h2]Market Square Part 3 - Release Notes[/h2]
[h3]The Compass[/h3]
We’ll be introducing the in-game Compass! This handy tool will help you navigate Pax Dei, showing cardinal directions, nearby points of interest, and even your custom markers. Prefer to explore without it? No problem - you can toggle it off in the settings.

All details are on our dedicated spotlight.

[previewyoutube=yIOolirni9s;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Building changes[/h3]
As already mentioned, some important changes are coming to the building system, along with a bunch of new pieces - more details in the spotlight.

[h3]Discord - Voice Chat[/h3]
Communication will get a major upgrade! Party and Clan voice chat will now be integrated directly through Discord, making it easier than ever to coordinate with your allies. Just open your chat menu and jump into the new voice chat lobby!

But that’s not all—chat bubbles are back! Now, messages sent in Nearby, Party, and Clan chat will appear above your character, making in-game interactions more lively and immersive.

More info on our dedicated spotlight.

[previewyoutube=o3_hHYmJowE;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Markets updates[/h3]
Heartland browsing: You will now be able to browse through all the market stalls in your Home Valley from one menu! Open the ‘Tab’ menu, press Tab or I, and click on the Market tab at the top. Find what you need and press [View Location] to see the location on the map. You can even set a waypoint, which will appear on your map and compass.

Better Search & Sorting: We’ll be adding filters and sorting to make finding items easier! You can now sort by price, quantity, lifetime and more, on both local stalls and the Heartland Market. In the Heartland market, you can also sort by distance. This feature will be refined in the following updates.
New Market Stall Variant: Pimp your markets! A new market stall variant will be available, giving you two designs to choose from.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/8dc95f2da667b359ca3e3b3f2d353c4276700d69.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/fe1f4b2120eadf4f4cc37e758b5ab4a6db63b03f.png[/img]

[h3]New emotes[/h3]
Ready to show off some moves? New emotes are coming! Your character can now salute, cheer, and even dance! Plus, sitting animations have been added, and special emotes can even be performed while seated.

We’ll let you discover the full list of possibilities on your own once the patch is released - just press B and have fun! We can’t wait to see your best screenshots and videos featuring the new animations!

[previewyoutube=RweKrYq7J0M;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Resource Gathering Changes[/h3]
Gathering wood and ore is about to get smoother than ever! A new interact UI will now appear when approaching tool-required nodes (like trees and ore deposits), showing the node’s name, description, required tool, and hardness level. If you have a valid tool in your inventory, pressing interact will automatically equip it, gather the resource, and switch back to your previous equipment when done. No more manual tool-swapping - just gather and go!

[h3]Unreal Engine 5.4[/h3]
In this content update, we will update our Unreal Engine to version 5.4., following our principle of using the latest and most outstanding features of Unreal Engine for the best possible visual fidelity and performance.

We’re super excited to hear your thoughts on all these updates! [url=https://discord.com/channels/1071081786962088018/1349003921275879467]Share your feedback on Discord[/url], and as always...

notes.title: Pax Dei - Answers to pressing questions
notes.content:
Hello Paxians,

Today we're going to answer some of the questions we've seen come up most often on Discord and other platforms. You might find some answers too vague or not to your liking — and that’s part of the game. Our teams are hard at work developing key features and systems, and there are quite a few details we can’t share at the moment. Thank you for your patience and continued support!

[h2]Content & Features[/h2]
[h3]Will you add a new province?[/h3]
Not in the near future, but we have plenty of designs for new regions and landscapes! While it's not coming too soon, the possibilities for expansion are definitely on our minds. 

[h3]When will you be adding new in-game emotes?[/h3]
Great news—new emotes are coming in the next content update! We know many of you are eager for more interactions like sitting on chairs or lying on beds, and we’re actively working on making that happen. In fact, we’re even working on dedicated emotes the character is seated! There’s still some work left to ensure everything functions smoothly, but stay tuned!

[h3]When will we get more lore content?[/h3]
We're developing a system to bring more lore and mysteries to the world of Pax Dei, and while we can't share details just yet, we think you'll love what’s coming!

[h3]When will you add fishing? Will you add farming?[/h3]
While we don’t have an exact timeline yet, they are features we absolutely want to bring into the game. For now, we’re focusing on bigger core systems—but your future homestead and fishing adventures are definitely in the works!

[h3]Will you run in-game events after release?[/h3]
Pax Dei is a true sandbox, and we’re already amazed by the creativity of our community! Clans are organizing races, archery contests, treasure hunts, and more. We focus on giving you the tools to create meaningful events rather than implementing time-limited ones that might not suit everyone. Keep the creativity coming—we can’t wait to see what you come up with! 

[h3]Will the previous forest ambiance come back?[/h3]
Absolutely! As we’ve mentioned before, the forests will return. But as any good forester knows… trees take time to grow!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/860c8c6687645206a08a234800728e800ce8ce44.jpg[/img]
[h2]Gameplay & Mechanics[/h2]
[h3]When are you adding fast travel?[/h3]
Fast travel is coming as part of the next set of Miracles! We don’t have an ETA yet, but it’s coming.
 
[h3]Where do you stand on mounts?[/h3]
We’ve been testing some prototypes, but they’re not yet at the level of quality we want for Pax Dei. The work-in-progress model you’ll see in the screenshots below might look “nearly done,” but in reality, it’s still far from final.

While animations, horse rigs, and models are coming along relatively well, the real challenge lies in fully integrating mounts into the world. Ensuring that horses move and behave naturally within the environment and that zone transitions are smooth, etc., is a complex process—and there’s still a lot of work ahead.

That said, our team will keep working on them, so stay tuned for more updates!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/11cb393d610509f7be0e6ee5d94ef448ac1355b3.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/caee3943d7ea4a7351d8ee40aa616ead6d60ca29.jpg[/img]
[h3]When will the option to dye clothes be available?[/h3]
We have a working prototype and a solid selection of colours and embroidery patterns, but before introducing the full system, we need to ensure the foundations of crafting and the economy are solid. Once those systems are in place, we’ll be able to move forward with the dyes!

[h3]Are higher stack sizes (100/200) for items planned?[/h3]
We’re making some adjustments behind the scenes, but we can’t share details just yet. Stay tuned!

[h2]Building & Housing[/h2]
[h3]When will you fix trees growing through foundations?[/h3]
We hear you! This issue has some deep roots (bad pun intended), and it’s taking longer to resolve than we initially expected. But we’re on it!

[h3]When will you fix the hole in the center when combining four plots?[/h3]
We’re actively working on a solution! No ETA yet, but we know it’s an issue, and we’re making progress.

[h3]Will you improve the permission feature and allow for more control?[/h3]
Yes! We do plan to improve the permission system, but we don’t have a timeline to share just yet.

[h3]When will the new building pieces be added?[/h3]
Exciting news! The stone set we teased last year should be included in the next major content update—if we’re happy with its level of polish. In the meantime, the upcoming minor update will bring new foundation pieces, including roundish ones! We know you’re eager for more building options, and we appreciate your patience as we make sure they’re just right.

[h3]When is recycling coming?[/h3] 
It’s still in development, and we hope to introduce it in one of the next major content updates!

[h3]Do you plan on adding a way to move everything in a plot at once (such as putting everything on a plot in the redeeming queue)?[/h3]
This is something we’d love to add in the future, especially for players transferring to another shard. No timeline yet, but we understand well how valuable this would be!

[h3]Can you add the ability to move storage/furniture around in our plots while they’re full, instead of emptying and destroying them?[/h3]
Right now, this isn’t in our plans, but we’re always open to feedback and ideas!

[h2]Crafting & Economy[/h2]
[h3]When will new cooking recipes be added (for example, a "Yule Log" during Christmas)?[/h3]
More recipes will be coming as the game evolves, and seasonal/event-specific recipes are something we’d love to include! Adding a recipe is more complex than it seems (ingredients, icons, models, balancing, etc.), but we’re definitely thinking about it.

[h3]Will you bring back Apple Trees, Plum Trees, etc.?[/h3]
Yes! They’ll be making a comeback in the future.

[h3]Will you add the ability to craft using items in storage?[/h3]
This isn’t in our plans at the moment, but we’ll keep listening to your feedback!

[h2]Technical & Performance[/h2]
[h3]Will you add DLSS 4 native support to Pax Dei? When will FSR3 return?[/h3]
DLSS 4 isn’t on our immediate roadmap, as we’re focused on general performance and stability improvements. We do plan to bring back FSR3 if we can fix the crashes some players were experiencing.

[h3]When will you upgrade to UE 5.4, and how will it help?[/h3]
The next update will include the UE 5.4 upgrade. This is mostly an internal update that allows us to keep offering players the best visual fidelity and performance Unreal can provide. The practical differences from UE 5.3 will be small.

[h3]Will you upgrade to UE 5.5 afterwards?[/h3]
Once we’ve successfully shipped the UE 5.4 update, we’ll start looking at 5.5 for future improvements.

[h2]Game Progress & Development Timeline[/h2]
[h3]You mentioned Early Access would last a minimum of one year. Are you on track with your initial development plans?[/h3]
We’ve hit some delays with certain features, but we’re confident that we should be able to release Pax Dei this year!

[h3]How many wipes will there be in Early Access?[/h3]
A full wipe will happen before release so that everyone can start fresh. We may do an additional world/character wipe before that, but we’re carefully considering how to make it as smooth as possible.

[h3]When will we know more about monetization?[/h3]
We’re finalizing some systems, and once everything is set, we’ll share the details with you! What we can state once more is that if you’ve already purchased a Founder’s Pack during Early Access, you won’t be charged again when the game transitions out of Early Access.

For more details, you can visit [url=https://playpaxdei.com/en-us/faq/purchase ]our complete FAQ on the website[/url].

[h3]Are more languages coming soon?[/h3]
We’re excited to confirm that we’ll be adding two new languages in an upcoming content update: you’ll soon be able to play Pax Dei in Spanish (Castilian) and Polish. Note that while the game and the website will be available in those languages, we won’t be able to add specific language sections on Discord for Spanish and Polish, as we currently do not have the bandwidth to moderate and engage in these two languages.

We know many other communities would also like the game localized in their language. While we can’t promise which languages will be added in the future or when, rest assured that we are looking into it. Even though Pax Dei doesn’t have quests or dialogue to translate, adding a new language is still quite a lot of work, and we won’t be able to add all languages at once.

Stay tuned for more details on the upcoming minor and major content updates!

Pax vobiscum,
The Mainframe Team

notes.title: Plot Cleaning Session on February 27
notes.content:
Hello Paxians,

On Thursday, February 27, we’ll perform a plot cleaning session on all shards, in order to remove inactive plots.

This will happen during a maintenance, which will start at 10 am UTC and is planned to last about one hour. 

Here are the five criteria a plot must fulfill to be considered inactive - all criteria must be met:
[list]
[*] [b]Player inactivity[/b]: The player who owns the plot has not logged in any of their characters in the past 28 days (on the day of the maintenance).
[*] [b]Building Pieces[/b]: The plot contains fewer than 20 building pieces.
[*] [b]Chests[/b]: The plot has fewer than 7 chests.
[*] [b]Crafters[/b]: The plot has fewer than 7 crafters.
[*] [b]Market Stalls[/b]: The plot has no Market Stall on it.
[/list]
While these thresholds are set conservatively, this cleanup should help free up a significant number of plots across all shards. However, please note that the effect may not be very noticeable in some of the most popular and, per se, overcrowded areas.

Please note that we are looking into implementing an automated process in order to clean inactive plots on a more regular basis. We will keep you informed on that topic as soon as possible.

Pax vobiscum,
The Mainframe Team

notes.title: Spotlight - Upcoming Building Changes
notes.content:
Hello Paxians,

Last week’s announcement about upcoming building changes led to a lot of questions from the community. Many of you wanted more information on the reasons behind these changes and what they might mean for building and crafting in the future.

Let’s do a deep dive into the upcoming changes with answers to all (or almost all) your questions.

[h2]Why make changes?[/h2]

Building in Pax Dei is about creativity and expression, but some inconsistencies in material costs have made certain choices feel less intuitive. We want players to design their structures based on aesthetics rather than minor differences in resource costs. Additionally, we’ve found that some crafting recipes were more complicated than necessary, slowing down the building process.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/a4cacf9d2ed42071a28cb906e59687e4b452c720.png[/img]
Our goal with these changes is twofold:
[olist]
[*] Consistency –  Comparable building pieces should have uniform costs, ensuring that your taste and aesthetics drive your choices more than the cost constraints. We also unified the unlock levels of the sets.
[list]
[*] Note that some pieces have moved level, such as half-timber railings, which have been moved from level 16 to 30. They have been unified into the building sets more accurately.
[*] New floor pieces have been added to all sets, and the old half-timber floors have been moved to level 30.
[/list]
[*]Simplification – Reducing the variety of materials required for each piece will enhance crafting accessibility while maintaining depth and variety.
[/olist]
We understand that some of you may worry these changes will make the game feel "too simple," but we want to reassure you that this is not our intention, nor is it the future of Pax Dei. As stated above, our goal is to make Pax Dei more accessible to newcomers while maintaining long-term challenges.
For the next content update, we are adjusting the building system and will continue refining other systems as needed. We are always reviewing balance and player feedback to ensure that crafting, building, and the overall game experience remain engaging and rewarding.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/cbbb46aba8b74e0e9875c3187daf43344100bf6f.png[/img]
[h2]What’s changing?[/h2]
In the upcoming content update - Market Square Part 3 - we’re making the following adjustments:
Wall and roof costs:

[list]
[*] Walls and walls with windows will now cost the same, letting players choose based on looks rather than a small price difference.
[*] Roof pieces and roof with windows pieces will also cost the same, following the same logic.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/608ed97f1f92d1586afc04f1246120191b5a7d29.png[/img]
[list]
[*] Triangular pieces adjustments:
[list]
[*] Triangular walls will now cost approximately half of a regular wall, rounded up to the nearest whole number. For example if a regular wall costs 25, a triangular wall will cost 13 (12.5 rounded up).
[*] Triangular foundations will cost exactly half of a full foundation.
[/list]
[*] Crafting recipe streamlining:
[list]
[*] Wooden pegs are being removed as building materials as they were an extra step in construction and didn’t add much value. Once the content update is released, pegs that were used for building pieces will not be refunded on destruction. We know you’re sad not to be able to use them anymore for building, but as they won’t be removed from your inventories, you can still keep the ones you have in your storage for the future recycling feature (no ETA on this one yet though). 
[*] Each building piece will now require only two types of materials (in varying amounts) among the vast selection of materials available for building, simplifying the crafting process without taking away from the experience of crafting and building.
[/list]
[*] Clay node adjustments:
[list]
[*]  The number of Clay nodes is being reduced by half, but each node will now yield twice as much Clay—so the overall resource gain remains the same but with fewer interactions required.
[/list]
[*]New pieces:
[list]
[*]We’re completing existing sets (foundation, hut, cottage, half-timber), particularly with new beams and floors.
[/list]
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43726614/b96ad8f07b0c8be12a7feaf8364babf5350d9012.png[/img]
[h2]What does that mean for me as a player?[/h2]

These changes mean a more intuitive and faster building experience. You’ll spend less time managing excessive materials and more time focusing on designing your dream structure.

The simplification of material requirements still means you’ll need to find and process resources, but it removes extra steps that added little to the overall experience, making it easier for both new and experienced players to build efficiently.

For example, a regular wall and a windowed wall now cost the same, so you can choose what you want based on style. Fewer crafting materials per piece also mean less back-and-forth to storage, letting you focus more on building.

[h2]Will other changes be made to crafting or resources?[/h2]

Yes! While the upcoming content update brings these refinements, we’re also working on new building pieces to complement existing sets like cottages, huts, and half-timber structures. 

Additionally, Limestone, Ornamental, and Log set pieces are planned for the next major content update (aka Verse 3), so more customization options are coming.

We look forward to your thoughts and feedback on the upcoming changes to building in this Discord [url=https://discord.com/channels/1071081786962088018/1339582027200204840]dedicated thread[/url].

As stated already, this is still a work in progress, so a few changes might occur before the next content patch is deployed to the live shards. Keep an eye out for more spotlights coming in soon. 

Pax vobiscum,
The Mainframe Team

notes.title: Medieval MMORPG Pax Dei gets new blessing system, starting with professions
notes.content:
There's something unquestionably appealing about the premise of Pax Dei. The medieval MMORPG is pitched as a social sandbox, bearing as many points in common with the likes of Rust and Ark as with more traditional MMOs. To make that process even slicker, a new update introduces a way to gain powerful blessings to help enhance your gathering and crafting abilities.

notes.title: Market Square Part 2 - Patch Notes
notes.content:
[h2]New features[/h2]

[h3]Grace: Essence of the Divine’s power[/h3]
[list]
[*] Grace is an ethereal currency central to player progression, rewards, and social systems in Pax Dei. It symbolizes the Divine's power, enabling you to perform miracles for yourself or those you care about.
[/list]
[b]How to Acquire Grace[/b]
[list]
[*] Daily Login: Receive a small amount of Grace for free each day just by logging in.
[*] Gold Exchange: Spend gold to acquire additional Grace. However, the cost increases progressively—the more Grace you buy in a single day, the more expensive each point becomes. This scaling resets every 24 hours (real-time).
[/list]
[b]How Grace Works[/b]
[list]
[*] Once obtained, Grace can be spent to perform miracles that provide powerful abilities, bonuses, or practical utilities. There’s no limit to how much Grace you can accrue, and your total Grace pool is shared across all your characters within the same server region (EU, US, or AP).
[*] You can track your current Grace balance in the Grace menu and unlock its potential to shape your journey in Pax Dei.
[*] Grace will be developed and become more prominent with future patches.
[/list]
[h3]Miracles: Unlocking Divine Powers[/h3]

Miracles are powerful and thematic abilities designed to enhance your experience in Pax Dei. Whether you're focused on exploration, crafting, combat, or socializing, there’s a Miracle for every playstyle and level of wealth. They allow you to perform supernatural feats, receive divine blessings, and harness extraordinary powers to shape your journey.

[b]Costs and Accessibility[/b]
[list]
[*] Most Miracles require Grace to cast, though some are free. Notably, familiar abilities like the home Teleport and corpse-summoning miracles (previously in the utility menu, T) are now integrated into the new Miracle menu and remain free of Grace cost.
[*] You can access the Miracle menu by pressing T.
[/list]
[b]Introducing New Miracles[/b]
[list]
[*] The first wave of new Miracles in this patch focuses on boosting your gathering and crafting efficiency.
[*] These essential blessings are automatically granted to all players.
[*] Additional Miracles will be introduced over time, many of which will require exploration and progression to unlock.
[/list]
[h3]New Miracles: Gathering and Profession Blessings[/h3]

[b]Gathering Blessings[/b]

Gathering blessings increase the efficiency of specific resource-gathering activities, offering bonus yields when active. These blessings have a duration of 1 hour and can be refreshed by recasting the same Miracle. Different gathering blessings can be used simultaneously.
[list]
[*] Bountiful Harvest: Increases yield from gathering plants, mushrooms, and other gathering nodes.
[*] Prospector’s Blessing: Boosts yield from mining nodes.
[*] Nature’s Favor: Enhances yield from tree chopping.
[*] Hunter’s Favor: Improves yield from skinning (e.g., hide drops).
[/list]
[b]Profession Blessings[/b]

Profession blessings temporarily enhance crafting skills, increasing the success rate of crafting tasks and, in turn, accelerating XP gains. These blessings do not impact XP rewards directly or unlock recipes, as the base skill is used for those purposes.
[list]
[*] Different profession blessings can be active at the same time.
[*] If two blessings boost the same skill, only the strongest buff applies (e.g., Armorer’s and Weapon Smith’s blessings both buff Blacksmithing but won’t stack).
[/list]
These blessings also have a duration of 1 hour and can be refreshed by recasting the same Miracle.
[list]
[*] Alchemist’s Blessing: +1 Alchemy.
[*] Baker’s Blessing: +1 Baking.
[*] Carpenter’s Blessing: +1 Carpentry.
[*] Cook’s Blessing: +1 Cooking and Charcuterie.
[*] Jeweler’s Blessing: +1 Jewelry Making.
[*] Tailor’s Blessing: +1 Tailoring.
[*] Winemaker’s Blessing: +1 Winemaking and Brewing.
[*] Armorer’s Blessing: +1 Armor Smithing and Blacksmithing.
[*] Weapon Smith’s Blessing: +1 Weapon Smithing and Blacksmithing.
[*] Hunter’s Blessing: +1 Leatherworking and Fletching.
[/list]
[b]Future Plans[/b]

In the future, higher-tier versions of these blessings will be introduced. These upgraded Miracles will offer greater benefits, come at a higher Grace cost, and may require unlocking through exploration and progression. We also plan to introduce other types of Miracles, such as ones that facilitate traveling.
Miracles are just the beginning of what Pax Dei has in store—let the Divine guide you on your path!

[h2]Changes and fixes[/h2]

[h3]Markets[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where the details panel would not refresh after purchasing an item. 
[*] Fixed an issue that would cause items to be dropped if the user attempted to drag and drop an item stack onto the Market Stall UI.
[*] Fixed an issue where the "Market at Full Capacity" message was shown erroneously.
[*] Fixed a crash that could occur when dismantling a Market Stall while the markets tutorial popup is open.
[*] Hovering over an empty inventory slot no longer shows the selected Market Stall item in the details panel.
[*] An Esc button prompt was added to the Market Stall tutorial screen.
[*] Fixed an issue where it was possible to trigger a purchase without sufficient Gold, which resulted in an error pop-up with missing text.
[*] Fixed an issue that prevented the Inventory backpack icon from updating when creating sell orders.
[*] The original slot now remains selected when moving an item from one inventory slot to another.
[*] The Market Stall's settings button now has a corresponding button prompt.
[*] Fixed an issue where various Market Stall pop-up windows were missing button prompts.
[*] The Sell button is now correctly greyed out when the market stall is at capacity.
[*] Fixed an issue that made closing market error message popups challenging to close in some cases.
[*] Button prompts for scrolling up or down have been changed from text to icons. 
[/list]

[h3]Gear & Crafting & Resources[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue with a colorless gemstone centerpiece within a coronet.
[*] Fixed a material and mesh issue on the mantle.
[*] Fixed a performance issue when dragging items in inventory.
[*] Fixed an issue where entering the crafting menu would cause a hitch.
[/list]

[h3]Building[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed performance issues on various flower and plant assets
[*] Fixed an issue that erroneously caused unsupported building elements to highlight green.
[/list]

[h3]Combat & World Interactions[/h3]
[list]
[*] World interactions are now better prioritized based on proximity to the aim location. 
[*] Fixed an issue where the Hurt II proc chance was incorrect.
[*] Fixed an issue preventing the use of the items in the hot bar while the inventory was opened.
[*] The transition animation when falling now appears more natural.
[*] Fixed an issue where resource harvesting would sometimes continue when switching between tools.
[*] Updated the animation that plays when teleporting to a Petra Dei.
[*] Fixed various PvE sites to prevent NPCs from spawning in unintended locations.
[/list]

[h3]Chat[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue that sometimes prevented chat messages from fading out automatically.
[*] The General Chat feed now defaults to Zone Chat when joining the game.
[*] Fixed an issue where some localized strings might not fit properly in the chat UI.
[*] Fixed an issue where a player's own messages were not indented properly.
[*] Fixed an issue that could cause the chat text field to not be focused when spamming the feed buttons.
[*] Fixed an issue that could cause the first chat message to appear or not appear erroneously.
[*] Social system messages will now show only in their relevant chat channels.
[*] Added the character's portrait, character name, and Discord account name to the chat settings.
[*] Party invites no longer require the party to already exist.
[/list]

[h3]UI fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added the keybind for name randomization to the character creation name selection screen [R]. 
[*] Fixed word wrapping on storage headers. 
[*] Fixed an issue where the ESC button label was tiny in some UI elements. 
[*] Fixed an issue where the build reticle would remain after death. 
[*] Fixed an issue that caused the 'Offset' Construction tooltip keybind to not show correctly.
[/list]

[h3]Localization[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added various missing localization strings.
[*] Fixed and modified various texts in English, French, and German.
[/list]

[h2]Known Issues[/h2]

[h3]Grace[/h3]
[list]
[*] After validation, players can still change the Grace for Gold amount during the animation. There is no exploit here. The final amounts for both Grace and Gold are the ones considered.
[*] Opening the Miracles' wheel should not prevent world interactions. 
[*] Grace for Gold action can be performed while falling - there is no miracle to prevent the fall damage.
[*] Grace menu: Sometimes, there is a visual glitch when closing the grace menu that may only be visible with low fps.
[*] The Crafting difficulty displayed is not updated correctly when a miracle is active - it is a display issue only, the system takes the miracles correctly into consideration.
[/list]

[h3]PvE / Dungeons[/h3]
[list]
[*] We are aware of the issue regarding some loot piles in dungeons that are too easily accessible. While some of these should now be better guarded, we are looking at making changes to all loot piles in the future so that players wouldn't be able to get the loot without having made the required effort first.
[*] A wall without collision is present in the corridor of The Absterium dungeon.
[*] Inconsistent camera behavior triggered by specific Zebian NPCs' proximity and attack animations.
[*] There are some visibility issues in a submerged shadowed room in The Oubliettes Dungeon.
[*] Casting a Pacify spell on an already aggroed enemy results in the lulled animation even though it is actively attacking.
[/list]

[h3]Crafting[/h3]
[list]
[*] Heartwood can be obtained with blessing without the woodcutting level requirement.
[*] The description of Basic Distilling Tools is incorrect - both the name and the description should be amended.
[*] Leather Brigandine is a solid shape with no holes for the neck and arms.
[*] Three pairs of shoes lack ankle holes when examined.
[*] Leather pants are a solid shape with no holes for the legs.
[/list]

[h3]UX/UI[/h3]
[list]
[*] The [E] key displayed in the Split Stack window is non-functional. Clicking on the button works.
[*] Pressing [E] closes the radial menu [T].
[*] Multiple parts of the inventory UI are misaligned.
[*] There is a one-slot gap in the second line of the buff bar.
[*] Chat UI appears for a brief second upon opening the "Party" or "Notifications" window.
[*] Icons are not representative of all wearable variants.
[*] The receiver of the Party invite also gets "Party invite has been sent" message, which often persists.
[/list]


[h3]Characters[/h3]
[list]
[*] Character Creator: Modifying the base face overrides pupil and iris size changes.
[*] Character Creator: Neutral male body appearance is misrepresented by default.
[*] The button to Randomize a name in Character Creator is always greyed out.
[*] Idling on the lobby and then trying to create a character will show an empty region select screen and kick the user back to the login screen.
[*] 2h Spears clip through the left fist.
[*] The player retains their items after the first death due to fall damage on a newly created character.
[/list]

[h3]Misc.[/h3]
[list]
[*] Having HP and Stamina recover simultaneously may cancel the logout timer.
[*] Summon Party Corpse and Summon Player Corpse do not display an error before casting when there is no corpse or no corpse in range.
[*] Time of day transitions are heavily stepped, with noticeable jumps in lighting when observing shadows.
[*] Humanoid NPC eye movement is visible when in a dead state.
[*] The moon and stars no longer rotate in the night sky.
[*] Double-clicking on a Custom Marker on the map while a Waypoint has been set will move the Waypoint to the Marker.
[*] The Early Access version text is misaligned with the rest of the interface and offsets it vertically. 
[/list]

notes.title: Market Square Part 2 Coming on January 23!
notes.content:
Hello Paxians,

We’re thrilled to announce that Part 2 of the Market Square content update will be deployed on [b]January 23[/b].

[i]Note:[/i] The maintenance will begin at 08 am UTC and is expected to last approximately eight (8) hours to perform some infrastructure changes, so please plan accordingly. Also, [b]no wipe[/b] of the world or characters is planned for this content update.

The second part of Verse 2 will introduce the much-anticipated Grace currency!

[h2]Grace, Blessings, and Miracles[/h2]
Grace represents divine favor and serves as a resource for performing miracles. Think of it as a spiritual energy, enabling you to cast unique, non-combat-related spells.

Miracles will include blessings that enhance crafting and gathering skills or utility abilities like fast travel home - though miracles involving teleportation will be introduced at a later point.

Every character will receive a small amount of Grace by logging in each day. Additional Grace can be obtained by using gold for those seeking more.

[h3]How to earn Grace?[/h3]
[list]
[*] Every player can earn Grace daily the first time any character on the same account and in the same region logs in per day.
[*] You may spend Gold to generate grace, however:
[list]
[*] The price of Grace has scaling diminishing returns each day
[*] The price of Grace resets each day to the base amount
[/list]
[*] Grace is region-based: characters on the same account and in the same region share the same Grace pool.
[/list]
[h3]What kind of blessings and miracles can you cast?[/h3]
In this initial version of the feature, you’ll be able to cast two different kinds of blessings:
[list]
[*] Tradesman’s blessings that buff specific professions’ skills for a limited duration. The buffed skill is used when determining the outcome of crafting tasks. However, the bonus is not used to unlock new recipes or determine XP rewards from crafting - which means that these blessings meaningfully help you earn XP because your success rate is increased. 
[*] Gatherer’s blessings make gathering more time efficient for a limited duration, yielding bonus resource rewards when the respective blessing for each skill is active.
[/list]
More blessings and miracles will be added over time, such as fast travel miracles. Some miracles will be unlocked by default while others will need to be earned through progression.

The full patch notes will be published once the maintenance has started, so you can review all changes in detail.

We can’t wait to hear your feedback on what’s coming!

Pax vobiscum,
The Mainframe Team

notes.title: New Shards
notes.content:
[h2]Hello Paxians,[/h2]

As we mentioned in a previous announcement, we closely monitor the population on all Pax Dei shards. Currently, both Apollo (US) and Mimir (EU) are getting full, making it difficult for newcomers to find free spots to settle and start playing.

As such, we have decided to open two new shards on Friday, January 10, at 10 a.m. UTC.
[list]
[*] US - Sif
[*] EU - Bran
[/list]
To be able to see the newly added shards on Friday, note that you might need to restart the game. 

We will be temporarily opening character transfers from existing shards to the new shards in the same region. Check our FAQs below for more details on how to do this. 

We are also working on additional solutions to better manage populations on the shards, including self-initiated character transfers and implementing an automated system to remove inactive plots sooner than initially planned. While we don’t have any ETA to share on these systems right now, rest assured that our teams are actively working on making them a reality.

Thank you for your patience and understanding.

Pax vobiscum,
The Mainframe Team

[h2]FAQ[/h2]
[h3]Are the new shards RP (Roleplay)?[/h3]
No, the two new shards are standard. They are not flagged as RP.

[h3]Why don’t you open a shard for the SEA region as well?[/h3]
Nuadu’s population levels are stable, and most areas are still low in population, offering enough space for plots to be placed. As such, there is no need to open a new shard for this region at the moment. 

[h3]When I create a character on the new shards, will I get access to my redeeming queue?[/h3]
If you already have a redeeming queue with your other characters and create a new character on a new shard [b]in the same region[/b], you’ll have access to the same redeeming queue.

[h3]Can I transfer an existing character to the new shards?[/h3]
As we do not yet have a self-service character transfer, we will temporarily offer character transfer via our Customer Support team. Note, however:
[list]
[*] You cannot transfer your character if
[list]
[*] You have a placed plot,
[*] You are part of a clan,
[*] You are in a party.
[/list]
Make sure to release your plot, leave your clan and any parties you’re in before contacting our Support Team. 

[*] Only the items that are in your character’s inventory will be transferred to the new shard:
[list]
[*] The gear your character is wearing and the items in their inventory will be carried over.
[*] The skill levels reached by your character will also remain.
[*] [b]BUT[/b]: all the items and material left on a plot you release will not be carried over, will not be added to the redeeming queue, and will be up for grabs publicly as soon as the plot is released. Make sure to add any precious items you’d like to carry over to your character’s inventory so as not to lose them. 
[/list]
[*] If the character name is already taken, your character will need to be renamed. 
[*] You can only transfer to a shard from the same region (US to US, and EU to EU).
[*] We will only offer transfers until January 31st.
[list]
[*] If the population levels of the destination shards reach their limit sooner than the date mentioned above, we will stop offering character transfers to them. 
[/list][/list]
If you wish to have your character transferred to one of the new shards in the same region, please contact our [url=https://support.playpaxdei.com/hc/]Support team directly[/url].

Please note this is a manual process, and some delays may arise when processing your request.

notes.title: Market Square - Patch Notes & Known issues
notes.content:
[h2]Hello Paxians![/h2]
First, here is the content recap for Verse 2, Market Square (with a little teaser about the next update with Grace and Miracles):
[previewyoutube=3yiUpkrGOJM;full][/previewyoutube]
[h2]New Feature: Gold and Markets[/h2]
[h3]Gold[/h3]
[list]
[*] You can now obtain Gold in the game:
[list]
[*] Kill some humanoid NPCs and check what they drop;
[*] Gold operates as an 'ethereal currency' represented only in the UI;
[*] When you receive Gold, the system adds it to a wallet in your inventory;
[*] You can transfer Gold from your wallet to any chest where it will also appear as in a wallet;
[*] Your Gold balance is unaffected by your avatar's death and can't be looted in PvP.
[/list][/list]
[h2]Market Stalls[/h2]
[list]
[*] You can build Market Stalls to sell and buy items for Gold.
[list]
[*]Market Stalls are available with Carpentry level 5.
[*]The recipe will appear in the crafters' list.
[*]Each Market Stall has a maximum capacity of active sell orders. Currently, this limit is at 120 per Market Stall.
[/list]
[*] Permissions - currently only the Market Stall’s owner can change them
[list]
[*]You can set the following permissions to determine who can sell goods at your Market Stall:
[list]
[*]Private,
[*]Clan,
[*]Clan - Elders,
[*]Clan - Alderman.
[/list]
[*]Actions you can't change the permission for:
[list]
[*]Everyone can purchase from any Market Stall,
[*]An order can be canceled by the seller, the Market Stall owner, or the plot owner.
[/list][/list]
[*] Creating a sell order
[list]
[*]Put an item or a stack of items from your inventory on sale and give it a gold price. Each sell order size corresponds to one inventory slot.
[*]Creating a sell order comes at a brokering fee gold charge.
[*]This can only be done if the Market Stall is not at full capacity, the player can afford the broker's fee, and the player has sell permission.
[*]Once created, each sell order shows the item, the stack size, the seller name, and the price. 
[*]Items with less than 100% durability and lifetime can still be sold. The buyer can see the durability state of the item in the details panel.
[/list]
[*] Market Stalls don't yet have detailed filters or sorting options, but you can use the text search to filter items by name or by the seller's name.
[list]
[*]You can also use a quick filter for a single item type by hovering over an item or sell order and pressing the input displayed as “Filter by item. “ This option automatically sets the item's name into the text search filter.
[/list]
[*] Purchasing an item
[list]
[*]Anyone can browse any Market Stall and purchase items from it.
[*]You can only purchase an item when you have available inventory space and carry enough Gold to afford it.
[*]Upon purchase, Gold is immediately transferred to the seller's avatar wallet.
[/list]
[*] Canceling an order
[list]
[*]Orders can only be canceled by the seller, the Market Stall owner, and the plot owner.
[*]You can only cancel an order if you have free inventory space to withdraw it.
[*]Canceling an order withdraws the item from the stall and [b]places it in the inventory of the player who canceled it.[/b] As with the permissions on your plot(s), you must trust the people you work with!
[*]When an order is canceled, the fee spent upon creation is lost.
[/list]
[*] Market Stall Notifications
[list]
[*] When your sell order is filled out, you receive the gold immediately in your wallet.
[*] The initial release of the Market Stalls doesn't give you a visual notification when you sell a good. Your gold wallet updates as gold is transferred to it. We're still working on clear notifications for this and a Market Log where you review your active orders and trade activity.
[/list]
[*] Destroying a Market Stall
[list]
[*]Market Stall can only be destroyed if it has no active sell orders. The plot owner, the market stall owner, or the sell order owner(s) must cancel any active orders to be able to destroy a market stall.
[/list]
[*] If a plot with a Marker Stall is released:
[list]
[*] As there is no plot owner anymore, only the Market Stall owner and the owners of the different sell orders can cancel the orders.
[*] If someone now places a plot on top of the Market Stall, they become the plot’s owner and obtain rights on the Market Stall. This means they can empty it by canceling all orders and getting all the goods. Again, be careful with who you work with on the Market Stalls.
[/list][/list]

[h2]Changes & Fixes[/h2]
[h3]Gameplay[/h3]
[list]
[*] A lot of stack sizes have been increased. 
[*] The system for selecting interactable items—loots, gatherables, and props—is now more reliable when the items are stacked on each other.
[*] The interaction range has also been slightly increased.
[*] The Unstuck ability can no longer be used during combat and now requires full stamina to activate.
[*] Mining and tree-chopping animations have been enhanced.
[*] Clan names will now consistently appear below player names in character nameplates.
[/list]

[h2]Combat Balance and fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Projectiles can now penetrate water surfaces.
[*] Reduced forward movement of all melee attacks by 10%.
[*] The stamina cost of blocking in PvE combat has been reduced.
[*] Base stamina regeneration is paused during blocking, but food and potion regeneration will continue.
[*] The melee targeting has been improved to prioritize enemies close by.
[*] The melee Aim Assist slider has been removed from the game.
[*] The damage of all sword types has been increased.
[*] Combat skills for one-handed and two-handed spears have been divided into Handspears and Polearms  categories.
[*] Fixed an issue where One Handed Spears incorrectly used Polearm damage on the final combo-chain attack.
[*] The area of effect range of the two-handed mace special attack has been reduced.
[*] Balanced the damage output of maces and spears to better align with their utility.
[*] The axe special attack now reduces target physical resistances by 20% (used to be flat value).
[*] The Hurt Proc effect has been adjusted to reduce stun duration, application chance, and flat damage.
[*] Spell Casting now correctly displays the spell icon and text on NPCs' nameplates.
[*] Fixed an issue where attempting to cast a spell on cooldown would prevent subsequent casts in the same slot.
[*] Enemies stuck attempting to path to their target will now teleport to a valid spot near their target. This is a temporary workaround to a dungeon exploit where the enemy movement is blocked so they cannot reach their target.
[*] NPCs will now verify their teleport destination to prevent unintended teleportation.
[*] Fixed issues related to NPC disappearance, aggro, and pathfinding.
[*] Fixed over-prediction of attacks against enemies moving near the player where some hits would be considered being done from behind, ignoring the blocking mitigation.
[*] Fixed an exploit where it was possible to drop an item during combat and “hide” behind it to prevent receiving damages.
[/list]

[h2]Audio[/h2]
[list]
[*] Improved Inquisitor grunts and sounds when fighting in groups.
[*] Fixed the frequency of noises enemies make while idling.
[/list]

[h2]Discord[/h2]
[list]
[*] Added several clan and party events to broadcast to the chat, e.g., new members joining, members leaving, or being kicked out…
[*] Added a settings menu to the general chat that allows players to filter what chat lobbies they see.
[*] Removed the Discord account name displayed in the chat under the player character’s name. The Discord account name information is still available in the interaction menu when clicking on a player's chat entry.
[*] Updated the Discord button textures and text so they should not appear pixelated or blurry at different UI scales.
[*] Fixed several issues with the Direct Message button usability. 
[*] Fixed an issue in which the friend requests, clan invites, and party invites were also displayed to the requester.
[*] Fixed an issue where the nearby chat lobby might not appear in the general chat lobby selector.
[*] Fixed an issue where you couldn't DM a player from the chat interaction menu after sending them a friend request.
[*] Fixed an issue where texts with a line break pasted into the chat would automatically be sent.
[*] Fixed an issue where successfully linking your account to Discord from the chat settings or friend list wouldn't trigger a pop-up.
[/list]

[h2]World[/h2]
[list]
[*] Increased the size of the Skullcap resource for better visibility.
[*] Added a missing icon for Green Apples.
[*] Updated assets and icons for reeds and grain resources.
[*] Updated the model and icon for Green Grapes.
[*] Fixed an issue preventing the placement of blast furnaces on foundations and other flat structures.
[*] Corrected the 3D model of wrought iron bars when dropped on the ground.
[*] Addressed floating and clipping issues with decorative props in enemy camps.
[*] Fixed the smoke effect emitted by Alchemy Tables.
[*] Fixed lighting anomalies when entering and exiting water volumes in pre-dungeon catacombs.
[*] Squared away some extra sound effects used to play when interacting with the map.
[*] Improved the visual appearance of the Petra Dei.
[/list]

[h2]Character Art[/h2]
[list]
[*] Beards and mustaches can now be selected independently during the character creation.
[*] Subtle adjustments have been made to avatar faces.
[*] Additional body shape options and normal mapping have been implemented.
[*] Optimized several NPCs for better performance.
[*] Adjusted some shaders to improve metal brightness.
[*] Reduced excessive shininess on leather chest armor pieces.
[*] Improved cape clipping behavior.
[*] Ensured the "always cover body" feature persists in the characters' lobby.
[*] Optimized texture scaling by removing dynamic bounding boxes for detail textures.
[*] Fixed an issue causing head transparency when wearing specific clothing.
[*] Corrected display issues with specific earring models.
[/list]

[h2]Resources[/h2]
[list]
[*] Some resources and animals' spawn points have been updated.
[*] Increased Tree Branch and Gneiss Stone density in starter areas. 
[*] Increased spawns for Level 14 boars, Level 24 bears, grapes, red onion, reeds, and pure iron deposits in the Wildlands.
[*] Adjusted Meadowsweet to spawn more along the water in the grasslands and all non-tree biomes in the Home Valleys. Also added it to the wetlands biome in the Wildlands.
[*] Ensured all quarries in the world have mineable spawning.
[/list]

[h2]Crafting[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue that caused the skinning skill to not always receive XP from looting animal corpses.
[*] Adjusted recipes for starter professions to align with the stack amounts for the ingredients.
[*] Fixed an issue that caused the map to no longer focus on the player's location in some cases.
[*] Fixed an issue where holding shift and double-clicking G would move all items from one inventory to another.
[*] Fixed an issue with inventory where the button prompts stack vertically.
[*] Updated recipe names for smithy signs to be more descriptive.
[*] Fixed an issue where items sometimes drop to the ground when moving them from the inventory slot to the hotbar.
[*] Fixed an issue that could sometimes cause Craft All to stop functioning.
[/list]

[h2]Localization[/h2]
[list]
[*] The game is now localized in French and German. Open the Setting, General, and pick your language in the drop-down menu. You won’t need to restart the game.
[*] You can post feedback on our Discord channels dedicated to French and German localization.
[/list]

[h2]Known Issues[/h2]
[h3]Markets[/h3]
[list]
[*] Creating or purchasing a sell order can sometimes trigger a random error message despite being successful.
[*] Market Stall settings window is missing the confirmation and reset buttons.
[*] The right panel is not refreshed after an item is purchased, which leaves a non-functional ghost item displayed.
[*] The original slot remains selected when moving an item from one inventory slot to another.
[*] The settings button in the Market Stall UI is missing a corresponding key bind.
[*] A sell order and an inventory item can both be selected at once.
[*] If the player does not have enough gold and purchases an order using the keyboard key, an error pop-up appears with missing strings.
[*] Primary action button prompts are missing for all modal windows related to interacting with sell orders.
[*] The "Market at Full capacity!" window lacks the visuals [X] and ESC close window options.
[*] Text in the "Market at Full capacity!" modal is grammatically incorrect.
